summary: Author, 加里·奥多诺霍（Gary O'Donoghue） Author, 布兰登·德雷农（Brandon Drenon） 民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）赢得德克萨斯州（Texas；得州）关键的参议员选举，被视为今次美国中期选举的最大爆冷之一。 他击败共和党对手肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton），是1988年以来首次有民主党人在德州赢得联邦参议员席位。这场胜利不仅改写德州数十年来的政治版图，也进一步巩固民主党对美国国会的控制。 塔拉里科是教师
content:
Author, 加里·奥多诺霍（Gary O'Donoghue）
Author, 布兰登·德雷农（Brandon Drenon）
民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）赢得德克萨斯州（Texas；得州）关键的参议员选举，被视为今次美国中期选举的最大爆冷之一。
他击败共和党对手肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton），是1988年以来首次有民主党人在德州赢得联邦参议员席位。这场胜利不仅改写德州数十年来的政治版图，也进一步巩固民主党对美国国会的控制。
塔拉里科是教师出身，直到去年之前都鲜为人知。他将共和党执政下生活成本上升作为竞选主轴，争取选民支持。
共和党的帕克斯顿则曾多次与特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）同台造势，并将塔拉里科描绘成对德州而言过于进步的候选人。
此文包含Instagram提供的内容。由于这些内容会使用曲奇或小甜饼等科技，我们在加载任何内容前会寻求您的认可。 您可能在给与许可前愿意阅读Instagram小甜饼政策和隐私政策。 希望阅读上述内容，请点击“接受并继续”。
在德州首府奥斯汀的一场观票派对上，当电视宣布塔拉里科胜选时，他的支持者陷入狂欢。
他们拥抱、亲吻、举杯庆祝。许多人说，自己不敢相信这会实现。
塔拉里科在附近一间表演艺术中心的正式观票派对上登台，现场掌声雷动。他宣布：“我们刚刚夺回了德州。”
“我们证明了，再多的金钱也比不上德州人民的力量。”
这是指他击败了共和党对手帕克斯顿，而帕克斯顿的竞选活动获全球首富马斯克（Elon Musk）的支持。
他竞选期间常用宗教语言，把自己的胜算渺茫，比作《圣经》中“大卫战胜歌利亚”的故事。
他说：“这场胜利，是献给每一位曾经怀疑是否有人在聆听的德州人。我听见你们了，我们听见你们了。今晚，全世界都听见你们了。”
Play video, "為何美國中期選舉對特朗普至關重要？", 节目全长 8,18
数十年来，对德州的自由派来说，民主党人赢得全州性选举，一直像是白日梦。
德州是美国人口第二多的州，一直是保守主义的堡垒，经常推行日后被其他地方效法的共和党政策。
但在整个竞选期间，民调显示身为州议员的塔拉里科，逐渐突破传统政治版图，激励了急切渴望新领导层的德州民主党基本盘。
选战开支也随之大幅飙升，很快成为美国联邦参议员选举史上最昂贵的一场，花费超过5亿美元（36亿元人民币；150亿元新台币）。
马斯克向支持共和党帕克斯顿的超级政治行动委员会（Super PAC），注资1.58亿美元，而这也成为塔拉里科攻击对手的重要素材。
更令人意外的是，以德州作为政治根据地的共和党政治世家布什家族（Bush family；布希／布殊），竟有两名成员公开支持塔拉里科，此举被视为帕克斯顿败选的预兆。
乔治华盛顿大学（George Washington University）政治学教授夸德里科斯·德里斯克尔（Prof Quardricos Driskell）向BBC表示，帕克斯顿是共和党失败的主要原因之一，称他是“客观而言糟糕的候选人”。
他说，塔拉里科在德州的胜利，加上周二（11月3日）另一场爆冷，击败了该州共和党籍州长阿博特（Greg Abbott），“绝对是历史性的”。阿博特落败，也意味着民主党自1990年代以来首次赢得德州州长选举。
德里斯克尔教授谈到民主党在这个“孤星之州”的收获时说：“这不只是海啸，不只是公投，而是一场血洗。⋯⋯这明确显示，这个国家想走向不同的方向。”
塔拉里科在民主党初选中，击败了知名对手、达拉斯国会议员贾丝敏·克罗基特（Jasmine Crockett）。
此后，尽管面对大量负面广告攻击，包括针对他过去支持跨性别者权益的言论，他的支持度仍维持稳定。
竞选期间，他经常谈及自己的宗教背景。他的祖父是一名南方浸信会（Southern Baptist）牧师，而他本人也曾在神学院学习，因此演说中经常引用《圣经》典故。
Play video, "The expensive battle to turn Texas blue", 节目全长 0,31
2023年，他被自己所属政党以贪腐指控弹劾，后来获该州参议院宣判无罪。他也曾遭美国证券交易委员会（SEC）以联邦诈欺罪名起诉，但案件后来被撤控。
特朗普则多次赴德州，替帕克斯顿及其他共和党候选人站台，甚至前往原本稳定支持共和党的地区举办造势活动，显示共和党高层对投票率感到忧心。
选民对高昂的物价感到不满，包括汽油价格，并将原因归咎于特朗普的关税政策及对伊朗战争。
此外，美墨边境地区及拉丁裔选民亦对特朗普移民政策感到不满。
尽管特朗普执政下非法越境人数大幅下降，而这一直是德州选民重视的议题，但民调显示，特朗普在拉丁裔选民中的支持度明显流失。
拉丁裔约占德州总人口三分之一。自夏末以来的多项调查显示，多数德州拉丁裔选民如今不认同特朗普的施政，而许多人曾在2024年大选中转而支持他。
多位在选前接受BBC访问的德州拉丁裔选民表示，促使他们改变立场的重要原因之一，是特朗普强力打击移民的政策。
他们提到，部分执法措施导致美国公民遭拘留，非暴力犯罪者也被大规模逮捕，让许多人感到不安。

content:
美国中期选举2026：民主党历史性胜利 深入共和党票仓攻城掠地——BBC记者泽克尔观察 - BBC News 中文
Author, 安东尼·泽克尔（Anthony Zurcher）
民主党改写了唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）的政治版图，而这个夜晚所带来的冲击波，未来多年都将震撼美国政坛。
随着民主党在一连串数十年来稳定支持共和党的州份赢得重要参议院胜利，其中堪萨斯州更是近一个世纪以来首次出现这种情况，一股蓝色巨浪席卷全国，将共和党逐出权力中心。
在特朗普总统第二个任期过半之际，民主党如今已牢牢掌控众议院，并重新夺回参议院多数席位。
他们将有能力阻挠特朗普的施政议程，并对其政府展开调查。史无前例的第三次弹劾尝试也可能被提上日程。
在特朗普于2025年1月重返白宫，并在共和党全面掌控国会的情况下执政后，几乎没有人能想像会出现这样的结果。
随着公众舆论转而反对他及其政党，民主党曾寄望重新夺回众议院。
但面对一张看来对自己不利的参议院选举版图，他们原本认为前景艰难，因为其中许多州在两年前都由特朗普轻松拿下。
然而，民主党最终凭藉在德克萨斯州（Texas；得州）、缅因州、堪萨斯州、俄亥俄州、艾奥瓦州（Iowa；爱荷华／衣阿华）以及北卡罗来纳州和南卡罗来纳州的胜利，改写了政治算式。
Play video, "為何美國中期選舉對特朗普至關重要？", 节目全长 8,18
在接受BBC美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）访问时，特朗普承诺将与国会民主党人达成协议，并表示自己不希望在任期最后两年都花时间否决他们提出的法案。
不过，他稍后在“真相社交”（TRUTH Social）上发布了一张自己标志性的红色棒球帽照片，上面印有“veto”（否决）字样，某程度上削弱了这番表态。
总统接着指出，今年的选票上没有他的名字，但如果有的话，共和党将取得压倒性胜利。
然而，特朗普曾帮助许多共和党候选人提升声势，并敦促选民将这次选举视为他争取连任。
在参议院方面，民主党至少翻转六个席位，轻松取得多数地位。
亚当·汉密尔顿（Adam Hamilton）在堪萨斯州胜出。该州上一次选出民主党参议员还是在近100年前的大萧条时期。
詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）在德州参议院选举中击败共和党人肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton），终结民主党在该州全州级选举38年的连败纪录。

在南卡罗来纳州，安妮·安德鲁斯（Annie Andrews）击败达琳·格雷厄姆（Darline Graham），后者是在其兄长、参议员林赛·格雷厄姆（Lindsey Graham）去世后获任命接替该席位。即使在几个月前，也鲜有分析人士认为这个席位具有竞争性。
五度当选的共和党参议员苏珊·柯林斯（Susan Collins）承认在缅因州参议院选举中败给民主党人特洛伊·杰克逊（Troy Jackson）。
残奥运动员乔什·图雷克（Josh Turek）夺下由即将退休的共和党参议员乔妮·恩斯特（Joni Ernst）持有的艾奥瓦州参议院席位。民主党也重新夺回俄亥俄州的参议院席位，由谢罗德·布朗（Sherrod Brown）在复出之战中击败乔恩·赫斯特德（Jon Husted）。
与此同时，在密歇根州一场激烈角逐的参议院选举中，民主党人阿卜杜勒·埃尔—赛义德（Abdul El-Sayed）击败共和党人迈克·罗杰斯（Mike Rogers）。
民主党挑战者吉娜·伊诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）击败现任共和党州长格雷格·阿博特（Greg Abbott）。就在今年稍早，后者仍被视为稳操胜券。
民主党同时赢得艾奥瓦州、俄亥俄州及佐治亚州的州长选举。佐治亚州更创下历史，选出首位黑人女性州长。
与此同时，民主党自2022年以来首次赢得众议院多数席位。
预计民主党将赢得245个众议院席位，共和党则为166席。

民主党翻转了德州、北卡罗来纳州、宾夕法尼亚州、艾奥瓦州、肯塔基州及科罗拉多州等地的众议院席位，并准备在弗吉尼亚州及印第安纳州扩大战果。
南方各州的黑人民主党选民以破纪录人数投票，协助该党取得胜利。而曾帮助特朗普在2024年赢得总统大选的拉丁裔选民，也明显转向支持民主党。
民主党赢得了德州与墨西哥边境沿线三个以拉丁裔人口为主的国会选区全部众议院席位。
在佛罗里达州，拉丁裔选民也帮助民主党守住众议院席位，挫败州内共和党透过重划选区夺取席位的计划。
事实上，去年数月以来主导新闻头条的国会选区重划之争，最终对共和党而言并未带来成果。
在德州，他们原本希望透过重新划线为本党增加五个席位，但到星期二（11月3日），他们最终甚至可能失去一席。
如果说保守派还有一线希望，那就是整体而言佛罗里达州似乎仍偏向右翼。
共和党参议员阿什莉·穆迪（Ashley Moody）以些微优势成功连任，众议员拜伦·唐纳兹（Byron Donalds）也当选这个“阳光之州”首位黑人州长。
而陷入困境的共和党人也成功保住佛蒙特州及新罕布什尔州州长职位。但这样的亮点寥寥可数。
随后，他便以此姿态施政，推动在贸易及移民议题上的部分不受欢迎政策，并发动一场遭多数美国民众反对的对伊朗战争。
星期二，选民向他作出了沉重斥责，而这种教训将不会轻易被遗忘。

Department of Commerce National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Commerce.
Notice; nominations for shark stock assessment advisory panel.
NMFS solicits nominations for the Atlantic Highly Migratory ( printed page 69550) Species (HMS) SouthEast Data, Assessment, and Review (SEDAR) Workshops Advisory Panel, also known as the “SEDAR Pool.” The SEDAR Pool is comprised of a group of individuals who, if selected, review data and advise NMFS on the scientific information, data, and models used in stock assessments for oceanic sharks in the Atlantic Ocean, including the Gulf of America and Caribbean Sea. NMFS is seeking nominations for a 5-year term beginning in 2027. NMFS will consider individuals with definable interests in recreational and commercial fishing and related industries, including those from the environmental community, academia, and non-governmental organizations, for membership on the SEDAR Pool.
Submit nominations on or before December 4, 2026.
You may submit nominations and request the SEDAR Pool Statement of Organization, Practices, and Procedures electronically via email to SEDAR.pool@noaa.gov.
Additional information on SEDAR and the SEDAR guidelines can be found at http://sedarweb.org/​. The terms of reference for the SEDAR Pool, along with a list of current members, can be found at https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/​atlantic-highly-migratory-species/​southeast-data-assessment-and-review-and-atlantic-highly.
Karyl Brewster-Geisz or Delisse Ortiz at 301-427-8503.
HMS fisheries (swordfish, sharks, tunas, and billfish) are managed under the 2006 Consolidated HMS Fishery Management Plan (FMP) and its amendments pursuant to the authority of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act; 16 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.) and consistent with the Atlantic Tunas Convention Act (16 U.S.C. 971 et seq.). HMS implementing regulations are at 50 CFR part 635.
NMFS established the SEDAR Pool consistent with section 302(g) of the Magnuson-Stevens Act. NMFS may select individuals of the SEDAR Pool to review and advise NMFS on the scientific information, data, and models used in stock assessments for oceanic sharks in the Atlantic Ocean, including the Gulf of America and Caribbean Sea. While NMFS created the SEDAR Pool specifically for consultation on Atlantic shark stock assessments, NMFS may expand consultation to other HMS, as needed.
NMFS may select individuals in the SEDAR Pool to participate in the various data and assessment workshops during the stock assessment process. The primary responsibility of selected individuals is to review and provide advice regarding the scientific information, data, and models that NMFS will use or consider for use in the relevant stock assessment. To ensure that the peer review is unbiased, individuals who participated in a data and/or assessment workshop for a particular stock assessment cannot serve as a peer reviewer for the same stock assessment. However, these individuals may be asked to attend the review workshop to answer specific questions from the reviewers concerning the data and/or assessment workshops. Members of the SEDAR Pool may serve as members of other advisory panels or committees established under section 302(g) concurrent with, or following, their service on the SEDAR Pool.
The SEDAR Pool is comprised of individuals that represent the commercial and recreational fishing communities for Atlantic sharks, the environmental community active in the conservation and management of Atlantic sharks, and the academic community that have relevant expertise with sharks and/or stock assessment methodologies for marine fish species. Additionally, individuals who may not necessarily work directly with sharks, but who are involved in fisheries with similar life history, biology, and fishery issues may be part of the SEDAR Pool. Members of the SEDAR Pool must have demonstrated experience in the fisheries, related industries, research, teaching, writing, conservation, or management of marine organisms. The distribution of representation among the interested parties is not defined or limited.
Additional members of the SEDAR Pool may also include representatives from the 5 Atlantic Regional Fishery Management Councils, the 18 Atlantic states, the U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico, and the relevant interstate commissions (Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission and Gulf States Marine Fisheries Commission).
If NMFS requires additional members to ensure a diverse pool of individuals for data or assessment workshops, NMFS may request individuals to become members of the SEDAR Pool outside of the annual nomination period.
SEDAR Pool members serve at the discretion of the Secretary. Not all members will attend each SEDAR workshop. Rather, NMFS will invite certain members to participate at specific stock assessment workshops dependent on their ability to participate, discuss, and offer scientific input and advice regarding the species being assessed.
NMFS is not obligated to fulfill any requests ( e.g., requests for an assessment of a certain species) that may be made by the SEDAR Pool or its individual members. Members of the SEDAR Pool who are invited to attend stock assessment workshops will not be compensated for their services, but may be reimbursed for their travel-related expenses to attend such workshops.
B. Nomination Procedures for Appointments to the SEDAR Pool
Member tenure is 5 years. Nominations are sought for terms beginning early in 2027 and expiring at the end of 2031. Nomination packages should include:
1. The name, address, phone number, and email of the applicant or nominee;
2. A description of the applicant's or nominee's interest in Atlantic shark stock assessments or the Atlantic shark fishery;
3. A statement of the applicant's or nominee's background and/or qualifications; and
4. A written commitment that the applicant or nominee shall participate actively and in good faith in the tasks of the SEDAR Pool, as requested.
Individual members of the SEDAR Pool meet to participate in stock assessments at the discretion of the Office of Sustainable Fisheries, NMFS. Stock assessment timing, frequency, and relevant species will vary depending on the needs determined by NMFS and SEDAR staff. In 2027, NMFS plans to finalize the sandbar shark stock assessment and begin the bull shark stock assessment. All meetings are open for observation by the public.
Director, Office of Sustainable Fisheries, National Marine Fisheries Service.

Department of Commerce International Trade Administration
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that certain oil country tubular goods (OCTG) from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are being, or are likely to be, sold in the United States at less than fair value (LTFV). The period of investigation (POI) is April 1, 2025, through March 31, 2026. Interested parties are invited to comment on this preliminary determination.
Applicable November 4, 2026.
Alexander Rodriguez or Dylan Hill, AD/CVD Operations, Office IV, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-0190 or (202) 482-1197, respectively.
This preliminary determination is made in accordance with section 733(b) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act). Commerce published the notice of initiation of this investigation on April 28, 2026.[1] On August 28, 2026, Commerce postponed the preliminary determination of this investigation and the revised deadline is now October 29, 2026.[2]
For a complete description of the events that followed the initiation of this investigation, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.[3] A list of topics included in the Preliminary Decision Memorandum is included as Appendix II to this notice. The Preliminary Decision Memorandum is a public document and is on file electronically via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS), which is available to registered users at https://access.trade.gov. In addition, a complete version of the Preliminary Decision Memorandum can be accessed directly at https://access.trade.gov/​frnotices.
The product covered by this investigation is OCTG from the UAE. For a complete description of the scope of this investigation, see Appendix I.
In accordance with the Preamble to Commerce's regulations,[4] the Initiation Notice set aside a period of time for parties to raise issues regarding product coverage ( i.e., scope).[5] Certain interested parties commented on the scope of the investigation as it appeared in the Initiation Notice, whereby they requested that Commerce find certain mechanical pipe products to be outside the scope of this investigation. These products include: mechanical pipe for oilfield tools, mechanical pipe for perforating guns, and expandable mechanical pipe.
We note that there is an ongoing scope inquiry related to the antidumping duty orders on OCTG from Argentina and Mexico with respect to these same mechanical pipe products.[6] In that inquiry, Commerce preliminarily found that the products were outside the scope of the orders,[7] based on comments identical to the scope comments received in this investigation. Consistent with that finding, Commerce preliminarily finds and clarifies that mechanical pipe for oilfield tools, mechanical pipe for perforating guns, and expandable mechanical pipe are outside the scope of this investigation. Because this is a clarification, Commerce is not preliminarily modifying the scope language as it appeared in the Initiation Notice. See the scope in Appendix I to this notice.
The final determination in the above-referenced scope inquiry is currently scheduled to be made no later than December 22, 2026.[8] We intend to consider that final determination when making a final scope ruling in this investigation. Case briefs or other written comments regarding the scope of this investigation may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance no later than 30 after the preliminary determination of this investigation. Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs regarding the scope of this investigation, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing of the scope-related case briefs.[9] Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.310(c), interested parties who wish to request a hearing regarding the scope of this investigation, limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal, may do so in accordance with the instructions detailed below within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice.
Commerce is conducting this investigation in accordance with section 731 of the Act. Commerce has calculated export prices in accordance with section 772(a) of the Act. Constructed export prices have been calculated in accordance with section 772(b) of the Act. Normal value is calculated in accordance with section 773 of the Act. For a full description of the methodology underlying the preliminary determination, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
Sections 733(d)(1)(ii) and 735(c)(5)(A) of the Act provide that in the preliminary determination Commerce shall determine an estimated all-others rate for all exporters and producers not individually examined. This rate shall be an amount equal to the weighted average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins established for exporters and producers individually investigated, excluding any zero and de minimis margins, and any margins determined entirely under section 776 of the Act.
In this investigation, Commerce calculated estimated weighted-average dumping margins for Universal Tube ( printed page 69540) Industries FZE and Ajmal Steel Tubes and Pipes Industries, LLC. (collectively, the examined respondents) that are not zero, de minimis, or based entirely on facts otherwise available. Commerce calculated the all-others rate using a weighted average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents using each company's publicly-ranged values for the merchandise under consideration.[10]
Commerce preliminarily determines that the following estimated weighted-average dumping margins exist:
Exporter/producer Weighted-average dumping margin (percent) Ajmal Steel Tubes and Pipes Industries, LLC 68.88 Universal Tube and Pipe Industries FZE; THL Pipe and Tube Industries LLC 11 61.45 All Others 68.23
In accordance with section 733(d)(2) of the Act, Commerce will direct U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to suspend liquidation of entries of subject merchandise, as described in Appendix I, entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register . Further, pursuant to section 733(d)(1)(B) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.205(d), Commerce will instruct CBP to require a cash deposit equal to the estimated weighted-average dumping margin or the estimated all-others rate, as follows: (1) The cash deposit rate for the companies listed above will be equal to the company-specific estimated weighted-average dumping margins determined in this preliminary determination; (2) if the exporter is not a respondent identified above, but the producer is, then the cash deposit rate will be equal to the company-specific estimated weighted-average dumping margin established for that producer of the subject merchandise; and (3) the cash deposit rate for all other producers and exporters will be equal to the all-others estimated weighted-average dumping margin.
These suspension of liquidation and cash deposit instructions will remain in effect until further notice.
Commerce intends to disclose its calculations and analysis performed to interested parties in this preliminary determination within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the date of publication of this notice in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b).
Consistent with 19 CFR 351.224(e), Commerce will analyze and, if appropriate, correct any timely allegations of significant ministerial errors by amending the preliminary determination. However, consistent with 19 CFR 351.224(d), Commerce will not consider incomplete allegations that do not address the significance standard under 19 CFR 351.224(g) following the preliminary determination. Instead, Commerce will address such allegations in the final determination together with issues raised in the case briefs or other written comments.
As provided in section 782(i)(1) of the Act, Commerce intends to verify the information relied upon in making its final determination.
Case briefs or other written comments, unrelated to scope, may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance no later than seven days after the date on which the last verification report is issued in this investigation. A timeline for the submission of case briefs and written comments will be notified to interested parties at a later date. Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing case briefs.[12] Interested parties who submit case briefs or rebuttal briefs in this proceeding must submit: (1) a table of contents listing each issue; and (2) a table of authorities.[13]
As provided under 19 CFR 351.309(c)(2)(iii) and (d)(2)(iii), we request that interested parties provide at the beginning of their briefs a public, executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs.[14] Further, we request that interested parties limit their executive summary of each issue to no more than 450 words, not including citations. We intend to use the executive summaries as the basis of the comment summaries included in the issues and decision memorandum that will accompany the final determination in this investigation. We request that interested parties include footnotes for relevant citations in the executive summary of each issue. Note that Commerce has amended certain of its requirements pertaining to the service of documents in 19 CFR 351.303(f).[15]
Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.310(c), interested parties who wish to request a hearing, limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal briefs, must submit a written request to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance, U.S. Department of Commerce, within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice. Requests should contain: (1) the party's name, address, and telephone number; (2) the number of participants, and whether any participant is a foreign national; and (3) a list of the issues to be discussed. If a request for a hearing is made, Commerce intends to hold the hearing ( printed page 69541) at a time and date to be determined. Parties should confirm by telephone the date, time, and location of the hearing two days before the scheduled date.
Section 735(a)(1) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.210(b)(1) provide that Commerce will issue the final determination within 75 days after the signature date of its preliminary determination. Accordingly, Commerce will make its final determination no later than 75 days after the signature date of this preliminary determination.
U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) Notification
In accordance with section 733(f) of the Act, Commerce will notify the ITC of its preliminary determination. If the final determination is affirmative, the ITC will determine before the later of 120 days after the date of this preliminary determination or 45 days after the final determination whether these imports are materially injuring, or threaten material injury to, the U.S. industry.
This determination is issued and published in accordance with sections 733(f) and 777(i)(1) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.205(c).
Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.
The merchandise covered by the investigation is certain oil country tubular goods (OCTG), which are hollow steel products of circular cross-section, including oil well casing and tubing, of iron (other than cast iron) or steel (both carbon and alloy), whether seamless or welded, regardless of end finish ( e.g., whether or not plain end, threaded, or threaded and coupled) whether or not conforming to American Petroleum Institute (API) or non-API specifications, whether finished (including limited service OCTG products) or unfinished (including green tubes and limited service OCTG products), whether or not thread protectors are attached. The scope of the investigation also covers OCTG coupling stock.
Subject merchandise includes material matching the above description that has been finished, packaged, or otherwise processed in a third country, including by performing any heat treatment, cutting, upsetting, threading, coupling, or any other finishing, packaging, or processing that would not otherwise remove the merchandise from the scope of the investigation if performed in the country of manufacture of the OCTG.
Excluded from the scope of the investigation are: casing, tubing, or coupling stock containing 10.5 percent or more by weight of chromium; drill pipe; unattached couplings; and unattached thread protectors.

With two respondents under examination, Commerce normally calculates: (A) a weighted-average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents; (B) a simple average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents; and (C) a weighted-average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents using each company's publicly-ranged U.S. sales values for the merchandise under consideration. Commerce then compares (B) and (C) to (A) and selects the rate closest to (A) as the most appropriate rate for all other producers and exporters. Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice (DOJ), will be submitting the following information collection request to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. The proposed information collection was previously published in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026, 91 FR 56212, allowing a 60-day comment period.
Comments are encouraged and will be accepted for 30 days until December 4, 2026.
If you have comments especially on the estimated public burden or associated response time, suggestions, or need a copy of the proposed information collection instrument with instructions or additional information, please contact: Counter-UAS Operations Unit, Unmanned Aviation Section, Critical Incident Response Group, Federal Bureau of Investigation, email: cuas@fbi.gov.
Written comments and suggestions from the public and affected agencies concerning the proposed collection of information are encouraged. Your comments should address one or more of the following four points:
—Evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
—Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
—Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and/or
—Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology, e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses.
Written comments and recommendations for this information collection should be submitted within 30 days of the publication of this notice on the following website www.reginfo.gov/​public/​do/​PRAMain. Find this particular information collection by selecting “Currently under 30-day Review—Open for Public Comments” or by using the search function and entering either the title of the information collection or the OMB Control Number 1110-0090. This information collection request may be viewed at www.reginfo.gov. Follow the instructions to view Department of Justice, information collections currently under review by OMB. If you do submit a comment, please send a copy to cuas@fbi.gov.
DOJ seeks PRA authorization for this information collection for three (3) years. OMB authorization for an ICR cannot be for more than three (3) years without renewal. The DOJ notes that information collection requirements submitted to the OMB for existing ICRs receive a month-to-month extension while they undergo review.
Abstract: The SAFER SKIES Act, Title LXXXVI of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, as implemented by the interim final rule codified at 6 CFR part 124 and 28 CFR part 124, extends counter-UAS detection and mitigation authority to State, local, tribal, and territorial (SLTT) law enforcement and correctional agencies under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2). This collection covers the coordination, authorization, reporting, and recordkeeping submissions the rule requires, made through the designated Federal C-UAS coordination portal. The current approval was granted on an emergency basis and expires November 30, 2026. This revision requests a standard three-year approval, reflects revisions to five instruments (C-UAS-AN, C-UAS-OPLAN, C-UAS-TTE, C-UAS-ATT, and C-UAS-POR) made during initial implementation, and re-estimates burden for every instrument. The FBI received one public comment in response to the 60-day notice, from an independent researcher. The commenter supported the collection and raised questions about the cost burden, the basis for the recordkeeping and plan estimates, the treatment of filed forms under the retention provisions of 6 CFR and 28 CFR 124.14, access to the instruments, and opportunities to reduce burden through data reuse and machine-readable filing. In response, the FBI has added a one-time form training line to the burden table, split the recordkeeping estimate by agency tier and raised the mitigation-tier figure, documented the task-level basis for each estimate in the supporting statement, explained the basis for the cost estimate, provided the instruments to the commenter, and committed to adding a State-law citation field to the Extended Retention Notification, publishing the data schema for each instrument, extending data reuse to the Post-Operation Report and Semiannual Summary, and offering a one-step no-activity summary for detection-tier agencies. The comment and the FBI's response are summarized in the supporting statement. The FBI is transitioning the instruments from the current offline, emailed workflow to a secure web portal that will host the same instruments with the same data elements, authenticate users through existing federated identity providers, and capture completion timing for future burden estimates; go-live is expected in the second or third quarter of fiscal year 2027. Following publication of the 60-day notice, the FBI also made minor clarifying edits to the instruments; those edits did not add or remove data elements.
1. Type of Information Collection: Revision of a previously approved collection.
2. Title of the Form/Collection: SAFER SKIES State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Counter-UAS Information Collection.
3. Agency form number, if any, and the applicable component of the Department of Justice sponsoring the collection: Form numbers: C-UAS-ATT; C-UAS-OPLAN; C-UAS-AN; C-UAS-MAA; C-UAS-NOI; C-UAS-LAD; C-UAS-OAN; C-UAS-POR; C-UAS-ERN; C-UAS-SUM; C-UAS-VSR; C-UAS-ASLN; C-UAS-ARR; C-UAS-TTE. The sponsoring component is the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice.
4. Affected public who will be asked or required to respond, as well as a brief abstract: Affected Public: State, Local, or Tribal Government (State, local, ( printed page 69577) tribal, and territorial law enforcement and correctional agencies).
Abstract: Respondents submit the attestations, plans, notifications, reports, and records required by 6 CFR and 28 CFR part 124 to coordinate, authorize, and oversee SLTT counter-UAS operations.].
5. Obligation to Respond: Required to obtain or retain a benefit for most instruments (the accreditation and certification needed to exercise counter-UAS authority under 6 U.S.C. 124n(a)(2) and 6 CFR and 28 CFR part 124); certain reports and notifications are mandatory under the same authorities; a small number of instruments are voluntary.
6. Total Estimated Number of Respondents: 1,850 SLTT agencies.
7. Estimated Time per Respondent: Varies by instrument, from approximately 5 minutes for feedback on a listed counter-UAS system to approximately 5 hours for initial policy adoption and attestation; a detection and warning operations plan is estimated at approximately 45 minutes and a mitigation operations plan at approximately 1 hour.
8. Frequency: On occasion for most instruments; annually for policy attestation renewals and testing, training, and exercise plans; semiannually for the semiannual summary; once for form training; ongoing for recordkeeping.
9. Total Estimated Annual Time Burden: 28,689 hours, across approximately 26,205 annual responses.
10. Total Estimated Annual Other Costs Burden: $0.
If additional information is required, contact: Darwin Arceo, Department Clearance Officer, Enterprise Portfolio Management, Justice Management Division, United States Department of Justice, Two Constitution Square, 145 N Street NE, 4W-218 Washington, DC 20530.

National Credit Union Administration (NCUA)
Interim final rule; request for comments.
The NCUA Board (Board) is amending its regulations governing member business loans and commercial lending. This interim final rule eliminates an outdated, transitional provision that is no longer necessary. This action is necessary to reduce regulatory complexity and improve the clarity of the NCUA's regulations. The intended effect is to enhance clarity and simplify compliance for federally insured credit unions (FICUs).
This rule is effective on November 4, 2026. Comments must be received on or before January 4, 2027.
Comments may be submitted in one of the following ways. (Please send comments by one method only):
Federal eRulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov. The docket number for this rule is NCUA-2026- ( printed page 69496) 1884. Follow the “Submit a comment” instructions. If you are reading this document on federalregister.gov, you may use the green “SUBMIT A PUBLIC COMMENT” button beneath this rulemaking's title to submit a comment to the regulations.gov docket. A plain language summary of the rule is also available on the docket website.
Mail: Address to Melane Conyers-Ausbrooks, Secretary of the Board, National Credit Union Administration, 1775 Duke Street, Alexandria, Virginia 22314-3428.
Hand Delivery/Courier: Same as mailing address. Mailed and hand-delivered comments must be received by the close of the comment period.
Mailed and hand-delivered comments must be received by the close of the comment period.
Public inspection: Please follow the search instructions on https://www.regulations.gov to view the public comments. Do not include any personally identifiable information (such as name, address, or other contact information) or confidential business information that you do not want publicly disclosed. All comments are public records; they are publicly displayed exactly as received and will not be deleted, modified, or redacted. Comments may be submitted anonymously. If you are unable to access public comments on the internet, you may contact the NCUA for alternative access by calling (703) 518-6540 or emailing OGCMail@ncua.gov.
Office of Examination and Insurance: Naghi Khaled, Associate Director, the Office of Examination and Insurance, at (703) 518-6360 or at 1775 Duke Street, Alexandria, VA 22314. Office of General Counsel: Ariel Woodard-Stephens, Staff Attorney, Office of General Counsel, at (703) 518-6540 or at the above address.
The Board is publishing this interim final rule (IFR) amending its regulations at 12 CFR part 723, which governs member business loans and commercial lending for FICUs. This part establishes the safety and soundness standards FICUs must adopt for their commercial lending programs and implements the statutory limits on the aggregate amount of member business loans a credit union may hold, as established by the Federal Credit Union Act (FCU Act). The Board's statutory authority for this part is derived from several provisions of the FCU Act, including 12 U.S.C. 1756, 1757, 1757A, 1766, 1785, and 1789.
On March 14, 2016, the Board published a final rule that substantially revised part 723.[1] The primary purpose of the 2016 rulemaking, which was part of the NCUA's Regulatory Modernization Initiative, was to modernize the agency's regulation of member business lending by shifting from a prescriptive, rules-based framework to a broad, principles-based regulatory approach. The prior rule included prescriptive requirements and limitations related to collateral, security, equity, and loan amounts. The Board determined that this approach caused credit unions to manage their lending practices based on rigid regulatory restrictions rather than on sound, individualized risk management practices. Furthermore, the prior rule's associated waiver process had become burdensome for both credit unions and the NCUA, requiring significant time and resources and sometimes preventing credit unions from acting on borrower applications in a timely manner.
The 2016 final rule was designed to provide FICUs with greater flexibility and individual autonomy to safely and soundly offer commercial loans to their members. It eliminated many of the prescriptive requirements and the associated waiver process, focusing instead on broad principles that clarified regulatory expectations for safe and sound commercial lending. To facilitate the shift, the 2016 final rule included transitional provisions at § 723.9, which became generally effective on January 1, 2017. This section was intended to govern circumstances where, at the time the new rule took effect, a FICU was operating under a waiver approved by the NCUA or was subject to an enforcement constraint related to its commercial lending activities.
Section 723.9(a) addresses previously approved waivers. Because the 2016 rule eliminated the prescriptive requirements for which waivers were typically granted, it rendered most such waivers moot as of the effective date. The provision established a specific exception, however, for waivers that had been granted for borrowing relationship limits. These specific waivers were grandfathered, allowing the existing debt relationship to continue, but prohibited any increase in the debt associated with those relationships.
Section 723.9(b) addresses ongoing enforcement constraints. This provision clarified that any limitations or other conditions imposed on a FICU through a written directive from the NCUA, such as a Document of Resolution or a Letter of Understanding and Agreement, were unaffected by the adoption of the new part. All such pre-existing constraints were to remain in place until formally modified or removed by the NCUA.
The Federal Credit Union (FCU) Act grants the Board a broad mandate to issue regulations governing both insured federal and state-chartered credit unions. Section 120 of the FCU Act is a general grant of regulatory authority, and it authorizes the Board to prescribe regulations for the administration of the FCU Act. Section 209 of the FCU Act is a plenary grant of regulatory authority to the NCUA to issue regulations necessary or appropriate to carry out its role as share insurer for all insured credit unions.
II. Discussion of the Interim Final Rule
The Board now amends its commercial lending regulations by removing the transitional provisions at § 723.9, which was intended to provide a clear and orderly transition from the former framework to the current principles-based approach to commercial lending. Paragraph (a) of the section rendered most pre-2017 waivers moot while grandfathering certain borrowing relationship waivers. Paragraph (b) clarified that existing enforcement constraints remained in effect. The circumstances this section was designed to address are no longer relevant to the ongoing operations of FICUs. The continued presence of this historical text in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) serves no practical function. The Board notes that any outstanding loans that were grandfathered remain grandfathered. As such, the Board finds that § 723.9 has served its purpose and is now outdated and requests comment on its removal from the CFR.
III. Regulatory Procedures
A. Administrative Procedure Act
The Administrative Procedure Act (APA) authorizes agencies to issue regulations without notice and public comment when an agency finds for good cause (and incorporates the finding and a brief statement of reasons thereof in the rules issued) that notice and comment is “impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.” [2] With respect to the “unnecessary” prong of the good cause exception, courts have generally held that its use is “confined to those ( printed page 69497) situations in which the administrative rule is a routine determination, insignificant in nature and impact, and inconsequential to the industry and to the public.” [3] The Board has determined that this rulemaking to remove an obsolete provision is exempt from the APA's notice and comment requirement.
Circumstances warrant publishing the removal of § 723.9 as an interim final rule. Effective January 1, 2017, § 723.9 was intended to govern circumstances where a FICU was operating under a waiver approved by the NCUA at the time the new rule took effect or was subject to an enforcement constraint related to its commercial lending activities.[4] Section 723.9(a) addresses previously approved waivers and (b) governs enforcement. Because the 2016 rule eliminated the prescriptive requirements for which waivers were typically granted, it rendered most such waivers moot as of the effective date.[5] At present, this transitional provision has been in place for eight years.[6]
In consultation with our regions, the Board renders this provision obsolete. Accordingly, the Board finds good cause exists to forego pre-promulgation notice and comment and issue this IFR. However, the Board seeks public comment on the removal of § 723.9 and will carefully consider each comment received to determine whether further changes are needed.
B. Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act of 2023
The Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act of 2023 (Act) requires that a notice of proposed rulemaking includes the internet address of a summary of not more than 100 words in length of a proposed rule, in plain language, that shall be posted on the internet website under section 206(d) of the E-Government Act of 2002 (commonly known as regulations.gov ).[7] The Act, under its terms, applies to notices of proposed rulemaking and does not expressly include other types of documents that the Board publishes voluntarily for public comment, such as notices and interim-final rules that request comment despite invoking “good cause” to forgo such notice and public procedure. As stated previously, this rulemaking is not subject to notice and comment as it removes an obsolete provision, and the Board will not issue a notice of proposed rulemaking. Nevertheless, to promote consistency and transparency, the Board is providing a plain language summary that meets the Act's requirements.
In summary, the Board is amending its regulations governing member business loans and commercial lending by eliminating an obsolete transitional provision.
The rule and required summary can be found at https://www.regulations.gov.
C. Executive Order 12866, 13563, and 14192
Pursuant to Executive Order 12866 (“Regulatory Planning and Review”), a determination must be made whether a regulatory action is significant and therefore subject to review by the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), within the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) in accordance with the requirements of the Executive Order.[8] Executive Order 13563 (“Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review”) supplements and reaffirms the principles, structures, and definitions governing contemporary regulatory review established in Executive Order 12866.[9] This interim final rule was drafted and reviewed in accordance with Executive Order 12866 and Executive Order 13563. OIRA has determined that this interim final rule is not a “significant regulatory action” as defined by section 3(f) of Executive Order 12866.
Executive Order 14192 (“Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation”) requires that any new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall, to the extent permitted by law, be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least 10 prior regulations.[10] This interim final rule is not an Executive Order 14192 regulatory action because this rule is not significant under Executive Order 12866.
D. The Regulatory Flexibility Act
The Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) requires that special consideration be given to the effects of regulations on small entities.[11] When an agency engages in notice and comment rulemaking or is required to publish a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking it must prepare a regulatory flexibility analysis describing the impact of the rule on small entities unless the agency certifies that the rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities. If the agency makes such a certification, it shall publish the certification at the time of publication of either the proposed rule or the final rule, along with a statement providing the factual basis for such certification.
As previously discussed, consistent with the APA, the Board has determined that general notice and opportunity for public comment does not apply to the removal of § 723.9's obsolete transition provision.[12] Rules that are exempt from notice and comment procedures are also exempt from RFA requirements, including conducting a regulatory flexibility analysis, when among other things the agency for good cause finds that notice and public procedure are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest. Accordingly, the Board has concluded that the RFA's requirements relating to initial and final regulatory flexibility analysis do not apply.
The Board, however, has elected to address the Act's requirement in the interests of administrative consistency and transparency. For purposes of this analysis, the NCUA considers small credit unions to be those having under $100 million in assets. Accordingly, the NCUA certifies the proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small credit unions.
E. The Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995
The Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA) generally provides that an agency may not conduct or sponsor, and not withstanding any other provision of law, a person is not required to respond to a collection of information, unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number. The PRA applies to rulemakings in which an agency creates a new or amends existing information collection requirements. For purposes of the PRA, an information-collection requirement may take the form of reporting, recordkeeping, or a third-party disclosure requirement. The ( printed page 69498) member business loan information collection is assigned OMB Control Number 3133-0101. This rule does not revise OMB Control Number 3133-0101.
F. Executive Order on Federalism
Executive Order 13132 encourages certain agencies to consider the impact of their actions on state and local interests. The NCUA, an agency as defined in 44 U.S.C. 3502(5), complies with the executive order to adhere to fundamental federalism principles. The IFR does not have substantial direct effects on the states, on the relationship between the federal government and the states, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government. While the rule applies to federally insured, state-chartered credit unions, its goal is to eliminate an outdated provision. The Board does not anticipate any impact on state-chartered credit unions and state regulators but welcomes comments on this issue.
G. Assessment of Federal Regulations and Policies on Families
The NCUA has determined that this rule will not affect family well-being within the meaning of Section 654 of the Treasury and General Government Appropriations, 1999. The proposed rule merely removes obsolete regulatory provisions.
F. Congressional Review Act
Subtitle E of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (also known as the Congressional Review Act or CRA) generally provides for congressional review of agency rules.[13] NCUA must submit a report to Congress and the Comptroller General when it issues a final rule, as defined by the CRA.[14] An agency rule, in addition to being subject to congressional oversight, may also be subject to a delayed effective date if the rule is a “major rule.” OIRA has determined that this interim final rule is not a major rule as defined by the CRA.[15] The delayed effective date required by the CRA does not apply to any rule for which an agency for good cause finds (and incorporates the finding and a brief statement of reasons therefor in the rule issued) that notice and public procedure thereon are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.[16] For the same reasons noted above with respect to forgoing notice and comment in adopting this final rule, NCUA is adopting the final rule without the delayed effective date generally prescribed under the CRA.

National Credit Union Administration (NCUA).
The NCUA Board (Board) is issuing a final rule adopting as final the revisions to the capital adequacy rule and the member business lending rule made under an interim final rule (IFR) published in the Federal Register on April 27, 2020.
The final rule is effective on November 4, 2026.
John H. Brolin, Senior Staff Attorney, Office of General Counsel, at (703) 518-6540 or at 1775 Duke Street, Alexandria, VA 22314.
On March 27, 2020, President Trump signed the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (CARES Act) into law.[1] The law provided aid to the U.S. economy during the COVID-19 pandemic. The CARES Act authorized the Small Business Administration (SBA) to create a loan guarantee program, the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), in response to the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on small businesses. The PPP helped participating businesses meet payroll needs and utilities, including employee salaries, sick leave, other paid leave, and health insurance expenses. Provided that credit union lenders complied with the applicable lender obligations set forth in the SBA's interim final rule (IFR), the SBA fully guaranteed loans issued under the PPP. Most federally insured credit unions (FICUs) were eligible to make PPP loans to members.[2] Under the CARES Act, PPP loans received a zero percent risk weighting under the NCUA's risk-based capital requirements.[3]
On April 27, 2020, the Board issued an IFR (April 27th IFR) to make a conforming amendment to its capital adequacy regulation following the enactment of the CARES Act.[4] As noted, the CARES Act required that, under the NCUA's risk-based capital requirements, PPP loans receive a zero percent risk weighting. To reflect the statutory requirement, the April 27th IFR amended the NCUA's capital adequacy regulation to provide that covered PPP loans receive a zero percent risk weight. The April 27th IFR also provided that the covered loan could be excluded from a credit union's accounting of total assets in its net worth ratio calculation if the covered loan was pledged as collateral for a non-recourse loan that was provided as part of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System's (FRB) PPP Loan Facility. The April 27th IFR also made a conforming amendment to the definition of commercial loan in the NCUA's member business loans and commercial lending rule. The Board found good cause to issue the April 27th IFR without advance notice-and-comment procedures and with an effective date upon publication.
This rule adopts as final the revisions to the capital adequacy rule and the member business lending rule published in the Federal Register on April 27, 2020.[5] The Board is adopting this IFR as final. Under this final rule, FICUs may continue to assign a zero percent risk weight to PPP loans under the NCUA's risk-based capital regulations and neutralize the regulatory capital effects of participating in the PPP Liquidity Facility (PPP Loan Facility). Because the IFR was effective immediately upon publication and the final rule does not require affected parties to adjust their behavior before the final rule takes effect, the Board is issuing this final rule to address the types of matters described in this paragraph with an immediate effective date.[6]
The Board has the legal authority to issue this final rule pursuant to its plenary rulemaking authority under the Federal Credit Union Act and its specific rulemaking authority under the various provisions the Board administers.[7]
A. Zero Percent Risk Weight for PPP Loans
The NCUA's April 27th IFR amended the NCUA's risk-based net worth rules to reflect the requirement that PPP loans receive a zero percent risk weight. In particular, the IFR classified PPP loans as low-risk assets. Under prior § 702.106(d), low-risk assets received a zero percent risk weight.[8] In addition, § 702.104(d) defined low-risk assets as cash on hand (for example, coin and currency, including vault, ATM and teller cash), the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund deposit, debt instruments unconditionally guaranteed by the NCUA, and loans issued under the SBA's PPP.[9] Thus, the April 27th IFR provided that PPP loans received a zero percent risk weight under the NCUA's risk-based capital rules as required by the CARES Act.
The NCUA's 2015 final rule regarding risk-based capital (2015 Final Rule) [10] went into effect on January 1, 2022,[11] making substantial changes to the NCUA's previous prompt corrective action (PCA) requirements under part 702 of the NCUA's regulations. Among other changes, the 2015 Final Rule eliminated the definition of “low risk asset” under § 702.104(d). To account for this change, in a December 23, 2021, final rule on capital adequacy (December 2021 Final Rule), the NCUA gave covered loans issued under the SBA's PPP a zero percent risk weight.[12] This amendment finalized the change made to the previous PCA regulations by the April 27th IFR, thus this final rule does not affect the changes that were made by the NCUA's December 2021 Final Rule and no further amendment is required.
B. Definition of Total Assets for Purposes of Calculating the Net Worth Ratio
Pursuant to section 13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act, the FRB authorized each of the Federal Reserve Banks to participate in the PPP Loan Facility as a means to provide liquidity to small business lenders and the broader credit markets, help stabilize the financial system, and provide economic relief to ( printed page 69494) small businesses nationwide.[13] Through the PPP Loan Facility, each of the Federal Reserve Banks extended non-recourse loans to eligible financial institutions to fund PPP loans. Under this construct, only PPP loans that were guaranteed by the SBA with respect to both principal and interest and were originated by an eligible institution could be pledged as collateral to the Federal Reserve Banks. Participation in the PPP Loan Facility affected a FICU's balance sheet because, as a function of participating in the PPP Loan Facility, the FICU was required to originate and hold PPP covered loans (that is, assets that are eligible collateral pledged to the Federal Reserve Banks) on its balance sheet.
As a result, FICUs that participated in the PPP Loan Facility could potentially be subject to increased regulatory capital requirements due to the increase in total assets from originating and holding PPP loans. To facilitate use of the PPP Loan Facility, the April 27th IFR allowed FICUs to neutralize the regulatory capital effects of PPP loans pledged to the PPP Loan Facility.[14]
Additionally, the Board believed that holding credit unions to the regulatory capital requirements for those PPP loans did not reflect the substantial protections (including the non-recourse nature of the FRB's extension of credit to a FICU) from risk provided to credit unions by the PPP Loan Facility. The Board believed that it was appropriate to exclude pledged PPP loans from regulatory capital.[15] Accordingly, the April 27th IFR excluded PPP loans pledged as collateral to the PPP Loan Facility from the definition of total assets in § 702.2 for purposes of calculating a FICU's net worth ratio.
As discussed previously, when the NCUA's 2015 Final Rule [16] went into effect on January 1, 2022,[17] it made substantial changes to the NCUA's PCA requirements under part 702 of the NCUA's regulations. Among other changes, the 2015 Final Rule eliminated the PPP loan provision that had been added by the April 27th IFR under the definition of “total assets.” [18] To account for this change, the definition of total assets in 12 CFR 702.2 was amended by the NCUA's December 2021 Final Rule to carry forward the PPP-related change made in the April 27th IFR. Specifically, under the NCUA's December 2021 Final Rule, the definition of total assets in current § 702.2 was amended to explicitly state that PPP loans pledged to the FRB's PPP Loan Facility to support PPP lending are excluded from the definition of total assets.[19] This finalized the change to the definition made by the April 27th IFR. Accordingly, this final rule does not affect the changes that were already made final by the NCUA's December 2021 Final Rule.[20]
C. Definition of Commercial Loan
The April 27th IFR clarified that PPP loans would not constitute commercial loans under part 723 of the NCUA's regulations. Commercial loans are generally defined as any loan, line of credit, or letter of credit (including any unfunded commitments), and any interest a credit union obtains in such loans made by another lender, to individuals, sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, or other business enterprises for commercial, industrial, agricultural, or professional purposes, but not for personal expenditure purposes.[21]
The current definition also provides various exclusions. The April 27th IFR amended the commercial loan definition to add PPP loans issued under the CARES Act as an exclusion from the definition of commercial loan in § 723.2. While other federally guaranteed loans may still be considered commercial loans under the regulation, the unique nature of PPP loans mitigates the need for enhanced commercial underwriting of these loans. The SBA's IFR specifically limits each lender's underwriting obligation under the PPP to the items noted in the rule.[22] Lenders are also held harmless for any borrower's failure to comply with PPP criteria and, in addition to the 100 percent guarantee, PPP loans may qualify for loan forgiveness.
The NCUA received no comments opposing this amendment made by the April 27th IFR to the definition of commercial loan in § 723.2. Commenters generally discussed that PPP loans are unique and the rules governing the PPP loans specifically limited the lender's underwriting responsibilities. One commenter said that applying the enhanced due diligence of the NCUA's part 723 to these loans is of little supervisory benefit. For these reasons, the Board is adopting as final the changes made to the definition of commercial loan made by the IFR. Accordingly, this rule makes final the sentence in the definition of “commercial loan” under § 723.2, that excludes from the definition covered loans issued under the SBA's PPP.[23]
A. Executive Orders 12866, 13563, 14192
Pursuant to Executive Order 12866 (“Regulatory Planning and Review”), a determination must be made whether a regulatory action is significant and therefore subject to review by the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), within the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) in accordance with the requirements of the Executive Order.[24] Executive Order 13563 (“Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review”) supplements and reaffirms the principles, structures, and definitions governing contemporary regulatory review established in Executive Order 12866.[25] This final rule was drafted and reviewed in accordance with Executive Order 12866 and Executive Order 13563. OIRA has determined that this final rule is not a “significant regulatory action” as defined by section 3(f) of Executive Order 12866.
Executive Order 14192 (“Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation”) requires that any new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall, to the extent permitted by law, be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least 10 prior regulations.[26] This final rule is not an Executive Order 14192 regulatory action because this rule is not significant under Executive Order 12866. This final rule ( printed page 69495) is considered an Executive Order 14192 deregulatory action.
B. The Regulatory Flexibility Act
The Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) generally requires that, in connection with a notice of proposed rulemaking, an agency prepare and make available for public comment an initial regulatory flexibility analysis that describes the impact of a proposed rule on small entities. A regulatory flexibility analysis is not required, however, if the agency certifies that the rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities (defined for purposes of the RFA to include credit unions with assets less than $100 million) [27] and publishes its certification and a short, explanatory statement in the Federal Register together with the rule. Moreover, rules for which notice and comment procedures are not required are not subject to the RFA's requirements, including conducting a regulatory flexibility analysis.[28] Consistent with the APA,[29] the Board determined for good cause in the IFR finalized by this rulemaking that general notice and opportunity for public comment is unnecessary and, therefore, the Board did not issue a notice of proposed rulemaking. Accordingly, the Board has concluded that the RFA's requirements relating to initial and final regulatory flexibility analyses do not apply.
Nevertheless, the Board fully considered the potential economic impact of the regulatory changes during the development of the rule. As noted in the preamble, the final rule adopts as final the amendments made by an IFR. The rule will not impose any new significant burden on FICUs. Accordingly, the NCUA certifies that this final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small FICUs.
C. The Paperwork Reduction Act
The Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA) generally provides that an agency may not conduct or sponsor, and not withstanding any other provision of law, a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information, unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget control number. The PRA applies to rulemakings in which an agency creates a new or amends existing information collection requirements. For purposes of the PRA, an information-collection requirement may take the form of a reporting, recordkeeping, or a third-party disclosure requirement. The NCUA has determined that the changes in this notice do not create a new information collection or revise an existing information collection as defined by the PRA.
D. Executive Order 13132 on Federalism
Executive Order 13132 encourages certain agencies to consider the impact of their actions on state and local interests. The NCUA, an agency as defined in 44 U.S.C. 3502(5), voluntarily complies with the executive order to adhere to fundamental federalism principles. This rule finalizes the amendments made by the IFR. It does not, however, rise to the level of material impact for purposes of Executive Order 13132 given that the rule makes no forward-looking changes to the NCUA's regulations.
E. Assessment of Federal Regulations and Policies on Families
The NCUA has determined that this final rule will not affect family well-being within the meaning of section 654 of the Treasury and General Government Appropriations Act, 1999, Public Law 105-277, 112 Stat. 2681 (1998) given that the rule makes no changes to the NCUA's regulations.
F. Congressional Review Act
Subtitle E of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (also known as the Congressional Review Act or CRA) generally provides for congressional review of agency rules.[30] NCUA must submit a report to Congress and the Comptroller General when it issues a final rule, as defined by the CRA.[31] An agency rule, in addition to being subject to congressional oversight, may also be subject to a delayed effective date if the rule is a “major rule.” OIRA has determined that this final rule is not a major rule as defined by the CRA.[32]
The delayed effective date required by the CRA does not apply to any rule for which an agency for good cause finds (and incorporates the finding and a brief statement of reasons therefor in the rule issued) that notice and public procedure thereon are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.[33] For the same reasons noted above with respect to an immediate effective date in adopting this final rule, NCUA is adopting the final rule without the delayed effective date generally prescribed under the CRA.

民進黨雲林縣長參選人劉建國（右）4日與台北市長參選人沈伯洋（左）手沖咖啡，邀民眾週末到古坑逛台灣咖啡節。 （劉建國提供） 中央社記者姜宜菁傳真 115年11月4日
（中央社記者姜宜菁雲林縣4日電）民進黨雲林縣長參選人劉建國今天與台北市長參選人沈伯洋手沖咖啡，邀民眾逛台灣咖啡節；國民黨雲林縣長參選人張嘉郡提「雲林ACG青年創業計畫」6大行動，鼓勵動漫創作。
劉建國今天與古坑鄉長林慧如，把古坑精品咖啡帶進立法院，邀請沈伯洋一同磨豆、手沖、品咖啡，為古坑咖啡宣傳，也邀請民眾週末到古坑逛台灣咖啡節。
「再忙，也要與伯洋喝一杯台灣道地、古坑最香、最甘、最醇的咖啡！」劉建國表示，一杯咖啡從栽培、採收、後製到烘焙，凝聚農民與職人的時間和心力。近年極端氣候讓咖啡收成更不容易，希望大家從喝一杯、買一包開始，支持台灣咖啡農，進一步走訪產地、認識古坑。
沈伯洋以「小水滴匯聚成洋流」比喻選舉與民主。沈伯洋說，好咖啡靠一滴一滴累積，選舉也是每個人一個一個站出來，才會形成強大力量，「一滴都不能少」，並呼籲大家11月28日返鄉投票。劉建國希望大家都能喝著台灣道地的古坑咖啡、聊台灣未來，一起打一場正面的選舉。
張嘉郡今天提出「雲林ACG青年創業計畫」6大行動，從空間活化、資金支持、國際接案、IP商品化、人才培育及品牌活動等面向，鼓勵喜愛動畫、漫畫及遊戲的青年創作、創業，並提供創業支持金，最高可獲補助新台幣48萬元。
張嘉郡指出，「ACG」是動畫（Animation）、漫畫（Comic）與遊戲（Games）的縮寫，此產業為目前極具發展潛力的文化內容產業，未來將從大學育成到商業接軌、從歷史空間到動漫街區，與學界及地方共同努力，讓動漫融入斗六、斗南的街區生活，成為雲林兼具創意、產業與觀光的新特色。
受邀出席的雲林科技大學副教授翁漢騰期盼藉由學界的專業與實務經驗，共同為雲林的動漫產業打下穩固基礎。翁漢騰帶領學生以張嘉郡爭取的建設與政見為題，製作一篇漫畫作品，當場致贈給張嘉郡。（編輯：李錫璋）1151104

國民黨新北市長參選人李四川（前右白衣者）與同黨市議員曾煥嘉的聯合競選總部成立大會4日舉行，李四川出席並與支持鄉親致意。中央社記者黃旭昇攝 115年11月4日
（中央社記者黃旭昇新北4日電）新北市長侯友宜、中國國民黨前主席洪秀柱，今天為市長參選人李四川與同黨籍市議員曾煥嘉聯合競選總部成立站台。李四川說，將強化板橋聯外交通動脈，也打造「新北小巨蛋」。
李四川與新北市議員曾煥嘉聯合競選總部成立大會，今天在板橋區民生公園舉行，在地里長、鄉親揮舞旗幟熱情相挺，高喊「凍蒜」；侯友宜、洪秀柱、國民黨立法委員葉元之與新北市議員陳偉杰到場站台。
侯友宜致詞表示，李四川是他多年並肩作戰的兄弟，從共同擔任新北市副市長時就建立深厚的合作默契。他說，城市建設講求一棒接一棒，捷運環狀線、市立土城醫院順利營運，都是跨任期接力完成的典範。
侯友宜推薦李四川是新北建設的重要推手，未來「板橋醫療園區」與「新北大巨蛋」等重大建設，更需要交由最熟悉市政與工程的李四川接續完成。
李四川表示，自己住在板橋區多年，板橋也是新北市的發展關鍵樞紐，將以40餘年的工程專業與市政經驗，接續侯友宜的建設方向，推動地方建設與「泰板輕軌」等聯外交通。
李四川說，如當選將結合以往興建台北小巨蛋與推動台北大巨蛋完工的實務經驗，將板橋體育館升級為兼具國際賽事、大型演唱會與多元展演功能的「新北小巨蛋」，並加速推進「板橋醫療園區」，深化板橋、土城與中和區的醫療分工，建構優質的大板橋醫療生活圈。
李四川說，將與里長一起合作傾聽需求；對於長者的照顧，也會將敬老卡點數中的300點，擴大用於超商、超市、農會、藥局購物，照顧長者民生需求。
新北會計師後援會今天傍晚也在李四川競選總部成立，到場會計師為李四川加油打氣並合影。（編輯：李錫璋）1151104

content:
韩联社首尔11月4日电 韩国联合参谋本部（联参）4日表示，军方探测到朝鲜当天上午在咸镜南道宣德一带向韩半岛东部海域发射多枚导弹。
联参表示，韩美从朝鲜发射准备阶段起就进行严密监视，并在发射后立即展开追踪。双方正基于牢固的联合防卫态势密切关注朝方各种动向，保持能够压倒性应对任何挑衅的戒备态势。
联参通常在发现朝鲜发射弹道导弹后立即向媒体通报，而在当天通报中‌使用了“导弹”这一表述而非“弹道导弹”。据悉，军方研判朝鲜所射飞行器飞行距离不及300公里，因此不排除朝方发射近程弹道导弹（CRBM）的可能性，正对导弹的具体参数进行分析。
11月4日，在首尔火车站候车室，市民收看有关朝鲜射弹的新闻报道。 韩联社
值得关注的是，朝鲜此次射弹在美国中期选举当日（当地时间3日）、劳动党中央委员会总务部长金与正发表谈话提及“对话选项”之际进行。金与正在谈话中称，维护和平的选项中无疑包括对话，但对朝鲜而言，这未必能与国家利益相提并论。此番话被解读为，朝鲜为与美方对话留下余地，但不会只执着于对话这一条路。
若朝鲜发射的飞行器被证实为弹道导弹，这将是朝鲜在一周内第三次发射弹道导弹；若包括巡航导弹，这就是朝鲜最近一周内第四次发起导弹挑衅。上月29日，朝鲜同时发射了10多枚600毫米口径超大型火箭炮（KN-25）；同月31日，朝鲜进行了战术弹道导弹散布战斗部（集束弹头）战斗适用性及威力评估试验。本月3日，朝鲜又公布了2日进行的战略巡航导弹散布战斗部威力评估试验和垂直打击飞行特性试验结果。（完）

content:
台北市长选战进入白热化阶段，街头观察显示，相较于绿营议员候选人看板频繁与民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋合体，与现任市长蒋万安合体的蓝营议员看板似乎不如预期中多。图为沈伯洋（左）与同党松山信义区市议员候选人洪健益合体登上路口巨型看板，下方驶过的巴士车身则有蒋万安的竞选广告。 （缪宗翰摄）
台北市长选战进入白热化阶段，蓝绿阵营母鸡效应的方向正在改变，显示选战进入新一轮拉锯。国民党阵营从现任市长蒋万安早期凭领先声势带动议员候选人，在民进党籍挑战者沈伯洋声势上升后反而转为议员集体陪同企图拉抬市长选情；沈伯洋则从本来要靠议员带着频走地方，转为议员借“洋流”聚集人潮、带动选情。
两人10月31日举行首场电视辩论。主办单位之一的TVBS隔天公布辩论后电话调查，蒋万安以46%支持率领先沈伯洋42%，差距缩至四个百分点；另有47%受访者认为沈伯洋辩论表现较佳，40%认为蒋万安较佳。
蒋万安在辩论后宣示“吹起反攻的号角”，攻防随即转向街头。沈伯洋11月1日则在大安文山区举行车队扫街拜票，并在大安森林公园集结和开讲政见，直捣蓝营铁票仓，台媒报道现场逾3万5000人参与。
隔天，蒋万安到同个公园向晨运民众拜票，并称将走访各公园争取支持；星期二（11月3日）晚间，更与高雄市长候选人柯志恩在“洋流”起始地点宁夏夜市联合街扫。
沈伯洋以大规模集结展现洋流动员，蒋万安则回防同一地点，再与柯志恩跨区合体，双方较量由辩论表现转向街头声势和组织动员。
台北市长蒋万安（中右）与国民党高雄市长候选人柯志恩（中左）11月3日晚在台北宁夏夜市合体扫街拜票，展现国民党跨县市联动辅选。（缪宗翰摄）
从提名以来，蒋万安一度明显领先。国民党7月正式征召蒋万安竞选连任；TVBS 5月民调显示，蒋万安以58%领先沈伯洋的30%。
随着沈伯洋知名度提高，加上台北市食安、鼠患及儿虐等市政问题受到检视，TVBS 10月上旬民调显示，蒋万安支持率降至49%，沈伯洋升至41%，差距缩至8个百分点。
10月19日，台中市长卢秀燕出任蒋万安竞选总部主委，台北市五名国民党立委也加入竞选团队，出现地方诸侯和党籍立委共同助选的罕见场景。
民进党5月提名沈伯洋时，他是立委与学者，没有地方选举经验，知名度也不及现任市长；去年积极参与大罢免行动更使他成为蓝营攻击焦点。
早期民调中，沈伯洋落后蒋万安近三成。之后，沈伯洋透过走访地方、与议员合体及街头开讲增加曝光。8月18日，沈伯洋到宁夏夜市扫街，支持者沿途等候、排队签名合照；这场活动也成为“洋流”形成的早期节点。
10月11日，首场大洋流大型车扫从中山、大同区出发，逾2000名骑士加入，晚间在大龙峒保安宫开讲，现场近万人，直播观看逾6万人次。“洋流加油站”串联地方议员竞选总部，将沈伯洋的行程衔接议员选区组织。
民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋（中）参选初期知名度低，需要由绿营议员陪同拜票，但在9月“洋流”声量上涨后，沈伯洋逐渐从被小鸡带动，转为带动同党议员选情。图为沈伯洋10月4日在台北竞选总部成立活动上发表政见。（法新社档案照片）
政治学所称的“裙摆效应”（coattail effect），是指某一层级的高人气候选人带动同党其他层级参选人的得票，台湾选战常称为“母鸡带小鸡”。
这次选战中，蓝营从蒋万安早期领先、带动小鸡，转为在沈伯洋声势上升后加强合体看板和集体陪同，出现“小鸡撑母鸡”趋势；绿营则由议员带着知名度不足的沈伯洋跑地方，转为沈伯洋以大洋流集结人潮、带动小鸡。
曾任蒋万安国会办公室法案助理的国民党籍台北市议员詹为元接受《联合早报》采访时分析，市长候选人选情看好，能提高支持者投票热情，进而带动同党议员；但中间选民不会因为投票支持蒋万安，就自然把票投给国民党议员，“他（中间选民）不会因为母鸡的声势强或弱来决定他的外溢会不会到议员的部分”，议员仍须各自争取。
看板是母鸡效应的可见信号。街头观察显示，相较于绿营议员候选人看板频繁与沈伯洋合体，与蒋万安合体的蓝营议员看板似乎不如预期中多。
担任过丁守中、郝龙斌及江启臣竞选团队发言人的詹为元说，起初他认为市长与市议员合体“本来就是必然的事情”，自己曾在蒋万安办公室工作，不必靠看板证明两人的关系。后来看到绿营候选人与沈伯洋合体看板增加，詹为元才有意识地增挂与蒋万安的合照，“不想让这个声势（给人感觉）好像蒋万安都没出现”，其他蓝营议员也随后跟进。
台北民权东路与吉林路口可见民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋与同党市议员候选人林亮君、颜若芳合体看板，下方则有国民党市议员候选人叶林传等蓝营候选人的竞选广告。（缪宗翰摄）
詹为元也提到，蒋万安声势受到挑战后，蓝营议员反而更常集体陪同蒋万安到选区，没有因民调胶着而“跑掉”。他强调：“就算小鸡撑母鸡也没关系。”
民进党籍台北市议员颜若芳是中山、大同选区议员，也参与了沈伯洋“台北大洋流”首场大型车扫。她接受本报采访时回忆，沈伯洋刚投入选战时知名度不足，地方行程常由议员带着沈伯洋走，“大家（选民）认识议员比认识沈伯洋还要多”。
颜若芳认为，宁夏夜市活动及之后的洋流人潮是转折，选战已从“小鸡带着他（沈伯洋）在地方上跑”，转为“大母鸡带着我们全部的小鸡往前冲”。
民调专家戴立安星期二在信民协会记者会上分析，民进党可能把沈伯洋当作“战略武器”，让沈伯洋短暂、分散地到各地助阵，以免盖过当地候选人或出现边际效应递减；但若离开台北太久，也可能让选民质疑“你不在台北”。
综合来看，台北市长选战的母鸡效应已从看板合影延伸到地方造势、集体拜票与跨区行程。选举结果将检验市长候选人的声势能否落到议员票上，也将显示小鸡在借力母鸡之后，能否建立自己的地方支持。

content:
中国官方星期三（11月4日）公布，从公众视野中“消失”多时的武警上将、武警部队原司令员王宁，被免去全国政协常委、外事委员会副主任职务，并被撤销全国政协委员资格。 （互联网）
中国官方公布，从公众视野中“消失”多时的武警上将、武警部队原司令员王宁，被免去全国政协常委、外事委员会副主任职务，并被撤销全国政协委员资格。包括王宁在内，中国连续三任武警司令员全数“出事”。
据新华社报道，中国全国政协第十四届全国委员会常务委员会第十九次会议，星期三（11月4日）下午在北京闭幕。中共政治局常委、中国全国政协主席王沪宁主持闭幕会并讲话。
经表决，会议通过关于申长雨不再担任第十四届全国政协常委职务，并接受他请辞委员的决定；通过关于免去王宁第十四届全国政协常委、外事委员会副主任职务，并撤销他委员资格的决定；通过关于撤销张建明、余艳红、王彤宙第十四届全国政协委员资格的决定。
公开信息显示，63岁的申长雨是中国科学院院士、中国国家知识产权局原局长。官方通稿仍以“同志”称呼申长雨，但在提到王宁等人时，则没有以“同志”来称呼。
71岁的王宁是曾是武警部队司令员、党委副书记，在2015年晋升武警上将警衔。他也是第十九届中共中央委员。
王宁自2023年3月起开始担任第十四届全国政协常委、全国政协外事委员会副主任，至此番被撤职。
王宁已从公众视野中消失多时，他早在今年3月，就已缺席全国“两会”（人大、政协年会）这一中国年度重要政治活动。
王宁的前任、武警部队原司令员王建平在2016年落马，成为2012年中共十八大后首位落马的现役解放军上将。
2020年接任王宁出任武警司令员的王春宁，因涉嫌严重违纪违法，在去年被开除中共党籍和军籍。
其余被撤资格的三人中，张建明是四川明宇集团有限公司董事长；余艳红曾任中国国家卫生健康委员会党组成员，以及国家中医药管理局党组书记、局长等职；王彤宙曾任中国交通建设集团有限公司中共党委书记、董事长。中国媒体曾报道，王彤宙在去年6月“被带走”。
据新华社报道，中共政治局委员、中国全国政协副主席石泰峰，全国政协副主席胡春华、沈跃跃、王勇、周强、何厚铧、梁振英、巴特尔、苏辉、邵鸿、高云龙、穆虹、咸辉、王东峰、姜信治、蒋作君、何报翔、王光谦、秦博勇、朱永新、杨震出席了星期三闭幕的这次政协会议。

中新社台北11月4日电 交易商称，台湾股市周三收盘走低，但从当日低点回升，原因是股价下跌后逢低买进，而投资者则对美国中期选举进行评估，预计民主党将在此次中期选举中获得国会控制权。
台湾证券交易所基准指数在 41,855.82 点至 43,741.54 点之间波动，最终下跌 358.63 点，至 42,948.91 点，跌幅为 0.83%。成交总额为新台币 1.11 万亿（340.2 亿美元），高于周二的约新台币 1 万亿。
Mega International Investment Services分析师亚历克斯·黄(Alex Huang)表示，“这是一场戏剧性的会议，特朗普表示他将与民主党合作，预计民主党将在中期选举中大获全胜，之后投资者在中午左右开始买入。”
黄指的是《纽约时报》的一篇报道，其中美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示他将接受选举结果，并期待与民主党合作。
黄说：“从技术上讲，随着台交所跌破42,000点，买入机会出现，因此在美国AI芯片设计商AMD和AI服务器制造商Supermicro隔夜公布好于预期的业绩后，抄底者开始买入精选的AI相关半导体股票。” “所以，今天的成交量扩大了。”
半导体股中，智能手机集成电路设计公司联发科上涨1.09%，收于新台币3,715.00元；IC封装测试公司日月光上涨1.79%，收于新台币627.00元。
占市场总价值超过 40% 的合约芯片制造商台积电 (TSMC) 下跌 1.53%，收于新台币 2,260.00 元，但从新台币 2,235.00 元的低点回升。其反弹帮助台交所收复约200点。
科技股方面，智能手机镜头供应商大立光电因应AI热潮，进军光学封装业务，股价上涨1.31%，收于新台币5,010.00元。
iPhone组装商和AI服务器制造商鸿海精密工业公司下跌2.24%，至新台币240.00元；另一家AI服务器供应商广达电脑公司下跌2.89%，收于新台币302.50元。
黄说，投资者还买入了一些传统行业的股票，石化指数上涨了1.19%。
南亚塑胶股上涨2.03%，收于新台币276.50元；台化纤股上涨1.17%，收于新台币69.20元；台塑股上涨0.58%，收于新台币69.10元。
集装箱运输公司也跑赢大盘，长荣海运上涨0.56%，收于新台币268.00元，阳明海运上涨0.32%，收于新台币62.30元。
金融板块下跌0.71%，国泰金控跌1.77%，收于新台币111.00元；富邦金控微涨0.32%，收于新台币154.00元。
“美国中期选举后，不确定性依然存在，”黄说。 “因为特朗普是一个不可预测的人，没有人知道他会做什么。波动可能会持续下去。”
据台交所统计，周三境外机构投资者在主板净售股1,498.99亿元新台币。

Taiwan shares close lower but recover from lows amid U.S. midterms
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 4 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan closed lower Wednesday but recovered from the day's low as bargain hunters bought shares after prices fell, while investors assessed the U.S. midterm elections, in which Democrats were projected to gain control of Congress, dealers said.
The Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, ended down 358.63 points, or 0.83 percent, at 42,948.91 after moving between 41,855.82 and 43,741.54. Turnover totaled NT$1.11 trillion (US$34.02 billion), up from about NT$1 trillion Tuesday.
"It was a dramatic session as investors began buying around noon after Trump said he would work with the Democrats, who were projected to win big in the midterms," Mega International Investment Services analyst Alex Huang said.
Huang was referring to a New York Times report in which U.S. President Donald Trump said he would accept the election results and looked forward to working with the Democrats.
"Technically speaking, buying opportunities emerged as the Taiex dipped below 42,000 points, so bargain hunters began buying select AI-related semiconductor stocks after U.S,-based AI chip designer AMD and AI server maker Supermicro delivered better-than-expected results overnight," Huang said. "So, today's turnover expanded."
Among semiconductor stocks that recovered from earlier weakness, smartphone integrated circuit (IC) designer MediaTek Inc. rose 1.09 percent to close at NT$3,715.00, while IC packaging and testing firm ASE Technology Holding Co. gained 1.79 percent to end at NT$627.00.
Contract chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which accounts for over 40 percent of the market's total value, fell 1.53 percent to close at NT$2,260.00 but recovered from a low of NT$2,235.00. Its rebound helped the Taiex recover about 200 points.
Elsewhere in the tech sector, smartphone camera lens supplier Largan Precision Co., which has entered the co-packaged optics business to tap into the AI boom, rose 1.31 percent to close at NT$5,010.00.
iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. fell 2.24 percent to NT$240.00 and Quanta Computer Inc., another AI server supplier, lost 2.89 percent to close at NT$302.50.
Huang said investors also bought shares in selected traditional industries, with the petrochemical index rising 1.19 percent.
Nan Ya Plastics Corp. rose 2.03 percent to close at NT$276.50, Formosa Chemicals & Fibre Corp. gained 1.17 percent at NT$69.20, and Formosa Plastics Corp. added 0.58 percent to end up at NT$69.10.
Container shippers also outperformed the broader market, with Evergreen Marine Corp. rising 0.56 percent to close at NT$268.00 and Yang Ming Marine Transport Corp. gaining 0.32 percent to NT$62.30.
In the financial sector, which fell 0.71 percent, however, Cathay Financial Holding Co. fell 1.77 percent to close at NT$111.00, while Fubon Financial Holding Co. edged up 0.32 percent to NT$154.00.
"Uncertainty remained after the U.S. midterms," Huang said. "Because Trump is an unpredictable person, nobody knows what he will do. Volatility could continue."
According to the Taiwan Stock Exchange, foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$149.899 billion worth of shares on the main board Wednesday.

content:
2027年QS亚洲排名 台大仍居第23位 - 聚焦台湾
台大2027年QS亚洲排名保持第23位
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社伦敦11月4日电 周二公布的2027年QS亚洲大学排名中，国立台湾大学（NTU）位列第23位，继续保持台湾排名最高的院校，而国立成功大学（NCKU）则在当地学校中跃升幅度最大。
英国高等教育研究公司 QS Quacquarelli Symonds 发布的排名显示，台湾大学有七所进入亚洲前 100 名，其中四所进入前 50 名。
今年的排名共有 59 所台湾院校上榜，评估了亚洲 26 个国家和地区的 1,722 所大学。
台湾排名最高的七所大学是南大（第23位）、成大（第33位）、国立清华大学（第35位）、国立阳明交通大学（第36位）、国立台湾科技大学（第54位）、国立台湾师范大学（第74位）和国立中山大学（第76位）。
台南成大在台湾大学中涨幅最大，上升 10 位至第 33 位。
国立清华大学上升两位至第 35 位，国立阳明交通大学上升 5 位至第 36 位。两所大学均位于台湾半导体中心新竹。
总体而言，台湾的表现好坏参半。根据 QS 的数据，在该国之前排名的大学中，21% 的排名上升，9% 保持不变，70% 下滑，排名净变化为负 49%。
根据 QS 的比较表，台湾在这方面的表现优于日本（-78%），但落后于韩国（-21%）、马来西亚（-10%）和新加坡（+20%）。
QS 表示，就指标而言，台湾的研究影响力依然稳固，多达 20 所台湾大学在相关类别中排名上升。
南洋理工大学在学术声誉和雇主声誉方面名列台湾第一，分别在亚洲排名第 9 和第 19。然而，大多数台湾机构在亚洲的这两个类别中都出现下滑。
QS 表示，国际化仍然是台湾最大的弱点。
尽管2025-26学年国际学生人数达到创纪录的140,420人，但由于地区竞争对手进步更快，大多数台湾大学的国际师资和国际学生比例排名有所下降。
QS高级副总裁Ben Sowter表示，台湾领先的大学继续表现强劲，并与该国先进技术产业的联系不断加深。
他表示，南洋理工大学仍然是亚洲最受尊敬的大学之一，成大、国立清华大学和国立阳明交通大学的排名均名列前茅。
然而，在谈到台湾在国际学生和教师方面的弱点时，索特表示，随着国内大学适龄人口持续萎缩，台湾的学校将需要越来越多地依赖海外人才。
香港大学继续位居榜首，其次是北京大学和清华大学。

National Taiwan University remains 23rd in 2027 QS Asia rankings
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
London, Nov. 4 (CNA) National Taiwan University (NTU) held on to 23rd place in the 2027 QS Asia University Rankings released Tuesday, remaining Taiwan's highest-ranked institution, while National Cheng Kung University (NCKU) posted the biggest jump among local schools.
The rankings, published by British higher education research firm QS Quacquarelli Symonds, placed seven Taiwanese universities among Asia's top 100, including four in the top 50.
A total of 59 Taiwanese institutions were included in this year's rankings, which assessed 1,722 universities across 26 countries and territories in Asia.
The seven highest-ranked Taiwanese universities were NTU (23rd), NCKU (33rd), National Tsing Hua University (35th), National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (36th), National Taiwan University of Science and Technology (54th), National Taiwan Normal University (74th), and National Sun Yat-sen University (76th).
Tainan-based NCKU recorded the biggest gain among Taiwan's universities, climbing 10 places to 33rd.
National Tsing Hua University rose two places to 35th, while National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University advanced five spots to 36th. Both universities are based in Hsinchu, Taiwan's semiconductor hub.
Overall, Taiwan's performance was mixed. Among the country's previously ranked universities, 21 percent moved up in the rankings, 9 percent remained unchanged and 70 percent slipped, yielding a net ranking change of minus 49 percent, according to QS.
Taiwan performed better on that measure than Japan (-78 percent) but trailed South Korea (-21 percent), Malaysia (-10 percent) and Singapore (+20 percent), according to QS's comparison table.
By indicator, QS said Taiwan's research impact remained solid, with as many as 20 Taiwanese universities moving up in related categories.
NTU was Taiwan's top performer in the academic reputation and employer reputation categories, ranking ninth and 19th in Asia, respectively. Most Taiwanese institutions, however, slipped in Asia in both categories.
Internationalization remained Taiwan's biggest weakness, QS said.
Although the number of international students reached a record 140,420 in the 2025-26 academic year, most Taiwanese universities fell in the rankings for international faculty and international student ratios as regional competitors improved more quickly.
QS Senior Vice President Ben Sowter said Taiwan's leading universities continued to perform strongly, and had deepening ties with the country's advanced technology industries.
He said NTU remained among Asia's most respected universities, while NCKU, National Tsing Hua University and National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University all advanced in the rankings.
On Taiwan's weakness on international students and faculty, however, Sowter said Taiwan's schools will need to increasingly rely on overseas talent as the domestic college-age population continues to shrink.
The University of Hong Kong retained the top spot in the rankings, followed by Peking University and Tsinghua University in Beijing.
