summary: 民主党横扫参众两院，特朗普沦为“跛脚鸭”？图像来源: Mandel Ngan/AFP 德国之声：中国对美国中期选举结果反应谨慎。外交部发言人毛宁在例行记者会上被问及对美国中期选举的看法时表示，中期选举是美国内政。中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好落实好两国元首重要共识。您怎么看这样的表态？ 费多丽教授：首先，中国评价美国选举结果态度审慎是非常典型的做法。他们通常不会明确表达倾向，而是往往以“这是内政”作为回应。不过，“中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好落实好两国元首重要共识”这种措辞显示
content:
民主党横扫参众两院，特朗普沦为“跛脚鸭”？图像来源: Mandel Ngan/AFP
德国之声：中国对美国中期选举结果反应谨慎。外交部发言人毛宁在例行记者会上被问及对美国中期选举的看法时表示，中期选举是美国内政。中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好落实好两国元首重要共识。您怎么看这样的表态？
费多丽教授：首先，中国评价美国选举结果态度审慎是非常典型的做法。他们通常不会明确表达倾向，而是往往以“这是内政”作为回应。不过，“中方愿继续同美方一道，维护好落实好两国元首重要共识”这种措辞显示，中方预料到，外界可能会认为中国对选举结果会不那么满意，因为他们刚刚才和特朗普达成了安排。换句话说，他们认为民主党人，或者很多人认为民主党人，现在会采取更进一步的行动。因此中方强调，“我们仍然愿意合作。”
德国之声：中国看来有些担心中期选举的这一结果可能会对中美关系产生一些影响。那么您认为影响会有多大？
费多丽教授：根据近年来的经验，中国政府担心民主党人对华的态度会比特朗普更具批判性。特朗普被指折服于习近平的领导才能，在这一层面上建立了不一样的关系，因此在处理对华关系方面对抗性有所降低。但必须指出的是，美国在特朗普执政期间也对中国实施了制裁措施。虽然他们今年还没有向台湾交付武器，但也并没有真正对中国采取友好，或者和解的态度。情况非常复杂。可以说，过去这些年，无论谁入主白宫，在对华问题上都相对一致。拜登并没有完全推翻特朗普第一任期对华政策，特朗普也没有推翻拜登的做法。当然，他们的优先事项不同，处理方式也截然不同。但从根本上讲，共和党人和民主党人都认为中国是主要挑战，需要采取战略性应对措施。
德国之声：具体而言，中期选举后，美国在外交、贸易和关税政策上可能有不同的做法吗？
费多丽教授：就外交政策，包括贸易政策和关税政策而言，现任总统很明显不怎么遵循国会的建议。因此，我们不知道，民主党主导国会后，是否真的有能力通过国会正常的、合法的、既定的程序来阻止特朗普在这些领域采取独立行动。或许可以提起诉讼，但这需要时间。所以，目前情况很复杂。这不仅关系对华政策。
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
观察人士认为，民主党可能会试图对白宫施加更大的压力。但实际上——正如有人所说——特朗普现在这个所谓的“跛脚鸭”，在接下来的两年内，也可能变成一只愤怒的鸭子，想要强行推进某些事情。因此，我们对接下来会怎样其实一无所知。我们可以看看月底的APEC峰会上发生什么。我相信习近平和特朗普的会晤仍将按计划举行。或许我们能从中窥见事态的发展方向。我认为我们不会立即看到巨大的变化，短期内美国的对华政策不会有大的变化。
费多丽教授：我不是台湾问题专家，但如果我理解没错的话，在特朗普执政期间，原计划今年运往台湾的武器已被暂停。理论上讲，可以想象民主党人会更加努力地推动对这批武器的交付。但努力归努力，最终是否能促成此事就完全是另一回事了。
德国之声：您能简单总结一下特朗普执政两年来，中美的地位和力量对比发生什么变化吗？
费多丽教授：中国的确也受了特朗普政府制裁的打击，但我认为，目前最关键的是，世界其他地区，尤其是全球南方国家，认为特朗普政府在各种领域的政策都难以预测，很难知道特朗普政府下一步会做什么，想要什么，以及它的声明有多可靠。这包括贸易战，但也延伸到伊朗战争和类似问题。特朗普政府的这种等级森严且难以预测性，导致了中国形象和实力的普遍提升。但与此同时，也有另外一种趋势。在欧洲，我们也感受到了在美国蔓延的对中国的恐惧。这种恐惧正在欧洲日益扩散。
不过，如果我们暂时忽略这些因素，只关注特朗普及其政府在国际政治中的行为，那么中国无疑已经从中受益，中国在世界上的地位似乎得到了加强。
至于特朗普对中国的经济政策，中国现任领导层可以把功劳归于自己，说我们对特朗普的反应是正确的，我们挺身对抗他，展现了实力，事实证明这很有效，正因为如此，特朗普现在才相对放过了我们。有些人从心理层面分析，认为特朗普确实喜欢强人，所以他才会在某种程度上欣赏中国。不过，涉及实际的贸易冲突、安全冲突、信息和虚假信息问题等等，中国也并非完全占据上风。大家都在摸索，试图找到解决这些冲突的方法。
此外，中国经济目前面临着诸多问题，包括一些需求方面的问题。近期股市的疲软也被解读为对人工智能能力缺乏信心。中国经济目前似乎正处于低迷状态，但这种情况我们现在在美国也看到了。但这些问题并非主要由中美双边关系决定，中国目前面临的困境也并非出口市场之类的问题，而是与中国的经济政策、政策的实施方式以及优先事项的设定密切相关。
德国维尔茨堡大学费多丽教授（Dr. Doris Fischer）图像来源: Uni Würzburg
德国之声：美国对中国商品，比如电动汽车等商品进口有很多限制，这样的趋势还会继续吗？
费多丽教授：我不认为国会会向白宫施压，要求对中国实施更多贸易限制，至少不会以太多商品从中国流入美国为由。如果真有什么动向，那也只会是出于安全方面的考虑。但我认为他们不会把这作为首要任务。民主党首先需要理顺内部事务，弄清楚如何应对这种新局面，如何稳定现在这股浪潮，从而在两年后再次赢得总统大选。而且国会现在是否真的拥有影响力并能带来巨大变革，比如在关税政策方面，我对此表示怀疑。如果主要目的是抑制通货膨胀，他们也许会说，或许我们应该降低关税。但通货膨胀当然也很大程度上受能源价格的影响，而关税对能源价格没有影响。所以情况很复杂。我预计民主党人需要一些时间来站稳脚跟，适应他们的新角色。

网络新闻平台China Table认为，美国中期选举后，特朗普现有的对华政策将面临严峻考验。《南德意志报》则关注了中国一场关于跨国婚恋与爱国主义的讨论。
美国总统特朗普周四以极尽排场的礼宾规格在白宫欢迎中国国家主席习近平来访。盛大的欢迎仪式、近三小时小范围会谈以及科技巨头加持的豪华晚宴，无一不显现出特朗普对此次访问的重视。美中关系正如特朗普所说“从未像现在这样好”？
全球瞩目的特朗普习近平会谈，在周五晚落下帷幕。两国元首在贸易、AI安全等关键议题上显然没有取得重大突破，在伊朗等棘手议题上也只是匆匆聊过。不过，两人约定会在今年内再会晤两次。
周一，中共为前总书记江泽民举行百岁冥诞纪念大会。周二，前总理朱镕基的遗体在八宝山公墓火化，天安门等地降半旗致哀。江泽民与朱镕基留给习近平怎样的遗产？习近平能否借助已经逝去的时代安抚当下的民心，进一步巩固自己的权力？
北京香山论坛多国代表对军用人工智能的潜在风险深表担忧。在美中两国准备举行高层会晤之际，武器自主化正急剧压缩决策时间，大国在此类技术管控上的分歧再度引发广泛讨论。
在欧盟释放信号，表示愿意让加拿大以“准成员”身份成为其特殊伙伴后，美国总统特朗普对此发出嘲讽，并表示，这一设想属于“敌对行为”。
911恐袭事件迎来25周年纪念。纽约世贸中心大厦轰然倒塌的影像，是历史的见证，记录了当时惊心动魄的时刻。
特朗普宣布与委内瑞拉达成的石油协议，其合法性和透明度引发专家质疑。与此同时，委内瑞拉国内也传来批评声。
路透社独家援引美军武库知情人士报道说，美国在新近的中东伊朗冲突中，已消耗大部分高精度远程导弹库存。该消息引发了外界对美军应对未来冲突准备状态的担忧。特朗普对此类表述表达“很生气”，并威胁“严惩传播这些言论的叛徒”。

The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that Hangzhou Ailong Metal Products Co., Ltd. (Ailong) failed to establish its eligibility for a separate rate and, therefore, is part of the China-wide entity. The period of review (POR) is August 1, 2024, through July 31, 2025. In addition, we are rescinding the review with respect to 39 companies. Interested parties are invited to comment on these preliminary results of review.
Applicable November 4, 2026.
Krisha Hill, AD/CVD Operations, Office IV, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-4037.
On September 25, 2025, based on timely requests for review, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.221(c)(1)(i), we initiated an administrative review of the antidumping duty Order on light-walled rectangular pipe and tube (LWR pipe) from the People's Republic of China (China), including Ailong.[1]
On December 17, 2025, we released U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) information for comment.[2] We received no comments on the CBP Data Release. On June 16, 2026, we issued an intent to rescind, in part, memorandum.[3] We received no comments on Intent to Rescind, in Part.
Due to the lapse in appropriations and Federal Government shutdown, on November 14, 2025, Commerce tolled all deadlines in administrative proceedings by 47 days.[4] Additionally, due to a backlog of documents that were electronically filed via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS) during the Federal Government shutdown, on November 24, 2025, Commerce tolled all deadlines in administrative proceedings by an additional 21 days.[5] On June 24, 2026, we extended the preliminary results of this review to no later than November 2, 2026.[6]
The merchandise subject to this Order is certain welded carbon quality light-walled steel pipe and tube, of rectangular (including square) cross section, having a wall thickness of less than 4 mm.
The term carbon-quality steel includes both carbon steel and alloy steel which contains only small amounts of alloying elements. Specifically, the term carbon-quality includes products in which none of the elements listed below exceeds the quantity by weight respectively indicated: 1.80 percent of manganese, or ( printed page 69548) 2.25 percent of silicon, or 1.00 percent of copper, or 0.50 percent of aluminum, or 1.25 percent of chromium, or 0.30 percent of cobalt, or 0.40 percent of lead, or 1.25 percent of nickel, or 0.30 percent of tungsten, or 0.10 percent of molybdenum, or 0.10 percent of niobium, or 0.15 percent vanadium, or 0.15 percent of zirconium. The description of carbon-quality is intended to identify carbon-quality products within the scope. The welded carbon-quality rectangular pipe and tube subject to this Order is currently classified under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) subheadings 7306.61.50.00 and 7306.61.70.60. While HTSUS subheadings are provided for convenience and CBP's customs purposes, our written description of the scope of the Order is dispositive.
Rescission of Administrative Review, in Part
Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.213(d)(3), it is Commerce's practice to rescind an administrative review of an antidumping duty order where it concludes that there were no suspended entries of subject merchandise during the POR.[7] Normally, upon completion of an administrative review, the suspended entries are liquidated at the antidumping duty assessment rate for the review period.[8] Therefore, for an administrative review to be conducted, there must be a reviewable, suspended entry that Commerce can instruct CBP to liquidate at the calculated antidumping duty assessment rate for the review period.[9] Commerce notified all interested parties of its intent to rescind the instant review regarding the companies listed in the Appendix because there were no reviewable, suspended entries of subject merchandise from these companies during the POR and invited interested parties to comment.[10] No parties commented on Commerce's intent to rescind this review with respect to these companies. In the absence of any suspended entries of subject merchandise from these companies during the POR, we are rescinding this administrative review for the companies listed in the Appendix, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.213(d)(3).
Commerce is conducting this administrative review in accordance with section 751(a)(1)(B) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), and 19 CFR 351.213.
Commerce's policy regarding conditional review of the China-wide entity applies to this administrative review.[11] Under this policy, the China-wide entity will not be under review unless a party specifically requests, or Commerce self-initiates, a review of the entity. Because no party requested a review of the China-wide entity, the entity is not under review, and the entity's rate ( i.e., 255.07 percent) [12] is not subject to change.
The deadline for Ailong to submit a separate rate application (SRA) or separate rate certification (SRC) was October 9, 2025, and the deadline to submit a no-shipment certification was October 25, 2026.[13] Ailong, did not submit an SRA or SRC. Thus, Commerce preliminarily determines that Ailong has not demonstrated its eligibility for a separate rate and, therefore, Ailong is part of the China-wide entity and subject to the China-wide rate of 255.07 percent; thus, no decision memorandum accompanies this notice.
Normally, Commerce discloses to interested parties the calculations performed in preliminary results within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the date of publication of the notice of preliminary results in the Federal Register , in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b). However, because Commerce preliminarily found Ailong to be a part of the China-wide entity, in accordance with section 776 of the Act, there are no calculations to disclose.
Case briefs or other written comments may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance. Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.309(c)(1)(ii), we have modified the deadline for interested parties to submit case briefs to Commerce to no later than 21 days after the date of the publication of this notice.[14] As provided under 19 CFR 351.309(c)(2)(iii) and (d)(2)(iii), we request that interested parties provide at the beginning of their briefs a public executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs.[15] Further, we request that interested parties limit their public, executive summary of each issue to no more than 450 words, not including citations. We intend to use the public, executive summaries as the basis of the comment summaries included in the issues and decision memorandum that will accompany the final results in this administrative review. We request that interested parties include footnotes for relevant citations in the public, executive summary of each issue. Note that Commerce has amended certain of its requirements pertaining to the service of documents in 19 CFR 351.303(f).[16]
Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.310(c), interested parties who wish to request a hearing must submit a written request to ( printed page 69549) the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance, filed electronically via ACCESS by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice. Requests should contain: (1) the party's name, address, and telephone number; (2) the number of participants and whether any participant is a foreign national; and (3) a list of issues to be discussed. Oral presentations at the hearing will be limited to issues raised in the briefs. If a request for a hearing is made, Commerce will inform parties of the scheduled date for the hearing.[17]
Pursuant to section 751(a)(2)(A) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1), Commerce will determine, and CBP shall assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries of subject merchandise in accordance with the final results of this review.
Upon issuance of the final results of this review, Commerce will determine, and CBP will assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by this review.[18] We intend to instruct CBP to liquidate entries of subject merchandise exported by Ailong, if we continue to determine in the final results Ailong to be part of the China-wide entity, at the China-wide entity rate of 255.07 percent.[19]
For the companies listed in the Appendix for which the review is being rescinded, Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries. Antidumping duties shall be assessed at rates equal to the cash deposit rate for estimated antidumping duties required at the time of entry, or withdrawal from warehouse, for consumption, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(c)(1)(i). Commerce intends to issue rescission instructions for the companies listed in the Appendix to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register .
The final results of this review shall be the basis for the assessment of antidumping duties on entries of merchandise covered by the final results of this review and for future deposits of estimated duties, where applicable.
If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired ( i.e., within 90 days of publication).
The following cash deposit requirements will be effective upon publication of the final results of this administrative review for shipments of the subject merchandise from Vietnam entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the publication date, as provided by sections 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act: for Ailong, if it is found to not be eligible for a separate rate in the final results of review, then its cash deposit rate will be the rate applicable for the China-wide entity; (2) for previously investigated or reviewed Chinese and non-Chinese exporters not listed above that received a separate rate in a prior segment of this proceeding, the cash deposit rate will continue to be the existing exporter-specific rate; (3) for all Chinese exporters of subject merchandise that have not been found to be entitled to a separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the existing rate for the China-wide entity of 255.07 percent; and (4) for all non-Chinese exporters of subject merchandise which have not received their own rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate applicable to the China exporter that supplied that non-Chinese exporter. These deposit requirements, when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.
This notice also serves as a preliminary reminder to importers of their responsibility under 19 CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this review period. Failure to comply with this requirement could result in Commerce's presumption that reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties, and/or an increase in the amount of antidumping duties by the amount of the countervailing duties.
We are issuing and publishing these preliminary results of review in accordance with sections 751(a)(1) and 777(i)(1) of the Act, and 19 CFR 351.221(b)(4).
Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.

Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) finds that revocation of the antidumping duty (AD) orders on utility scale wind towers (wind towers) from India, Malaysia, and Spain would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping, at the levels indicated in the “Final Results of Sunset Reviews” section of this notice.
Applicable November 4, 2026.
Samuel Evans, AD/CVD Operations, Office IX, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: 202-482-2420.
On August 16, 2021 (for Spain), and December 6, 2021 (for India and Malaysia), Commerce published the Orders in the Federal Register .[1] On July 2, 2026, Commerce published the notice of initiation of these first sunset reviews of the Orders, pursuant to section 751(c) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act).[2]
On July 17, 2026, Commerce received timely and complete notices of intent to participate in the sunset reviews for the domestic interested party within the deadline specified in 19 CFR 351.218(d)(1)(i).[3] The domestic interested party claimed interested party status within the meaning of sections 771(9)(C) and 771(9)(F) of the Act as a U.S. manufacturer and producer of the domestic like product and as an association the majority of whose members produce the domestic like product.[4] On July 31, 2026, Commerce notified the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) that it had received notices of intent to participate from the domestic interested party.[5]
On August 3, 2026, pursuant to 19 CFR 351.218(d)(3)(i), the domestic interested party filed timely and adequate substantive responses.[6] Commerce did not receive a substantive response from any respondent interested party. On August 24, 2026, Commerce notified the ITC that it did not receive a substantive response from any respondent interested parties.[7] As a result, pursuant to section 751(c)(3)(B) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.218(e)(1)(ii)(C)(2), Commerce is conducting expedited (120-day) sunset reviews of the Orders.
The products covered by these Orders are wind towers from India, Malaysia, and Spain. For the full description of the scope of the Orders, see the Issues and Decisions Memorandum.[8]
A complete discussion of all issues raised in these sunset reviews, including the likelihood of continuation or recurrence of dumping in the event of revocation of the Orders and the magnitude of the margins likely to prevail if the Orders were to be revoked, is provided in the accompanying Issues and Decision Memorandum.[9] A list of the topics discussed in the Issues and Decision Memorandum is attached in the Appendix to this notice. The Issues and Decision Memorandum is a public document and is on file electronically via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS). ACCESS is available to registered users at https://access.trade.gov. In addition, a complete version of the Issues and Decision Memorandum can be directly accessed at https://access.trade.gov/​frnotices.
Pursuant to sections 751(c)(1), 752(c)(1) and (3) of the Act, Commerce determines that revocation of the Orders would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping, and that the magnitude of the dumping margins likely to prevail would be weighted-average dumping margins up to 54.03 percent for India, 3.20 percent for Malaysia, and 73.00 percent for Spain.
Notification Regarding Administrative Protective Orders
This notice also serves as the only reminder to parties subject to administrative protective order (APO) of their responsibility concerning the return or destruction of proprietary information disclosed under APO in accordance with 19 CFR 351.305. Timely notification of the return or destruction of APO materials, or conversion to judicial protective, orders is hereby requested. Failure to comply with the regulations and terms of an APO is a violation which is subject to sanction.
We are issuing and publishing these final results in accordance with sections 751(c), 752(c), and 777(i)(1) of the Act, and 19 CFR 351.218 and 19 CFR 351.221(c)(5)(ii).
Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.

Department of Commerce International Trade Administration
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines that certain oil country tubular goods (OCTG) from Taiwan are being, or are likely to be, sold in the United States at less than fair value (LTFV). The period of investigation (POI) is April 1, 2025, through March 31, 2026. Interested parties are invited to comment on this preliminary determination.
Applicable November 4, 2026.
Monica Gillis or Braeden Lowe, AD/CVD Operations, Office V, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-6384 or (202) 482-9124, respectively.
This preliminary determination is made in accordance with section 733(b) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act). Commerce published the notice of initiation of this investigation on April 28, 2026.[1] On August 28, 2026, Commerce postponed the preliminary determination of this investigation and the revised deadline is now October 29, 2026.[2]
For a complete description of the events that followed the initiation of this investigation, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.[3] A list of topics included in the Preliminary Decision Memorandum is included as Appendix II to this notice. The Preliminary Decision Memorandum is a public document and is on file electronically via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS), which is available to registered users at https://access.trade.gov. In addition, a complete version of the Preliminary Decision Memorandum can be accessed directly at https://access.trade.gov/​frnotices.
The product covered by this investigation is OCTG from Taiwan. For a complete description of the scope of this investigation, see Appendix I.
In accordance with the Preamble to Commerce's regulations,[4] the Initiation Notice set aside a period of time for parties to raise issues regarding product coverage ( i.e., scope).[5] Certain interested parties commented on the scope of the investigation as it appeared in the Initiation Notice, whereby they requested that Commerce find certain mechanical pipe products to be outside the scope of this investigation. These products include: mechanical pipe for oilfield tools, mechanical pipe for perforating guns, and expandable mechanical pipe.
We note that there is an ongoing scope inquiry related to the antidumping duty orders on OCTG from Argentina and Mexico with respect to these same mechanical pipe products.[6] In that inquiry, Commerce preliminarily found that the products were outside the scope of the orders,[7] based on comments identical to the scope comments received in this investigation. Consistent with that finding, Commerce preliminarily finds and clarifies that mechanical pipe for oilfield tools, mechanical pipe for perforating guns, and expandable mechanical pipe are outside the scope of this investigation. Because this is a clarification, Commerce is not preliminarily modifying the scope language as it appeared in the Initiation Notice. See the scope in Appendix I to this notice.
The final determination in the above-referenced scope inquiry is currently scheduled to be made no later than December 22, 2026.[8] We intend to consider that final determination when making a final scope ruling in this investigation. Case briefs or other written comments regarding the scope of this investigation may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance no later than 30 days after the preliminary determination of this investigation. Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs regarding the scope of this investigation, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing of the scope-related case briefs.[9] Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.310(c), interested parties who wish to request a hearing regarding the scope of this investigation, limited to issues raised in the scope case and rebuttal briefs, may do so in accordance with the instructions detailed below within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice.
Commerce is conducting this investigation in accordance with section 731 of the Act. Commerce has calculated export prices in accordance with section 772(a) of the Act. Normal ( printed page 69533) value is calculated in accordance with section 773 of the Act. For a full description of the methodology underlying the preliminary determination, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum.
Sections 733(d)(1)(ii) and 735(c)(5)(A) of the Act provide that, in the preliminary determination, Commerce shall determine an estimated weighted-average dumping margin, i.e., the all-others rate, for all exporters and producers not individually examined. This rate shall be an amount equal to the weighted average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins established for exporters and producers individually investigated, excluding any zero and de minimis margins, and any margins determined entirely under section 776 of the Act.
In this investigation, Commerce calculated estimated weighted-average dumping margins for Shin Yang Steel Co. Ltd. and Tension Steel Industries Co., Ltd. (collectively, the respondents) that are not zero, de minimis, or based entirely on facts otherwise available. Commerce calculated the all-others rate using a weighted average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the respondents using each company's publicly-ranged values for the merchandise under consideration.[10]
Commerce preliminarily determines that the following estimated weighted-average dumping margins exist:
Exporter/producer Estimated weighted-average dumping margin (percent) Shin Yang Steel Co. Ltd 51.19 Tension Steel Industries Co., Ltd 54.74 All Others 52.43
In accordance with section 733(d)(2) of the Act, Commerce will direct U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to suspend liquidation of entries of OCTG, as described in Appendix I, entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register . Further, pursuant to section 733(d)(1)(B) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.205(d), Commerce will instruct CBP to require a cash deposit equal to the estimated weighted-average dumping margin or the estimated all-others rate, as follows: (1) the cash deposit rate for the respondents listed above will be equal to the company-specific estimated weighted-average dumping margins determined in this preliminary determination; (2) if the exporter is not a respondent identified above, but the producer is, then the cash deposit rate will be equal to the company-specific estimated weighted-average dumping margin established for that producer of the subject merchandise; and (3) the cash deposit rate for all other producers and exporters will be equal to the all-others estimated weighted-average dumping margin. These suspension of liquidation instructions will remain in effect until further notice.
Commerce intends to disclose its calculations and analysis performed to interested parties for this preliminary determination within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the date of publication of this notice in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b).
Consistent with 19 CFR 351.224(e), Commerce will analyze and, if appropriate, correct any timely allegations of significant ministerial errors by amending the preliminary determination. However, consistent with 19 CFR 351.224(d), Commerce will not consider incomplete allegations that do not address the significance standard under 19 CFR 351.224(g) following the preliminary determination. Instead, Commerce will address such allegations in the final determination together with issues raised in the case briefs or other written comments.
As provided in section 782(i)(1) of the Act, Commerce intends to verify the information relied upon in making its final determination.
Case briefs or other written comments, unrelated to scope, may be submitted to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance no later than seven days after the date on which the last verification report is issued in this investigation. A timeline for the submission of case briefs and written comments will be notified to interested parties at a later date. Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing case briefs.[11] Interested parties who submit case briefs or rebuttal briefs in this proceeding must submit: (1) a table of contents listing each issue; and (2) a table of authorities.[12]
As provided under 19 CFR 351.309(c)(2)(iii) and (d)(2)(iii), we request that interested parties provide at the beginning of their briefs a public, executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs.[13] Further, we request that interested parties limit their executive summary of each issue to no more than 450 words, not including citations. We intend to use the executive summaries as the basis of the comment summaries included in the issues and decision memorandum that will accompany the final determination in this investigation. We request that interested parties include footnotes for relevant citations in the executive summary of each issue. Note that Commerce has amended certain of its requirements pertaining to the service of documents in 19 CFR 351.303(f).[14]
Pursuant to 19 CFR 351.310(c), interested parties who wish to request a hearing, limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal briefs, must submit a written request to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance, U.S. Department of Commerce, within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice. Requests should contain: (1) the party's name, address, and telephone number; (2) the number of participants, and whether any participant is a foreign national; and (3) a list of the issues to be discussed. If a request for a hearing is made, ( printed page 69534) Commerce intends to hold the hearing at a time and date to be determined. Parties should confirm by telephone the date, time, and location of the hearing two days before the scheduled date.
Postponement of Final Determination and Extension of Provisional Measures
Section 735(a)(2) of the Act provides that a final determination may be postponed until not later than 135 days after the date of the publication of the preliminary determination if, in the event of an affirmative preliminary determination, a request for such postponement is made by exporters who account for a significant proportion of exports of the subject merchandise, or in the event of a negative preliminary determination, a request for such postponement is made by the petitioner. Section 351.210(e)(2) of Commerce's regulations requires that a request by exporters for postponement of the final determination be accompanied by a request for extension of provisional measures from a four-month period to a period not more than six months in duration.
On September 8, 2026, pursuant to 19 CFR 351.210(e), the respondents requested that Commerce postpone the final determination and that provisional measures be extended to a period not to exceed six months.[15] In accordance with section 735(a)(2)(A) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.210(b)(2)(ii), because: (1) the preliminary determination is affirmative; (2) the requesting exporters account for a significant proportion of exports of the subject merchandise; and (3) no compelling reasons for denial exist, Commerce is postponing the final determination and extending the provisional measures from a four-month period to a period not greater than six months. Accordingly, Commerce will make its final determination no later than 135 days after the date of publication of this preliminary determination.
U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) Notification
In accordance with section 733(f) of the Act, Commerce will notify the ITC of its preliminary determination. If the final determination is affirmative, the ITC will determine before the later of 120 days after the date of this preliminary determination or 45 days after the final determination whether these imports are materially injuring, or threaten material injury to, the U.S. industry.
This determination is issued and published in accordance with sections 733(f) and 777(i)(1) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.205(c).
Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.
The merchandise covered by this investigation is certain oil country tubular goods (OCTG), which are hollow steel products of circular cross-section, including oil well casing and tubing, of iron (other than cast iron) or steel (both carbon and alloy), whether seamless or welded, regardless of end finish ( e.g., whether or not plain end, threaded, or threaded and coupled) whether or not conforming to American Petroleum Institute (API) or non-API specifications, whether finished (including limited service OCTG products) or unfinished (including green tubes and limited service OCTG products), whether or not thread protectors are attached. The scope of this investigation also covers OCTG coupling stock.
Subject merchandise includes material matching the above description that has been finished, packaged, or otherwise processed in a third country, including by performing any heat treatment, cutting, upsetting, threading, coupling, or any other finishing, packaging, or processing that would not otherwise remove the merchandise from the scope of this investigation if performed in the country of manufacture of the OCTG.
Excluded from the scope of this investigation are: casing, tubing, or coupling stock containing 10.5 percent or more by weight of chromium; drill pipe; unattached couplings; and unattached thread protectors.

V. Discussion of the Methodology
1. See Certain Oil Country Tubular Goods from Austria, Taiwan, and the United Arab Emirates: Initiation of Less-Than-Fair-Value Investigations,91 FR 22806 (April 28, 2026) ( Initiation Notice).
2. See Oil Country Tubular Goods from Austria, Taiwan, and the United Arab Emirates: Postponement of Preliminary Determinations in the Less-Than-Fair-Value Investigations,91 FR 55517 (August 28, 2026).
3. See Memorandum, “Decision Memorandum for the Preliminary Affirmative Determination in the Less-Than-Fair-Value Investigation of Certain Oil Country Tubular Goods from Taiwan” dated concurrently with, and hereby adopted by, this notice (Preliminary Decision Memorandum).
4. See Antidumping Duties; Countervailing Duties, Final Rule,62 FR 27296, 27323 (May 19, 1997) ( Preamble).
5. See Initiation Notice,91 FR 22807.
6. See Oil Country Tubular Goods from Argentina, Mexico, and the Russian Federation: Antidumping Duty Orders and Amended Final Affirmative Antidumping Duty Determination for the Russian Federation,87 FR 70785 (November 21, 2022).

9. See 19 CFR 351.309(d); see also Administrative Protective Order, Service, and Other Procedures in Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Proceedings,88 FR 67069, 67077 (September 29, 2023) ( APO and Service Procedures).
10. With two respondents under examination, Commerce normally calculates: (A) a weighted-average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents; (B) a simple average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents; and (C) a weighted-average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins calculated for the examined respondents using each company's publicly-ranged U.S. sales values for the merchandise under consideration. Commerce then compares (B) and (C) to (A) and selects the rate closest to (A) as the most appropriate rate for all other producers and exporters. See, e.g., Ball Bearings and Parts Thereof from France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the United Kingdom: Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Reviews, Final Results of Changed-Circumstances Review, and Revocation of an Order in Part,75 FR 53661, 53662 (September 1, 2010), and accompanying Issues and Decision Memorandum at Comment1. After performing this comparison, Commerce based the all-others rate on the publicly-ranged sales data of the mandatory respondents. For a complete analysis of the data, see the All-Others Rate Calculation Memorandum.
11. See 19 CFR 351.309(d); see also APO and Service Procedures.

14. See APO and Service Procedures.

英国内政部长马哈茂德（Shabana Mahmood）星期一（11月2日）在国会就全面改革移民规则发表声明。 （法新社）
英国收紧移民政策，在英国国民（海外）（简称BNO）签证计划下移居当地的香港人，虽然仍可像从前那样在移英五年后申请永久居留，但日后须面对更高的英文门槛和更严格的刑事纪录审查，许多移英港人因此批评英国政府改变对港人的承诺。
近年英国国内的反移民思潮升温，为了平息民众对移民政策的不满，英国内政部长马哈茂德（Shabana Mahmood）星期一（11月2日）公布全面改革移民规则的方案。
根据新的规定，大部分移民取得英国永久居留资格所需的基本居住年期，将从五年延长至10年。新措施有追溯力，目前已经在英国的移民也会受到影响。
在新规下，持有BNO签证的港人，仍可在移英五年后申请永居。不过，马哈茂德在国会应询时透露，BNO港人日后在申请永居时，须达到更高的B2英文水平要求，并面对更严格的刑事纪录审查。但截至星期二（3日），英国政府官网的BNO移民规则仍列明，申请永居者只须达到较低的B1英文水平。
英国内政部星期二两度回复海外港人网媒“绿豆”询问时证实，英国政府对香港BNO签证持有人的承诺维持不变，只要符合要求仍可在移英五年后申请永居，但在新制度下，申请者须符合普遍适用于永居申请的新要求，包括新的刑事纪录规定及B2英语水平要求，除非已获豁免或有保障安排。
上述豁免或保障安排，是指在英语要求方面，目前对儿童、65岁或以上人士，以及因身体或精神状况无法达到要求的人士，将继续获得豁免。
英国内政部也说，在刑事纪录方面，当局也会保留酌情权，考虑不同司法制度之间的差异，包括某些行为在海外被列为刑事罪行，但在英国并不构成犯罪的情况。
近年通过BNO签证计划移英的香港人大约有17万人。英国政府公布新要求后，部分原本已在准备B1考试的移英港人都担心受到影响，在网上批评当局改变对港人的承诺，促请当局尽快澄清新规及作出过渡安排。
关注香港人权的组织“香港监察”发表声明，对英国政府提高BNO永居门槛表示失望，担心政策变动影响已按原有制度规划生活的港人家庭。
除了英文门槛，新的刑事纪录审查也引起关注。由前香港葵青区议员郭子健发起的社区组织Dandelion Solidarity CIC星期一致函马哈茂德，关注新规可能影响因参与香港政治活动而被定罪的港人。郭子健担心，若英国政府未能区分政治性定罪与一般刑事犯罪，部分曾遭政治迫害的港人恐因此失去定居机会。
香港公共管治学会理事长陈财喜博士接受《联合早报》访问时说，近年英国经济欠佳，许多人将问题归咎于移民，英国政府因此大幅提高移民要求。“虽然香港的情况比较特殊，英国政府自认对香港人有道义责任，但在国内强烈的反移民氛围下，也要稍微提高港人移居英国的门槛，包括英文水平。”
他认为，澳大利亚、加拿大等西方国家过去几年都收紧移民要求，不排除英国日后还会提高香港移民的申请门槛。“各国都只想争取高质素人才或者有钱的人，除非是投资移民或者通过专才计划，否则移民西方国家的难度将会更大。”

content:
美国总统特朗普（左）与中国国家主席习近平9月24日在美国白宫会面。 （路透社）
美国共和党在中期选举中惨败，民主党赢得国会两院多数席位。受访美国学者认为，特朗普对华政策将受到更大政治制约，白宫与国会在台湾、科技和经济安全议题上的分歧可能加深，让中美“建设性战略稳定关系”面临考验；深圳APEC峰会将成为观察中美关系走向的重要窗口。
中国学者则认为，美国选民更关注生活成本和物价上涨，中国并非此次选举的核心议题。民主党胜选虽对特朗普构成政治打击，但不会实质改变中美关系基本走向。
美国中期选举也引发中国舆论关注。“特朗普说中期选举未打击到他”等话题星期三（11月4日）一度登上微博热搜。上证综指当天也上涨2.2%，创七个月来最大单日涨幅。路透社报道分析，除了中国政府出台的支持措施提振市场，民主党胜选的消息也成为中国投资者逢低买入的催化剂。
中国外交部发言人毛宁星期三在例行记者会上没有直接评论选举对中美关系的影响，只强调中方愿与美方落实两国元首重要共识，加强沟通，妥处分歧，拓展合作，构建中美建设性战略稳定关系。
美国昆西研究所高级研究员西蒙（Denis Simon）向《联合早报》分析，民主党掌控国会“不会必然终结中美建设性战略稳定关系”，但会使这一目标“更难实现和维持”。特朗普希望保留对华外交灵活，国会则可能加强制度约束，防止美国对中国作出过多让步。特朗普或许有空间与习近平谈判，却未必能保证华盛顿落实每一项协议。
西蒙认为，分歧在对台军售和科技政策上尤其明显。特朗普今年5月与习近平会晤后，暂缓总额约140亿美元（179亿新元）的对台军售案。民主党可能通过加强国会审查、要求行政部门解释延迟原因及推动立法，增加特朗普拖延军售的政治成本。不过，军售启动和批准仍主要由行政部门掌握，国会则拥有获得通知、审查军售和立法的权利。
科技方面，民主党可能收紧半导体出口许可，加强对先进人工智能晶片和计算设备的审查，并限制敏感技术转移及中国对美国战略产业的投资。不过，民主党内部并非意见一致，部分议员也关注美国企业的经济成本及过度与中国脱钩的后果。
APEC领导人非正式会议将于11月18日至19日在中国深圳举行。西蒙认为，特朗普可能寻求中国增加采购美国农产品和能源、扩大美国企业在华市场准入，并在关键矿产和供应链稳定方面取得成果，但若美国不在关税和科技限制方面作出对等承诺，北京将不愿作出重大让步。
清华大学战略与安全研究中心副研究员孙成昊评估，APEC期间可能举行的中美元首会晤，将成为检验中美建设性战略稳定能否经受美国国内政治变化的“重要节点”。特朗普可能争取扩大美国对华出口、降低贸易不确定性和稳定关键矿产供应，但不代表他对华立场必然软化。
孙成昊强调，关键是元首共识能否落实，而非只在会晤当天改善气氛。双方能否延续降税、贸易投资机制和人工智能对话，也值得观察。
他认为，生活成本压力可能限制特朗普进一步加征关税，先进晶片出口限制则更可能获得两党支持。特朗普还可能赶在美国新一届国会明年1月3日开议前，于今年底推进经贸安排，也可能在两国元首会晤后宣布军售或收紧对华限制，以回应美国国内指责他“对华让步”的批评。
南京大学中国南海研究协同创新中心执行主任朱锋和新加坡南洋理工大学公共政策与全球事务副教授骆明辉均认为，民主党赢得国会两院多数席位不会从根本上改变中美关系走向。
朱锋说，中美建设性战略稳定关系符合双方利益，民主党也清楚这一点；特朗普的交易型外交风格不会改变，中国本来也未对特朗普抱有过度期待。对北京而言，“最重要的是坚持自身发展战略，避免陷入大国竞争的恶性循环”。
骆明辉则指出，美国两党对华战略存在相当程度的共识，即使特朗普接下来两年“跛脚”，美国对华政策也不会出现重大变化；中国会继续重视元首外交，同时着眼下一届美国总统选举及更长远的中美关系。他认为，若特朗普与习近平在APEC期间会晤，将体现中美建设性战略稳定关系的延续，而非考验。

content:
调查：卤肉饭最能代表台湾美食 - 焦点台湾
调查：卤肉饭最能代表台湾美食
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月4日电 国立台湾师范大学周三发布的一项调查显示，卤肉饭是台湾最具代表性的美食。
挪威科技大学文化教育策略团队于8月13日至16日进行的这项调查发现，29.2%的受访者选择红烧肉饭，即蒸白米饭，上面撒上切碎或剁碎的五花肉。
以气味刺鼻而闻名的臭豆腐以11.8%位居第二，其次是珍珠奶茶，这是一种用茶、牛奶和木薯珍珠制成的流行饮料，占10.5%。
科技大学研究组组长钟宗贤。中央通讯社照片2026年11月4日
研究小组负责人钟宗宪在评论研究结果时表示，这三种主要选择通常不会出现在正式宴会上，这表明台湾人喜欢吃什么反映了他们的日常饮食习惯。
调查显示，台湾东部30-34岁的客家男性以卤肉饭为主，而北部桃园、新竹、苗栗等县市25-29岁的原住民女性则偏爱臭豆腐。
其他选择包括台湾炸鸡（8.4％）、蚵仔煎（6.9％）、牛肉面（2.8％）、饭团和刈包（同一类别的饭团和刈包）2.4％、粽子（1.7％）、炒菜（1.7％） % 和卤味 1.5%。
钟先生表示，令他感到惊讶的是，被广泛认为是台湾人最喜爱的食物的牛肉面仅排名第六，只有2.8%的受访者选择它作为最能代表台湾美食的菜肴。
他说，调查结果反映了台湾人饮食偏好的多样性。
该调查还询问了受访者对外国美食的偏好。
日本料理排名第一，有 44.1% 的受访者选择日本料理，其次是泰国菜（13.1%）和西餐（11.8%）。
钟说，移民影响了台湾人的饮食。调查发现，6%的受访者更喜欢越南菜。
大约一半的受访者表示，他们选择去哪里吃饭没有固定的计划，并且优先考虑口味而不是价格。
研究小组表示，调查结果表明，台湾的饮食文化越来越强调用餐体验，而不仅仅是满足饥饿。
该调查共收集了1,073份台湾消费者的有效回复。它的置信度为 95%，误差范围为正负 2.99 个百分点。

Braised pork rice best represents Taiwan's cuisine: Survey
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 4 (CNA) Braised pork rice, or "lu rou fan" (滷肉飯), is the food most representative of Taiwan's cuisine, according to a survey released Wednesday by National Taiwan Normal University (NTNU).
The survey, conducted Aug. 13-16 by NTNU's cultural education strategy team, found that 29.2 percent of respondents chose braised pork rice, which consists of steamed white rice topped with finely chopped or minced pork belly.
Stinky tofu (臭豆腐), known for its pungent smell, ranked second with 11.8 percent, followed by bubble tea (珍珠奶茶), a popular drink made with tea, milk and tapioca pearls, at 10.5 percent.
NTNU research team leader Chung Tsung-hsien. CNA photo Nov. 4, 2026
Commenting on the findings, research team leader Chung Tsung-hsien (鍾宗憲) said the three leading choices were not typically served at formal banquets, suggesting that what Taiwanese people like to eat reflected their everyday eating habits.
According to the survey, Hakka men ages 30-34 in eastern Taiwan predominantly chose braised pork rice, while Indigenous women ages 25-29 in the northern counties and cities of Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli tended to favor stinky tofu.
Other choices included Taiwanese fried chicken (鹹酥雞 and 雞排) at 8.4 percent, oyster omelets (蚵仔煎) at 6.9 percent, beef noodles (牛肉麵) at 2.8 percent, rice balls and gua bao (飯糰 and 刈包, listed in the same category) at 2.4 percent, rice dumplings (粽子), at 1.7 percent, stir-fried dishes (熱炒) at 1.7 percent and braised dishes (滷味) at 1.5 percent.
Chung said he was surprised that beef noodles, widely considered a favorite food in Taiwan, ranked only sixth, with 2.8 percent of respondents choosing it as the dish that best represents Taiwanese cuisine.
He said the findings reflected the diversity of Taiwanese people's dietary preferences.
The survey also asked respondents about their preferences for foreign cuisines.
Japanese cuisine ranked first, with 44.1 percent of respondents selecting it, followed by Thai cuisine at 13.1 percent and Western food at 11.8 percent.
Chung said immigration had influenced what people eat in Taiwan. The survey found that 6 percent of respondents preferred Vietnamese food.
About half of respondents said they chose where to eat without a fixed plan and prioritized taste over price.
The findings suggested that Taiwan's food culture had increasingly emphasized the dining experience rather than just satisfying hunger, according to the research team.
The survey collected 1,073 valid responses from Taiwanese consumers. It has a 95 percent confidence level and a margin of error of plus or minus 2.99 percentage points.

前中央电视台主持人在台寻求庇护被驱逐至泰国 - 聚焦台湾
前中央电视台主持人在台湾寻求庇护被驱逐到泰国
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新网台北11月4日电 入出国及移民署表示，周一从泰国搭乘转机抵达桃园国际机场并在台湾寻求庇护的中国公民程万军于周三凌晨被驱逐回泰国。
在社交媒体平台 X（以前称为 Twitter）上流传的一段视频中，程自称是中国中央电视台（CCTV）前主持人，并表示他正在台湾寻求临时人道主义保护。
程说，他在2019年因批评“失去国家的统治者”而被记录并向当局举报后被判处六年监禁。他说，出狱后，他被迫流亡国外，以便出版他在狱中写的作品。
程还声称，联合国难民事务高级专员办事处（难民署）驻泰国办事处将他的案件列为最高风险级别，但无法保证他在那里的安全。他说，他因此前往台湾，以避免受到中国当局的进一步迫害。
据消息人士透露，郑周一搭乘转机航班抵达台北，但没有登机。相反，他将视频发布到网上寻求帮助。国家移民管理局随后安排他住在指定区域，并为他提供膳食和休息场所，但不允许他自由活动。
国家移民局在周三的一份声明中表示，已咨询包括大陆委员会在内的相关机构，并确定郑没有资格在台湾寻求庇护，因为他缺乏有效的入境文件，也没有提供具体证据来证实他的说法。该机构表示，因此根据《移民法》，他被驱逐到泰国。
然而，程某拒绝登机时受伤，促使当局依法采取措施确保飞行安全。

Former CCTV host seeking asylum in Taiwan deported to Thailand

Taipei, Nov. 4 (CNA) Chinese national Cheng Wanjun (程萬軍), who remained at Taoyuan International Airport after arriving on a connecting flight from Thailand on Monday and sought asylum in Taiwan, was deported to Thailand early Wednesday, the National Immigration Agency (NIA) said.
In a video circulating on social media platform X, formerly Twitter, Cheng identified himself as a former host at China Central Television (CCTV) and said he was seeking temporary humanitarian protection in Taiwan.
Cheng said he was sentenced to six years in prison after he was recorded and reported to authorities in 2019 for criticizing "a ruler who loses his country." After his release, he said, he was forced to go into exile abroad in order to publish writings he had produced while in prison.
Cheng also claimed that the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Thailand had classified his case as being at the highest risk level but could not guarantee his safety there. He said he therefore traveled to Taiwan to avoid further persecution by the Chinese authorities.
According to sources, Cheng arrived in Taipei on Monday on a connecting flight to Beijing but did not board his onward flight. Instead, he posted the video online appealing for assistance. The NIA subsequently arranged for him to stay in a designated area, where he was provided with meals and a place to rest but was not allowed to move about freely.
In a statement Wednesday, the NIA said it had consulted relevant agencies, including the Mainland Affairs Council, and determined that Cheng was not eligible to seek asylum in Taiwan because he lacked valid entry documents and had not provided concrete evidence to substantiate his claims. He was therefore deported to Thailand under the Immigration Act, the agency said.
However, Cheng sustained injuries when he resisted boarding the aircraft, prompting authorities to take measures to ensure flight safety in accordance with the law, the NIA added.

# 独家报道：众议院中国委员会敦促空军削减智库开支

根据一封写给空军部长特洛伊·梅克的信，中国航天研究院（CASI）“资源不足”“可能会削弱军事领导人和文职决策者理解”北京航空航天战略和军事实力的能力。

 2025 年 4 月 21 日，在马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地举行的“了解中国航空航天”活动中，中国航天研究院的扑克牌放在桌子上。（美国空军照片/高级飞行员 Gianluca Ciccopiedi）

华盛顿——众议院中国问题特别委员会(https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/)的议员们正在敦促空军就其以北京为中心的智囊团计划缩减规模的问题寻求答案，并警告说，该组织产出的任何减少都可能影响美国的国家安全。

根据《Breaking Defense》独家看到的信函副本，中国航天研究院（CASI）的使命“资源不足”，“可能会损害军事领导人和文职决策者理解”北京航空航天战略和军事实力的能力。

这封信是写给空军部长特洛伊·梅克（Troy Meink）的，由共和党主席约翰·穆勒纳尔（John Moolenaar）和民主党资深议员罗·卡纳（Ro Khanna）签署，信中要求在 11 月 20 日之前进行简报，以便为 CASI 提供“资源和人事决定”。
众议院议员在信中表示，由于中国不断发展的航空航天能力和“在印太地区的侵略活动”，CASI 技能的“任何潜在损失”都“尤其令人担忧”。立法者赞扬 CASI 的工作，表示该研究所“内部专业知识”的替代方案可能需要空军和其他政府实体“花费大量资源从外部供应商购买合同专业知识”。

鉴于中国人民解放军空天力量的快速发展，立法者表示，相关分析的减少“尤其令人担忧”。

# EXCLUSIVE: House China committee pushes Air Force on think tank cuts

“Under-resourcing” the China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI) “could risk undermining the ability of military leaders and civilian policymakers to understand” Beijing’s aerospace strategy and military prowess, according to a letter addressed to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink.

By [Michael Marrow](https://breakingdefense.com/author/mmarrow/) on November 04, 2026 11:28 am

 China Aerospace Studies Institute playing cards rest on a table during the Understanding China’s Aerospace event at Joint Base Andrews, Md., April 21, 2025. (U.S. Air Force photo/Senior Airman Gianluca Ciccopiedi)

WASHINGTON — Lawmakers on the [House Select Committee on China](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/) are pushing the Air Force for answers about a planned downsizing of its Beijing-focused think tank, warning that any reduction in the group’s output could impact America’s national security.

“Under-resourcing” the mission of the China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI) “could risk undermining the ability of military leaders and civilian policymakers to understand” Beijing’s aerospace strategy and military prowess, according to a copy of the letter viewed exclusively by Breaking Defense.

Addressed to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink and signed by Republican Chairman John Moolenaar and Democratic Ranking Member Ro Khanna, the letter requests a briefing by Nov. 20 to provide “resourcing and personnel decisions” for CASI.

In their letter, House lawmakers say that “[a]ny potential loss” of CASI’s skills “is particularly worrisome” due to China’s burgeoning aerospace capabilities and “aggressive activities in the Indo-Pacific region.” Praising CASI’s work, the lawmakers say that alternatives to the institute’s “in-house expertise” would likely require the Air Force and other government entities “to expend considerable resources to purchase contracted expertise from external vendors.”

Given rapidly advancing air and space power by the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA), the lawmakers say that diminishing relevant analysis is “particularly concerning” and could impact American deterrence, as fears mount over a potential battle for Taiwan.

“As the PLA continues to expand its aerospace capabilities, our need to understand these advancements will continue to grow,” the letter says. An Air Force spokesperson told Breaking Defense that the service “will respond directly to the committee.”

The letter comes after it was revealed in September that the Air Force planned to axe CASI’s 10-member civilian workforce. While the Air Force maintained its premier China-focused think tank would remain open and operate with military personnel, its director, Brendan Mulvaney, stressed in an [interview with Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/09/the-air-force-says-its-china-think-tank-will-continue-its-director-says-its-basically-dead/) that the elimination of its civilian staff would functionally shutter the institute.

Systems that can work independently while still being part of a unit are critical to carrying out multi-domain operations.

 By [Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/author/breakingdefense/)

Founded by Mulvaney roughly a decade ago, CASI regularly publishes on Beijing’s air and space forces, drawing on open-source information translated from Mandarin. The institute’s publications and training courses are seen as valuable resources for educating the broader military policy community on Chinese air and space power, prompting experts to denounce CASI’s expected downsizing.

“The idea that you could do research or the translations that we’re doing is not credible” without civilian experts, Mulvaney previously told Breaking Defense.

Mulvaney explained that the think tank’s civilian posts are being converted to an unfunded status, meaning that staffers will continue to work until being moved to a different role elsewhere in the Department of the Air Force — and once they leave, their positions cannot be backfilled. CASI’s current commitments stretch until around March and will largely function as usual until then, but after that the institute’s fate becomes more unclear, according to Mulvaney.

News of the CASI cuts raised questions about similar efforts run by the Army, Navy and Marine Corps, though spokespeople for each service previously told Breaking Defense that there are no planned changes for their respective Beijing-focused programs.

Intelligent Model Routing, Governed: NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard + Kong AI Gateway
Not every step in an AI agent workflow needs the most powerful and expensive model. So can you ensure every request reaches the right model without sacrificing performance, security, or control?
As enterprises move toward multi-model agentic AI, intelligent model routing is becoming critical infrastructure. Choosing the right model is only half the challenge. Organizations also need to secure credentials, enforce governance policies, protect sensitive data, and maintain visibility across every AI interaction.
Join experts from Kong and NVIDIA to explore how Kong AI Gateway and NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard work together to make intelligent model routing secure, cost-efficient, and production-ready. Discover how Kong AI Gateway provides centralized security, governance, and observability across AI traffic while NeMo Switchyard dynamically selects models based on quality, cost, latency, and confidence.
See the integration in action through a live demonstration and explore benchmark results showing how optimized routing reduced cost per completed task while maintaining task completion rates.
A framework for secure AI governance: Discover how Kong AI Gateway centralizes credentials, enforces guardrails and PII masking, applies rate limits, and provides auditability across model interactions.
A smarter approach to model selection: Learn how NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard dynamically routes agent requests across open and proprietary models, including NVIDIA Nemotron, to optimize cost and performance.
Real-world performance insights: Explore benchmark results demonstrating how intelligent routing optimization reduced cost per completed task by nearly half, without compromising task completion.
A practical path to production-ready agentic AI: Understand how open model routing and centralized governance support secure, scalable AI infrastructure aligned with the Open Secure AI Alliance's principles.

Real Estate Investor Networking - Property Deal Network
Free monthly real estate investor networking in Omaha. Bring a deal, find capital, JV partners, agents, lenders and developers.
👉 Grab your FREE ticket here (required for entry): https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/real-estate-investor-networking-omaha-property-deal-network-pdn-tickets-1999158473811
Property Deal Network (PDN) is a relaxed monthly meetup for real estate investors, developers and professionals who want to do business face-to-face.
People bring deals. Others bring capital. Some are sourcing their next project, others are looking for JV partners or professional services. The format is simple: arrive, grab a drink and start conversations. No presentations, no pitches from the front – just direct networking with people who are actively working in real estate.
Investors (from first-timers to portfolio owners), developers, sourcing agents, brokers, attorneys, architects, lenders and accountants. If you're involved in real estate – or want to be – you'll find relevant people here.

• Cost: Free to attend. The venue asks that everyone buys a drink at full price
• Dress: Smart casual (no sportswear). Over 25s only; ID may be requested

content:
Soup-a-rama Potluck!, Sun, Nov 8, 2026, 1:00 PM | Meetup
Hosted by Jean D. and Lois Bright S.
Lois S. is graciously hosting us at her church. We'll have our very own whole-foods, plant-based, no-oil SOUPFEST.
Any plant-based soup is great, but you're free to bring anything that goes with soup--breads, corn bread, dessert. Bring dishes containing NO oil or animal products. Bring your own take-home containers, and we'll share our leftovers. Plates, eating utensils, and napkins provided. It might be helpful to bring your own serving utensils. We will provide coffee, tea, water, and maybe lemonade.
If you'd like to help set up, come a bit early.
If you're unfamiliar with our way of eating, check our discussion board. You'll find plenty of recipe websites that comply with the Forks Over Knives program. (I promise, it's easy!) A couple of websites with easy, compliant recipes: happyherbivore.com, drmcdougall.com/recipes. Can't cook? Think fruit salad, fruit plate, vegetable platter.
The church was kind enough to offer their space free of charge. We'll clean up after ourselves and wash the dishes after dinner. We'll have an optional free-will donation plate to give them as a thank-you.
(No need to RSVP if you can't make it.)
Omaha Forks Over Knives is a lively group celebrating the health benefits of a whole-foods, plant-based, no-oil diet. Each of us is in a different place with foods we do and do not consume; we're not The Food Police. We're here to support and learn from each other. (While we're at it, we entertain each other as well.) If you're new to this, we ask that, at a minimum, you limit your food selection to plant-based items.

Inspire others and help James Alan Stephen build momentum.
James Alan Stephen Smith is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is James Alan Smith. I’m an avid outdoorsman, fisherman and traveller. I raised four sons through construction and after my divorce, I got my Teaching credentials for Earth Science and Biology at the High School level. Teaching there three years I became frustrated by Teaching at this level. I then applied for a position Teaching English in Taiwan, at the Elementary level.I had a blast. Four of the best years in my life! Make no mistake, I took it seriously, studying Mandarin and taking in as much of their culture which amazed me daily. Forward many years, and my knees are gone with my mind increasingly fogged by a thyroid deficiency. Also, I have my fourth son living with me who, even as an adult has autism and other issues preventing him from being independent. Now, having worked outdoors as a fisherman and builder, I can say unequivocally that our environment IS changing rapidly. My education and observations made me ponder what solutions we must pursue to mitigate or repair damages to our precious gift; planet Earth! Having built many structures personally and designed more, I have drawn up a modest, and humble structure to help in neutralizing CO2 gain in our VERY thin and vulnerable atmosphere! It’s seemingly huge, but in reality only as thick as the skin on an onion, scaled down. Know that this structure will be inhabited by my son and I, though having done years of research I know by using the wood on my property, solar gain and utilizing prevailing westerly winds that I can achieve energy and corporate independence and hopefully share my successes with the public in the pursuit of carbon negativity. I have the land, am planting fruit and nut trees, with Nitrogen fixing trees and shrubs. I have worked very hard, running a contracting business and know the value of a dollar putting myself through College scalloping way off NY, salmon fishing off CA and mating of Montauk and Captree Island during summers when school was off.
I plan on starting a YouTube channel to none other than get the word out, being a Teacher at heart. ANY donation will be greatly appreciated and know that as a believer in miracles, NO money will be wasted or spent irresponsibly.
I also plan on writing a book to share my/our progress, initiatives, inventions, observations, mistakes, joys and frustrations. There are 61 acres, half of which are free, more or less for planting (via Permaculture methods) and raising livestock for food gaining complete self sufficiency, selling surplus for cash, maybe jams, JimJam. lol

content:
Fundraiser by Sean Dineen : Sean dineen's mission to get my dissertation published
Sean Dineen is organizing this fundraiser.
Support My Mission to Empower the Exceptionality Community
As a person with cerebral palsy and many years advocating for people with exceptionalities, I’ve seen firsthand how society often dismisses their potential. Many are denied opportunities and classified in ways that stifle their growth, creating dependency instead of independence. This is not just morally unacceptable—it holds society back from innovation and progress. When my wheelchair got mislaid, I crawled through the streets.
My research challenges these norms. By exploring how nondemocratic societies like Taiwan and apartheid South Africa engaged with the exceptionality community, I’ve uncovered surprising insights. These nations, despite their flaws, prioritized accessibility and genuine inclusion, consulting directly with the communities they aimed to serve. My work highlights how these approaches can inform global policies to create more inclusive and thriving societies.
Now, I need your help to complete this vital research. I’ve traveled extensively, gathering data from South Africa, Australia, and the U.S. But key documents are located in one South African city, while interviews with 13 political leaders are required in another. As someone with cerebral palsy, I also need two assistants to make my travel and research possible.
I’ve raised $1,500 toward my $10,000 goal, but I still need $8,500 to finish. Completing this dissertation is not just a personal milestone—it’s a step toward improving opportunities for the exceptionality community worldwide.
Your support, no matter the amount, will make a difference. Together, we can replace outdated perceptions with true inclusion, unlocking the potential of millions.
Thank you for joining me in this mission.

content:
Fundraiser by Lori Engel : Help Me Heal So I Can Serve!
Lori’s campaign keeps critical neuro care, daily basics, and Teddie’s needs financially covered
Lori Engel is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Lori Engel. I’m 59, homebound in Oregon. I live completely alone with life-altering neurological injuries and disabilities that have reshaped every part of my world.
I grew up as a missionary child in Brazil, where faith, service, and compassion became the foundation of my life. As an adult, I carried that forward—serving six years as a missionary teacher in Taiwan, then eleven years as a chaplain, walking alongside people in illness, grief, crisis, and loss. Caring for others wasn’t just my work; it was my identity. The last two years of my career, I was the Director of Chaplain Services for a healthcare organization.
Prior to becoming a chaplain, I was an English teacher for almost two decades, teaching both in Taiwan and at universities in the U.S.
My path shifted profoundly starting in late 2006. Over time, I sustained multiple traumatic brain injuries and a toxic reaction to Cipro that damaged my nerves and muscles. I developed serious neurological conditions, including cerebellar damage, ataxia, polyneuropathy, spasticity, severe balance impairment, swallowing difficulties, and vision disturbances, to name a few. These affect my ability to walk, stand, use my arms consistently, regulate my nervous system, or handle even basic daily tasks.
Despite these initial injuries, I continued working as a chaplain until 2015, pushing through pain and limitations to serve others, through God's grace and the aid of nutraceuticals. Additional neurological injuries in 2015 made it impossible to continue, leaving me homebound ever since, unable to drive.
Here is a brief summary of all my injuries:
My injuries consist of multiple TBIs (traumatic brain injury) from falling backward onto the kitchen tile floor, hitting the back of my head; slamming my forehead into a concrete bunk bed; and falling and hitting the side of my head here in Oregon. I also experienced medical malpractice that damaged my cervical spine. I was erroneously prescribed fluroquinolones Avelox and Cipro for 30 days straight, which severely damaged my nerves and tendons. (The FDA has issued warnings about these drugs.) Then I got a bad infection. Later, I also experienced thermal burns to my spine and base of my head.
Then, I was exposed to and living in wildfires so severe that ashes were all around me here in Oregon in 2020, which exponentially exacerbated all my autonomic, nerve, and vascular damage, as well as breathing. Then in 2021 I had Covid, which causes neurological issues in even healthy people. For me, it created additional issues.
There has been a compounded, cumulative effect of all the layered injuries. Most people struggle to comprehend such a parade of horribles, but I do have records.
It has been more than I can ever put into words. I am just thankful to be alive. I am thankful for the many years I worked as a chaplain, until there were just too many injuries.
Simple things most people take for granted—opening a package, standing at the sink, stepping outside, or even too much visual input—can overload my fragile system, causing loss of balance, neurological shutdown, or crushing exhaustion. Some days I can’t get out of bed. Others, I push through just to care for myself and my faithful dog Teddie, only to crash afterward.
I haven’t seen my family in 13 years (they live on the East Coast), and for the last 10-plus years I can’t travel. I receive no family financial support. The isolation is profound, and Teddie—my constant companion, emotional anchor, and service companion in many ways—is one of the biggest reasons I keep going, in addition to God's miraculous care.
Yet every day, I fight to heal and hold onto as much independence as possible. As my health allows, I write devotional pieces that integrate faith, neuroscience, and psychology—sharing insights on resilience, hope, and spiritual growth on social media. It’s a small but meaningful way I continue to give back and encourage others, even from home.
My lifeline is an intensive, carefully managed regimen: specialized therapies, targeted nutrition, and essential supplements that stabilize my brain, muscles, emotions, and overall functioning. When I can stay consistent with these protocols, I feel more like myself—steadier, clearer, hopeful. When I can’t, everything declines quickly: neurologically, physically, and emotionally.
My disability income is severely limited (SSDI), and it does not even cover rent. Ongoing costs far exceed what I can cover. Neurological medications/nutraceuticals alone are expensive and not covered by Medicare. I also need nutritious food tailored to my conditions, basic utilities, in-home support, and care for Teddie.
I’m not asking for luxuries—only the basics that allow me to continue healing, stay safe at home, avoid further decline, and keep writing when possible.
Your monthly - or one-time - support will directly help cover:
• Essential neurological and immunological supplements to stabilize my system and medical care not covered by Medicare.
• Basic in-home support and utility expenses
• Veterinary care, food, and supplies for Teddie, my vital companion
• Unexpected critical needs that protect my independence and safety
Every gift—no matter the size—becomes part of this lifeline. It prevents eviction. It helps me get through the hardest days, hold onto hope for continued (even if gradual) improvement.
Sharing this campaign is also a huge gift. When you’re largely invisible due to homebound disability, profound isolation, and no nearby support network, awareness can make all the difference.
After a lifetime of caring for others, I now humbly need care myself. It’s been a difficult shift, but I’m grateful for every act of kindness.God has never failed me during these long, lonely years.
It's been a long, agonizing road, but I still believe healing is possible. I still hold fast to faith that God can bring restoration, step by step—and use even my writing to touch lives. I will never stop trying.
Thank you for seeing me, for caring, and for helping carry what I cannot carry alone. Your support—financial, prayerful, or simply shared—means more than words can express.
With deepest gratitude and hope,
"Out of suffering come the strongest souls."

Lori Engel is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Lori Engel. I’m 59, homebound in Oregon. I live completely alone with life-altering neurological injuries and disabilities that have reshaped every part of my world.
I grew up as a missionary child in Brazil, where faith, service, and compassion became the foundation of my life. As an adult, I carried that forward—serving six years as a missionary teacher in Taiwan, then eleven years as a chaplain, walking alongside people in illness, grief, crisis, and loss. Caring for others wasn’t just my work; it was my identity. The last two years of my career, I was the Director of Chaplain Services for a healthcare organization.
Prior to becoming a chaplain, I was an English teacher for almost two decades, teaching both in Taiwan and at universities in the U.S.
That path shifted profoundly starting in late 2006. Over time, I sustained multiple traumatic brain injuries and a toxic reaction to Cipro that damaged my nerves and muscles. I developed serious neurological conditions, including cerebellar damage, ataxia, polyneuropathy, spasticity, severe balance impairment, swallowing difficulties, and vision disturbances, to name a few. These affect my ability to walk, stand, use my arms consistently, regulate my nervous system, or handle even basic daily tasks.
Despite these initial injuries, I continued working as a chaplain until 2015, pushing through pain and limitations to serve others, through God's grace and the aid of nutraceuticals. Additional neurological injuries in 2015 made it impossible to continue, leaving me homebound ever since, unable to drive.
Here is a brief summary of all my injuries:
My injuries consist of multiple TBIs (traumatic brain injury) from falling backward onto the kitchen tile floor, hitting the back of my head; slamming my forehead into a concrete bunk bed; and falling and hitting the side of my head here in Oregon. I also experienced medical malpractice that damaged my cervical spine. I was erroneously prescribed fluroquinolones Avelox and Cipro for 30 days straight, which severely damaged my nerves and tendons. (The FDA has issued warnings about these drugs.) Then I got a bad infection. Later, I also experienced thermal burns to my spine and base of my head.
Then, I was exposed to and living in wildfires so severe that ashes were all around me here in Oregon in 2020, which exponentially exacerbated all my autonomic, nerve, and vascular damage, as well as breathing. Then in 2021 I had Covid, which causes neurological issues in even healthy people. For me, it created additional issues.
There has been a compounded, cumulative effect of all the layered injuries. Most people struggle to comprehend such a parade of horribles, but I do have records.
It has been more than I can ever put into words. I am just thankful to be alive. I am thankful for the many years I worked as a chaplain, until there were just too many injuries.
Simple things most people take for granted—opening a package, standing at the sink, stepping outside, or even too much visual input—can overload my fragile system, causing loss of balance, neurological shutdown, or crushing exhaustion. Some days I can’t get out of bed. Others, I push through just to care for myself and my faithful dog Teddie, only to crash afterward.
I haven’t seen my family in 13 years (they live on the East Coast), and for the last 10-plus years I can’t travel. I receive no family financial support. The isolation is profound, and Teddie—my constant companion, emotional anchor, and service companion in many ways—is one of the biggest reasons I keep going, in addition to God's miraculous care.
Yet every day, I fight to heal and hold onto as much independence as possible. As my health allows, I write devotional pieces that integrate faith, neuroscience, and psychology—sharing insights on resilience, hope, and spiritual growth on social media. It’s a small but meaningful way I continue to give back and encourage others, even from home.
My lifeline is an intensive, carefully managed regimen: specialized therapies, targeted nutrition, and essential supplements that stabilize my brain, muscles, emotions, and overall functioning. When I can stay consistent with these protocols, I feel more like myself—steadier, clearer, hopeful. When I can’t, everything declines quickly: neurologically, physically, and emotionally.
My disability income is severely limited (SSDI), and it does not even cover rent. Ongoing costs far exceed what I can cover. Neurological medications/nutraceuticals alone are expensive and not covered by Medicare. I also need nutritious food tailored to my conditions, basic utilities, in-home support, and care for Teddie.
I’m not asking for luxuries—only the basics that allow me to continue healing, stay safe at home, avoid further decline, and keep writing when possible.
Your monthly - or one-time - support will directly help cover:
• Essential neurological and immunological supplements to stabilize my system and medical care not covered by Medicare.
• Basic in-home support and utility expenses
• Veterinary care, food, and supplies for Teddie, my vital companion
• Unexpected critical needs that protect my independence and safety
Every gift—no matter the size—becomes part of this lifeline. It prevents eviction. It helps me get through the hardest days, hold onto hope for continued (even if gradual) improvement.
Sharing this campaign is also a huge gift. When you’re largely invisible due to homebound disability, profound isolation, and no nearby support network, awareness can make all the difference.
After a lifetime of caring for others, I now humbly need care myself. It’s been a difficult shift, but I’m grateful for every act of kindness.God has never failed me during these long, lonely years.
It's been a long, agonizing road, but I still believe healing is possible. I still hold fast to faith that God can bring restoration, step by step—and use even my writing to touch lives. I will never stop trying.
Thank you for seeing me, for caring, and for helping carry what I cannot carry alone. Your support—financial, prayerful, or simply shared—means more than words can express.
With deepest gratitude and hope,
"Out of suffering come the strongest souls."
(With friends who brought Lori food in 2017)
In 2021, after wounds discovered under hair

content:
Fundraiser by Rebekah Wyse : Rebekah's Car- Road to Independence
Rebekah Wyse is organizing this fundraiser.
I have a condition called Osteogenesis Imperfect (OI Brittle Bones). When I was younger I would break my bones all the time. They would break so easily that the I would cough or sneeze my ribs would break. Each year, my bones became stronger because of all the medication and rodding surgeries. Thanks to Shriners Children’s Hospital. I have not broken anything since I was in 8th grade. My parents Keith and Cheryl Wyse adopted my twin and me from Taiwan. I was 21 months old when we came to the United States. When I was little doctors told my parents that I would not be able to sit up, walk with crutches, or do anything for myself. Today I am able to do all those and even drive. I am grateful they gave me a second chance at a wonderful life.
Being able to drive to work and drive to school independently is one of my many dreams I wish to achieve. Right now I am trying to finish off my general classes at Northwest Community College. Then I will transfer to Wright State University. My main goal is to receive my Master’s Degree in Social Work. I would like to eventually be able to work at a hospital, an adoption agency, or a grief and loss counseling facility. My father had passed away January 2017 and I want to be there for others and their loved ones in their time of need.
In order to buy my vehicle, I need to follow all the state requirements. Which is why it cost $20,000.
2) Has to be under 3,600 miles
With your help, I can accomplish my dreams and hopefully be an inspiration to other people.

Sofia Hernandez for Adriana Perilla Glen
Through Global Leadership Adventures (GLA) I have discovered a wonderful opportunity that is bound to change my life! GLA is an international education organization. Its mission is to operate programs around the world, which offer educational, service and leadership opportunities for young people in order to foster leadership development and global citizenship.
While volunteering in China I will be based in Shaxi village. During my stay there, I will be communicating with the locals to work on temple restoration projects. In the nearby Bai village I will be teaching some English to young kids who only speak the Bai dialect. From there, we will move on to learn about farming in China while helping local farmers remove weeds from their crops.
I am excited to meet the international staff and students, volunteer with local communities, and explore the history and culture of China while developing my leadership potential.
This is my fourth year studying Mandarin. I really enjoy learning a language that is completely different to Spanish, my first language, and English! Learning new characters and their meanings is especially challenging and fun!
In the course of my life I hope to become a fluent Mandarin speaker.
Traveling to Taiwan to attend intensive Mandarin courses will boost my Mandarin skills, while bringing me closer to my goal.
During my time in Taiwan I hope to travel to cultural attractions by riding the high speed railways which connect the country. Traveling alone will help me gain independence and give me the opportunity to use my Mandarin.
While learning a language in a classroom setting is an important step in the learning process, only through real-life application can I truly expand my knowledge.
The funds raised will be used to cover the GLA volunteering program cost in China and airfare tickets from the US to Asia and back. In Taiwan, the funds will cover language classes, lodging, meals, and transportation including visa costs for both countries.
Unfortunately I cannot afford to go on this 6 week trip without your help!
I hope that you will help me go on this life changing experience! Any donation, no matter the amount, gets me closer to my goal.

content:
Fundraiser by Kurshat Uyghur : Support Uyghur film & tell the story together
Kurshat Uyghur is organizing this fundraiser.
We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.
If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group
The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:
$100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter.
$200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter.
$500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film.
$5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer.
Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.
We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.
