title: Hey, Siri: Plug into my app like you said you'd do way back in 2024
zh_title: 嘿，Siri：插入我的应用程序，就像你在 2024 年说的那样
summary: 从周二开始，开发者可以通过 iOS 27.3、iPadOS 27.3、macOS 27.3 和 VisionOS 27.3 的测试版探索其 Apple 平台应用程序的扩展 Siri AI 集成。明年春天，在宣布更深入的第三方 Siri 集成计划近三年后，苹果预计将开始接受使用新功能的 App Store 提交。苹果在开发者新闻中表示：“这个开发者测试版让开发者可以一睹 Siri AI 应用程序的意图。” “通过这个早期的开发者预览版，您的应用程序可以直接与 Siri AI 配合使用，让您首先了解接触和使用 Siri 的新方法。
content:
从周二开始，开发者可以通过 iOS 27.3、iPadOS 27.3、macOS 27.3 和 VisionOS 27.3 的测试版探索其 Apple 平台应用程序的扩展 Siri AI 集成。明年春天，在宣布更深入的第三方 Siri 集成计划近三年后，苹果预计将开始接受使用新功能的 App Store 提交。苹果在开发者新闻中表示：“这个开发者测试版让开发者可以一睹 Siri AI 应用程序的意图。” “通过这个早期的开发者预览版，您的应用程序可以直接与 Siri AI 配合使用，让您首先了解接触和服务客户​​的新方法。”任何事情都可能有所改善。 Apple 的 Siri 是一项语音激活助理服务，其历史可以追溯到 2011 年，并于 2016 年获得了有限的第三方应用程序访问权限。2024 年，它成为与 Apple Intelligence（其生成人工智能功能套件）进行交互的界面。苹果的情报并不是很聪明——几项宣传的 Siri 功能被推迟，以至于苹果在 2025 年因误导性营销指控而被起诉。在 2025 年 12 月苹果机器学习团队进行改组后，Siri 和 Apple Intelligence 在 6 月份的苹果全球开发者大会上进行了改造。 “今年之前，Siri 是一个有声音的计时器，”一家媒体公司的苹果平台工程师、电子书 On-Device Intelligence 的作者 Roberto Gutierrez 在给 The Register 的电子邮件中说道。 “天气、警报、电话。
“在开发者方面，SiriKit 涵盖了少数领域，而只有当用户记住这句话时，快捷方式才起作用。Siri AI 是第一个能够理解上下文并可以跨应用程序链接操作的版本。这是一个真正的变化。”然而，古铁雷斯指出，有一个问题。 Siri AI 仅支持有限的语言和地区。预计到 2026 年底将支持繁体中文，而在欧盟的可用性仍然是一个谈判问题 - Siri AI 在欧盟的 iOS、iPadOS 和 watchOS 上不可用，因为苹果正在根据欧洲数字市场法案解决互操作性问题。该公司上个月表示，“苹果正在与欧盟进行建设性合作，试图找到前进的道路”，但没有承诺做出任何让步。古铁雷斯表示，他预计向第三方开发者开放 Siri 将在一定程度上发挥作用。 “Siri 只能做应用程序通过 App Intents 公开的事情，而 SiriKit 即将被淘汰，”他说。 “如果你的应用程序的主要操作没有暴露，新的 Siri 就看不到你。更大的转变是让 Claude、Gemini 和其他人插入。开发人员已经为每个 AI 功能在三个选项之间进行选择：Apple 的系统模型、通过 MLX 的开放模型或云 API。Siri 也在朝着同样的方向发展。它不需要是最智能的模型。它需要是最好的路由器。
这是正确的选择。”由于未能发布显示其基础模型与开放权重替代方案的比较基准，苹果公司使在这三个选项之间进行选择变得更加困难。该公司已经发布了第三代基础模型与其 2025 年前代产品相比的测量结果。但据我们所知，该公司的承诺 - “在今年夏天晚些时候的技术报告中[分享]有关我们最新基础模型的更多细节，包括更新的评估和基准” - 仍然没有兑现。 Gutierrez 运行了自己的基准测试，将 Apple 的 iOS 系统模型（FM 系统，~3B）与几个开放权重模型进行比较。

【原文 English Original】
As of Tuesday, developers can explore expanded Siri AI integration for their Apple platform apps through beta releases of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3. Next spring, nearly three years after announcing plans for deeper third-party Siri integration, Apple expects to begin accepting App Store submissions using the new capabilities. "This developer beta offers a sneak peek at Siri AI app intents for developers," Apple said in a developer news post . "With this early Developer Preview, your app can work directly with Siri AI, giving you a first look at new ways to reach and serve your customers." Anything is likely to be an improvement. Apple's Siri, a voice-activated assistant service, dates back to 2011 and gained limited third-party app access in 2016. In 2024, it became an interface for interacting with Apple Intelligence, its suite of generative AI features. Apple Intelligence has not been very intelligent – several advertised Siri capabilities were delayed, so much so that Apple was sued in 2025 over allegations of misleading marketing. After a shakeup of Apple's machine learning group in December 2025, Siri and Apple Intelligence received a makeover at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference in June. "Before this year, Siri was a timer with a voice," said Roberto Gutierrez, Apple platforms staff engineer at a media company and author of the e-book On-Device Intelligence, in an email to The Register . "Weather, alarms, calls. Anything past that was a coin toss. "On the developer side, SiriKit covered a handful of domains and Shortcuts only worked if users memorized the phrase. Siri AI is the first version that understands context and can chain actions across apps. That's a real change." There is a catch, however, Gutierrez observed. Siri AI is available in a limited number of languages and regions. Support for Traditional Chinese is expected by the end of 2026, and EU availability remains a matter of negotiation – Siri AI is unavailable on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS in the bloc as Apple works through interoperability concerns under Europe's Digital Markets Act. "Apple is working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward," the company said last month without committing to any concessions. Gutierrez said that he expects opening Siri to third-party developers will be useful to some extent. "Siri can only do what apps expose through App Intents, and SiriKit is on its way out," he said. "If your app's main actions aren't exposed, the new Siri can't see you. The bigger shift is letting Claude, Gemini and others plug in. Developers already choose between three options for every AI feature: Apple's system model, an open model through MLX, or a cloud API. Siri is heading the same way. It doesn't need to be the smartest model. It needs to be the best router. That's the right call." Apple has made choosing between those three options more difficult by failing to publish benchmarks that show how its Foundation Models compare with open-weight alternatives. The biz has published measurements of how its third-generation Foundation Models compare to their 2025 predecessors. But the company's commitment – to "[share] more details on our latest foundation models, including updated evaluations and benchmarks, in a technical report later this summer" – remains unfulfilled so far as we're aware. Gutierrez ran his own benchmark s to compare Apple's iOS system model (FM system, ~3B) to several open-weight models that are suitable for use on-device. "On an A17 Pro iPhone running iOS 26, I tested Apple's system model against Qwen3 1.7B and 4B, Llama 3.2 3B and Gemma 3 4B on a structured-output task," he said. "Speed: Apple's model ran at about 149 tok/s, roughly 3x the fastest open model (Qwen3 1.7B, about 46)." Quality, he said, was a tie, with every model passing five typed checks. But memory, he said, was where Apple's models had an advantage. "The system model's weights live outside your app's memory budget," he explained. "My app peaked at 12 MB during inference. An open 4B model costs 2.4-2.7 GB, and a 2.4 GB model plus your app plus a WebView is a crash report. So yes, it's competitive, and on iPhone it's the default I'd recommend. If you want your own model, Qwen3 1.7B is the one." But Gutierrez urged Apple to publish proper competitive benchmarks. "Their numbers compare against their own previous models," he said. "Developers aren't choosing between Apple 2025 and Apple 2026. We're choosing between Apple, Qwen and a cloud API. I had to build my own harness to answer a question Apple could settle with one table." The absence of competitive model metrics is not the only gap. Apple has also failed to accommodate web apps. "Web apps are locked out," said Gutierrez. "Foundation Models is a Swift API (and now Python). No JavaScript, no WebKit. A PWA's only option is to ship its own model into the browser and pay the full memory bill inside a WebView." And bringing your own model may pose performance problems. "On an A17 Pro iPhone, the 3-4B open models pushed the phone into 'fair' thermal state and dropped to 12-24 tok/s," he said. "In practice, your own model on iPhone means ~2B or smaller." With Siri AI unavailable on iPhones, iPads, and Apple Watches in the EU (and its rollout in mainland China subject to regulatory requirements), developers may need a fallback for global apps to handle regional restrictions. Apple's Private Cloud Compute offers eligible developers access to Foundation Models, Gutierrez observed, though it requires membership in the App Store Small Business Program, fewer than two million first-time App Store downloads across their apps, and the necessary entitlement. ®

title: Rare Earths Norway OKs $27 million Fen pilot plant
zh_title: 挪威稀土公司同意斥资 2700 万美元建造 Fen 试点工厂
summary: 私人控股开发商稀土挪威公司批准建造一座耗资 2400 万欧元（合 2700 万美元）的试点工厂，以测试其 Fen 项目材料的加工，推动将欧洲记录在案的最大稀土矿床转变为永磁原料来源的努力。该公司周二表示，该工厂位于奥斯陆西南约 160 公里处的 Ulefoss，计划于 2027 年第三季度开始运营。资金包括来自挪威创新署的 540 万欧元和来自 Telemark 发展基金的 190 万欧元。其他贡献没有具体说明。 “这项投资是一项持续
content:
私人控股开发商稀土挪威公司批准建造一座耗资 2400 万欧元（合 2700 万美元）的试点工厂，以测试其 Fen 项目材料的加工，推动将欧洲记录在案的最大稀土矿床转变为永磁原料来源的努力。该公司周二表示，该工厂位于奥斯陆西南约 160 公里处的 Ulefoss，计划于 2027 年第三季度开始运营。资金包括来自挪威创新署的 540 万欧元和来自 Telemark 发展基金的 190 万欧元。其他贡献没有具体说明。挪威稀土公司首席执行官 Håvard Moe 在声明中表示：“这项投资是 Fen 矿床投入生产的具体步骤。” “该试点项目将使我们能够验证我们的加工路线，生成必要的运营数据，并向欧洲合作伙伴提供稀土产品，以进行金属和磁铁的测试生产。”这项投资的消息传出之际，欧盟（EU）成员国正在加大力度减少对中国稀土和磁铁的依赖。 Fen 拥有钕和镨这两种稀土元素，用于电动汽车、风力涡轮机和国防设备的强力磁铁，使该项目在挪威以外具有重要意义。总部位于柏林的 EIT RawMaterials 财团首席执行官 Bernd Schäfer 在声明中表示：“欧洲对进口稀土的依赖是我们不能再忽视的战略弱点。”
EIT 是欧盟支持的原材料创新网络，正在为挪威项目提供资金。挪威稀土综合路线的目标是在 2030 年代初期开始商业化开采稀土。在此之前，该试点工厂将测试从矿石到稀土氧化物的综合路线，生成运行数据并向欧洲合作伙伴提供产品，用于金属和磁铁的试生产。它将坐落在现有的工业建筑内。 3 月份发布的芬矿资源更新概述了 1.23 亿吨稀土氧化物品位 1.35%，其中氧化物含量约为 170 万吨。推断资源量10.8亿吨，品位1.31%，其中储量1420万吨。该资源的生效日期为 12 月 31 日。所含氧化物总量比 2024 年报告的 880 万吨增加了约 80%。该估计还确定了芬的第一个指示资源，该类别比推断材料具有更大的地质信心。钕和镨氧化物约占指定类别稀土氧化物总量的 19%。此次扩张反映了挪威稀土公司拟议采矿方法的额外钻探和变化。该公司分析了约 30,000 米的钻芯，其中包括去年勘探活动中的 10,000 米。其设计将地下开口与地表之间的保护岩层从 25 米增加到 100 米。
国家利益挪威政府于4月接管了分区程序，因为该开发涉及国家利​​益问题。9月，政府设定了到2028年完成该计划的目标，最好是在明年年底。该过程将确定地下采矿、加工设施、尾矿储存和基础设施的位置和条件。挪威环境局 3 月份发布的试点申请设想在三年内加工 6,000 吨矿石，以优化精矿生产。

【原文 English Original】
Privately held developer Rare Earths Norway approved construction of a €24-million ($27 million) pilot plant to test processing of material from its Fen project, advancing efforts to turn Europe’s largest documented rare earths deposit into a source of permanent-magnet ingredients. The facility in Ulefoss, about 160 km southwest of Oslo, is scheduled to start operating in the third quarter of 2027, the company said Tuesday . Funding includes €5.4 million from Innovation Norway and €1.9 million from the Telemark Development Fund. Other contributions weren’t specified. “This investment is a concrete step towards bringing the Fen deposit into production,” Rare Earths Norway CEO Håvard Moe said in the statement. “The pilot will allow us to validate our processing route, generate essential operating data and supply rare earth products to European partners for test production of metal and magnets.” News of the investment comes as European Union (EU) member countries step up efforts to cut their dependence on Chinese rare earths and magnets. Fen holds neodymium and praseodymium – two rare earth elements that are used in powerful magnets for electric vehicles, wind turbines and defence equipment, giving the project significance beyond Norway. “Europe’s dependence on imported rare earths is a strategic vulnerability we can no longer afford to ignore,” Bernd Schäfer, CEO of the Berlin-based EIT RawMaterials consortium, said in the statement. EIT, an EU-backed raw materials innovation network, is providing funding for the Norwegian project. Integrated route Rare Earths Norway aims to begin extracting rare earths commercially in the early 2030s. Until then, the pilot plant will test an integrated route from ore to rare earth oxides, generate operating data and supply products to European partners for trial production of metals and magnets. It will sit inside an existing industrial building. A resource update for Fen released in March outlined 123 million indicated tonnes grading 1.35% total rare earth oxides, containing about 1.7 million tonnes of oxides. Inferred resources totalled 1.08 billion tonnes grading 1.31%, containing 14.2 million tonnes. The resource has an effective Dec. 31 date. Combined contained oxides rose about 80% from the 8.8 million tonnes reported in 2024. The estimate also established Fen’s first indicated resource, a category carrying greater geological confidence than inferred material. Neodymium and praseodymium oxides account for about 19% of total rare earth oxides in the indicated category. The expansion reflected additional drilling and changes to Rare Earths Norway’s proposed mining approach. The company had analysed about 30,000 metres of drill core, including 10,000 metres from last year’s exploration campaign. Its design increased the protective rock layer between underground openings and the surface to 100 metres from 25 metres. National interest Norway’s government took over the zoning process in April because the development involves matters of national interest. In September, the government set an ambition to complete the plan by 2028, preferably by the end of next year. The process will determine locations and conditions for underground mining, processing facilities, tailings storage and infrastructure. A pilot application published by Norway’s Environment Agency in March envisaged processing 6,000 tonnes of ore over three years to optimize concentrate production.

title: Avaza Summit Turns C6 Format Toward Practical Cooperation
zh_title: Avaza 峰会将 C6 格式转向实际合作
summary: 内容提要：10 月 8 日举行的阿瓦扎峰会是中亚国家元首首次磋商会议，阿塞拜疆作为正式成员，确认了巴库的地区作用，并任命其为 2027 年主席国。领导人将六国模式推向经济协调，提出联合生产链、更快启动基础设施发展委员会、共享电子商务平台、人工智能伙伴关系和区域绿色转型战略。由于提议将中华人民共和国与中国连接起来，中部走廊的交通量今年增长了近 20%。
content:
内容提要：10 月 8 日举行的阿瓦扎峰会是中亚国家元首首次磋商会议，阿塞拜疆作为正式成员，确认了巴库的地区作用，并任命其为 2027 年主席国。领导人将六国模式推向经济协调，提出联合生产链、更快启动基础设施发展委员会、共享电子商务平台、人工智能伙伴关系和区域绿色转型战略。由于提议将中华人民共和国-吉尔吉斯斯坦-乌兹别克斯坦铁路与巴库-第比利斯-卡尔斯线以及特朗普国际和平与繁荣路线走廊连接起来，中间走廊运输量今年增长了近20%。 10月8日，中亚五国和阿塞拜疆领导人齐聚土库曼斯坦阿瓦扎，举行第八次磋商会议。继2025年11月一致决定将巴库纳入其中之后，这次峰会是阿塞拜疆作为正式参与者举行的第一次正式协商会议。会议最后决定阿塞拜疆将在2027年主持协商会议。领导人还签署了两份文件——《联合声明》和《关于协商会议规范性文件的决定》（趋势通讯社；阿塞拜疆总统，10月8日）。
结果不仅重申了阿塞拜疆在区域架构中的地位，而且还表明六国模式（越来越多地被称为C6）正在获得更加实际和制度化的维度。协商会议于2018年启动，旨在鼓励政治对话和建立信任，现在更加注重区域经济举措的协调（见EDM，1月21日）。 Avaza会议通过提出联合生产链和更密切的产业合作反映了这一转变。阿塞拜疆总统伊利哈姆·阿利耶夫强调了阿塞拜疆与哈萨克斯坦、乌兹别克斯坦和吉尔吉斯斯坦联合投资基金的重要性，敦促更多地利用这些基金“实施联合项目，建立新的制造设施，扩大工业合作”（阿塞拜疆总统，10月8日）。阿塞拜疆的加入将这些不断扩大的双边关系纳入了一个共同的区域框架，为投资、运输和能源项目上更密切的协调创造了机会。这种渐进的制度化方法在 Avaza 表达的立场中显而易见。乌兹别克斯坦总统沙夫卡特·米尔济约耶夫呼吁进一步制定协商会议的法律框架，同时也强调各国并不寻求繁琐的机构。
他的建议集中于基础设施、投资、产业合作和新技术的实际协调（乌兹别克斯坦总统，10 月 8 日）。在提出“六大经济体 — 一种产品”公式时，他解释说，联合生产链将创造“比普通商品交换更强大、更可持续的经济联系”（阿塞拜疆总统，10 月 8 日）。为了促进这种合作，他建议2027年在乌兹别克斯坦希瓦举办中亚-阿塞拜疆商业论坛（乌兹别克斯坦总统，10月8日）。经济议程反映了阿塞拜疆与中亚之间不断变化的关系。阿利耶夫在峰会上表示，“去年阿塞拜疆与中亚国家的贸易增长了50%以上”。他补充说

【原文 English Original】
Executive summary: The October 8 Avaza summit was the first Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia with Azerbaijan as a full member, confirming Baku’s regional role and naming it the 2027 chair. Leaders moved the six-country format toward economic coordination, proposing joint production chains, a faster launch of the Council for Infrastructure Development, a shared e-commerce platform, an artificial intelligence partnership, and a regional green transition strategy. Middle Corridor transit rose nearly 20 percent this year, amid proposals to link the People’s Republic of China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway to the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars line and the corridor to the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity. On October 8, the leaders of the five Central Asian states and Azerbaijan gathered in Avaza, Turkmenistan, for the eighth Consultative Meeting. Following the unanimous decision to include Baku in November 2025, the summit was the first formal Consultative Meeting with Azerbaijan as a full-fledged participant. The meeting concluded with the decision that Azerbaijan would chair the Consultative Meeting in 2027. The leaders also signed two documents—the Joint Statement and the Decision on the Regulatory Documents of the Consultative Meeting ( Trend News Agency ; President of Azerbaijan , October 8). The results not only reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s position in the regional architecture, but also showed that the six-country format, increasingly referred to as C6, is acquiring a more practical and institutional dimension. The Consultative Meetings were initiated in 2018 to encourage political dialogue and confidence-building and now are becoming more focused on the coordination of regional economic initiatives (see EDM , January 21). The Avaza meeting reflected this shift by proposing joint production chains and closer industrial cooperation. Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev emphasized the importance of Azerbaijan’s joint investment funds with Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan, urging their greater use to “implement joint projects, establish new manufacturing facilities, and expand industrial cooperation” ( President of Azerbaijan , October 8). Azerbaijan’s accession brought these expanding bilateral ties into a shared regional framework, creating opportunities for closer coordination on investment, transport, and energy projects. This gradual approach to institutionalization was evident in the positions expressed at Avaza. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev called for further development of the legal framework that governs the Consultative Meetings, while also emphasizing that the countries did not seek cumbersome institutions. His proposals centered on the practical coordination of infrastructure, investment, industrial cooperation, and new technologies ( President of Uzbekistan , October 8). Presenting the “Six Economies – One Product” formula, he explained that joint production chains would create economic ties “far stronger and more sustainable than ordinary commodity exchange” ( President of Azerbaijan , October 8). To facilitate this collaboration, he suggested holding a Central Asia–Azerbaijan Business Forum in Khiva, Uzbekistan in 2027 ( President of Uzbekistan , October 8). The economic agenda reflects the evolving relationship between Azerbaijan and Central Asia. During the summit, Aliyev stated, “Last year, Azerbaijan’s trade with Central Asian countries increased by more than 50 percent.” He added that “over 400 companies with capital from Central Asian countries are actively operating in our country” ( President of Azerbaijan , October 8). These growing economic ties provide the expanded consultative format with a more robust practical foundation. Connectivity is another important pillar of C6 cooperation, with the Middle Corridor linking Central Asia to international markets through Azerbaijan. The Joint Statement identified the development of integrated regional transport infrastructure, including the East–West and North–South corridors, as a priority for sustainable economic growth and stronger interregional ties ( APA , October 8). Speaking at Avaza, Aliyev declared, “The Middle Corridor is gaining ever greater importance,” pointing out that transit cargo volumes along the route rose by nearly 20 percent in the first eight months of 2026 and by more than 10 percent in 2025 ( President of Azerbaijan , October 8). Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev also proposed expert discussions on integrating the Middle Corridor with the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), arguing that this would “expand its existing potential and serve the long-term interests of all our countries” ( President of Kazakhstan , October 8). Coordinated infrastructure development, dependable Caspian shipping services, streamlined border processes, and more consistent transit times will all be necessary to sustain this growth. Mirziyoyev called for accelerating the establishment of the Council for Infrastructure Development and for holding its inaugural meeting in Uzbekistan. He emphasized, “New transport corridors should be accompanied by production facilities, logistics and service centers, and industrial zones. In this way, a transport route creates an economy around itself and brings much greater benefits to every country through which it passes” ( President of Uzbekistan , October 8).  The council could coordinate projects currently developed mainly through bilateral agreements and smaller multilateral partnerships. The proposed integration of the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan (CKU) railway with the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars line illustrates the potential for a more interconnected transport network linking Central Asia and the South Caucasus through Azerbaijan (see EDM , July 15). Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov also emphasized the CKU railway’s potential to connect regional economies with international transport and production networks. “Our benchmark should be measurable results, lower delivery costs and reduced travel times,” he stated, stressing that all countries should benefit from regional transport projects ( Kyrgyz National News Agency , October 8). The coordination of investment priorities, infrastructure capacity, and logistics procedures is essential, as these projects are currently in varying stages of development. Another emerging dimension of C6 connectivity is energy cooperation. Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan are advancing the Central Asia–Azerbaijan Green Energy Corridor, which aims to transmit renewable electricity across the Caspian Sea to regional and European markets. Although developed outside the C6 mechanism, the project illustrates the potential for smaller partnerships to advance the wider cooperation agenda. The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Asian Development Bank have provided support for the project’s advancement to the feasibility-study stage ( Azerbaijani Ministry of Energy , March 4). Azerbaijani Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov announced in September that the feasibility study is expected to be finalized by May 2027, with commissioning planned from 2032 ( APA , September 25). Other leaders also proposed practical initiatives. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon suggested a regional strategy for the green transition and a large oil refinery to meet regional demand ( Turkmenistan’s State News Agency , October 8). Japarov suggested establishing a shared e-commerce platform for Central Asia and Azerbaijan to enhance market access for regional producers ( President of Azerbaijan , October 8). Tokayev proposed a Central Asian partnership program on artificial intelligence and called for a joint action plan to increase intraregional trade to at least $20 billion ( President of Kazakhstan , October 8). These proposals demonstrate the expansion of C6 cooperation to encompass industrial development, digital markets, and shared approaches to new technologies.  Azerbaijan’s 2027 chairmanship will provide an opportunity to transform the Avaza proposals into coordinated projects and to clarify the practical role of the six-country format. Baku’s transport, energy, and investment connections to Central Asia establish a robust foundation for advancing this agenda. The expanded format may also encourage external partners to collaborate with the six countries as cooperation intensifies. This could eventually facilitate the establishment of a C6+1 arrangement that more accurately reflects the expanding connections between Central Asia and the South Caucasus. When Bosnia and Herzegovina held general elections last month, it  used  biometric voter identification and ballot scanners — a reform widely praised for producing fast and accurate results. That’s a real achievement. But the region’s digital foundations remain fragile, and the region’s adversaries know it. The Balkan chessboard remains checkered, torn between attraction to the European Union and to Russia, with China maneuvering for leverage. Bosnian nationalists, including separatist, pro-Russian Serbs,  won  the recent vote. But Serbs  gave  a pro-European student-led movement a clear majority in another October election, while Montenegro and Albania  closed chapters  in their EU accession talks.  The cheapest way to shift the balance of power is to undermine trust in the ballot. For the region, cybersecurity is not a technical issue. It is a strategic one. Washington is waking up to the risk — but needs to increase its focus on digital dangers. The EU is already pressing for action but must also increase its scrutiny.  Across the region, national cyber-response teams remain small and underfunded, public systems are outdated, and responsibility is fragmented. Large volumes of sensitive data, from tax and health records to the new biometric voter data in Bosnia, are held in databases that are rarely audited.  Telecommunications and surveillance networks rely on Chinese equipment. Belgrade’s Chinese-supplied “ safe city ” facial-recognition system represents the best-known example. Kremlin-funded media and anonymous networks are ready to amplify disinformation, which artificial intelligence now makes cheap to produce in local languages. China’s Huawei remains the dominant supplier to Bosnia’s two largest mobile operators, BH Telecom and Republika Srpska’s M:Tel. The security risks of that choice have never been seriously considered. Western money paid for much of that infrastructure. Bosnia’s biometric voting carries its citizens’ calls, data, and biometric records — and it is only as trustworthy as the equipment and the vendors deployed. For a hostile power, this represents an attractive environment. It does not need to defeat Balkan institutions, only to find the least-protected one. Access gained can be used to collect data on officials, NATO personnel, and diaspora communities; to map energy grids and transport hubs; and to prepare disruption that can be switched on in a crisis. Consider Albania. Earlier this year, HomeLand Justice, a hacker group that the Albanian government links to Iran,  broke  into the national parliament, deleted data, and published lawmakers’ emails on Telegram. Investigators believe the attackers had administrative access well before they revealed themselves; passwords had reportedly not been changed for years, and intrusion alarms did not sound. It was the group’s third major attack on Albanian institutions since 2022.  There are other notable attacks. Ransomware paralyzed Montenegro’s government networks in 2022. Bosnia lacks a fully functioning state-level cyber emergency response team. A 2022 ransomware attack crippled the country’s Parliamentary Assembly, taking its servers, website, and email offline. Thousands of employees in state institutions were locked out of their networks for more than two weeks. No public report on the incident or its lessons was ever released . The pattern persists. In early 2024, hackers breached the Bosnian Republika Srpska’s health information system and its tax administration. Washington has started to worry. Representatives Ritchie Torres and Joe Wilson have introduced H.R. 10748 , the Balkans Security Cooperation Act, which asks the Pentagon to report on every Western Balkan country’s security cooperation with Russia, China, the US, and NATO, including arms deals, exercises, agreements, and intelligence ties. It also asks for an assessment of the Russian-Serbian Humanitarian Center in Niš, which has signed a new development plan with Serbia’s interior ministry for 2025-2027 and whose request for diplomatic status for its staff the US and EU have resisted since 2014. The bill counts tanks, missiles, and agreements. It does not count code, vendors, or data. That gap matters, because the most likely next attack on a Balkan state will not arrive by air. As the bill moves forward, Congress should add a cyber and data annex covering four questions: Which hostile cyber operations have targeted each country since 2012, and by whom? Which foreign vendors supply critical telecommunications, energy, surveillance, and election systems, and under what legal obligations to their home governments? How well are sensitive government and citizen data protected, including biometric data? Where would US, NATO, and EU assistance close gaps fastest? Iran, whose operations in Albania are well-documented, should be included alongside Russia and China. Europe should not wait for Washington. The EU already demands cybersecurity and data protection standards as part of the accession process, and Montenegro and Albania are moving quickly through the chapters. Brussels and NATO should make cyber-resilience a visible, funded priority across the region: shared incident response, regular audits of critical databases, support for election security, and clear rules on high-risk vendors in critical networks. The new political moment creates an opening. Serbia’s incoming government has promised transparency and the rule of law while keeping military neutrality. Cyber cooperation is one area where it can work closely with EU and NATO partners without changing that stance. Bosnia’s successful use of election technology shows what is possible, and also creates a new duty to protect biometric data. Western Balkan citizens want accountable institutions. Protecting that legitimacy means protecting their networks. Dr. Emir Kremić  is a cybersecurity strategist and AI & data governance expert.   He is the former head of the Federal Institute of Statistics of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Co-Founder of Auroris AI. title: How banking giant ICBC helped Chinese firms gain a foothold in Europe’s wind market
zh_title: 银行业巨头中国工商银行如何帮助中国企业在欧洲风电市场站稳脚跟
summary: 俄罗斯 2022 年入侵乌克兰扰乱了欧洲的天然气进口后，欧盟承诺到本世纪末将通过清洁技术采购近一半的能源。但随着欧盟推动能源独立，一个全球超级大国——而不是欧洲公司——准备从新战略中获益。近年来，中国多家风电企业在罗马尼亚、西班牙等国家开发风电场。欧洲官员怀疑，由于北京慷慨的国家补贴，这些公司可以提供更便宜的价格，并于 2024 年发起了调查
content:
俄罗斯 2022 年入侵乌克兰扰乱了欧洲的天然气进口后，欧盟承诺到本世纪末将通过清洁技术采购近一半的能源。但随着欧盟推动能源独立，一个全球超级大国——而不是欧洲公司——准备从新战略中获益。近年来，中国多家风电企业在罗马尼亚、西班牙等国家开发风电场。欧洲官员怀疑，由于北京慷慨的国家补贴，这些公司可以提供更便宜的价格，并于 2024 年启动了一项调查，评估国家援助是否给了他们不公平的优势。国际调查记者联盟审查的机密记录表明，早在这次调查之前，中国最重要的金融机构之一就在北京在欧洲建立经济立足点方面发挥了关键作用。记录显示，过去十年，中国工商银行悄悄为中国风能技术在非洲大陆的扩张提供了资金。工行伦敦分行官员在 2021 年内部备忘录中写道：“工行在为中国太阳能和风能可再生能源市场提供融资方面在商业银行中名列前茅。”该银行的客户包括全球最大的风力涡轮机供应商金风科技股份有限公司，该公司在深圳和香港证券交易所上市，其最大股东包括中国国有实体。
该公司控制着欧洲市场相对较小的份额，但目前是欧盟调查的主要目标，因为它获得了补助、税收和优惠银行贷款，据称这些贷款帮助其超越了欧洲同行。金风科技有时被称为“绿色能源界的华为”，指的是这家中国科技巨头，由于政府的持续支持，其竞争对手相形见绌。金风科技的全球收入在 2025 年突破了 100 亿美元。ICIJ 检查了数十份内部备忘录和其他银行记录。 2016 年和 2024 年，工银伦敦批准了超过 1.4 亿美元的贷款，帮助中国国有企业收购至少 16 个英国风电场的股份。该银行还为中国能源公司在欧洲的业务提供了至少 4.5 亿美元的融资。这些调查结果是 ICIJ 对中国资本调查的一部分，该调查揭示了该银行在中国争取技术霸权和国家自力更生方面的独特作用。这项调查是与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，基于来自中国工商银行伦敦分行和一家英国子公司（统称为“中国工商银行伦敦”）的 480 万份机密文件。中国工商银行伦敦总部。图片来源：Scilla Alecci/ICIJ 这些记录提供了关于工银伦敦如何例行证明交易合理性的新细节，作为支持政府首要任务的一部分：被称为“一带一路”倡议的大规模基础设施投资计划和“中国制造 2025”产业政策。
记录显示，工银伦敦为中国战略性能源公司的国际扩张提供了资金，其中一些公司被指控为中国军事机构谋取利益并窃取竞争对手的工业机密。在非洲、南美和其他地区，贷款帮助中国获得了经济转型所需的铜、锂和其他大宗商品，同时扩大了其在资源丰富国家的政治影响力。中国工商银行没有回应 ICIJ 的置评请求。近年来，欧盟委员会、欧盟

【原文 English Original】
After Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine disrupted Europe’s natural gas imports , the European Union pledged to source nearly half of its energy from clean technology by the end of the decade. But as the EU pushed for energy independence, a global superpower — not European companies — was poised to reap the benefits of the new strategy. In recent years, a number of Chinese wind companies have developed wind parks in Romania, Spain and other countries. European officials suspected those firms could offer cheaper prices thanks to Beijing’s generous state subsidies and in 2024 launched an inquiry to assess whether state aid had given them an unfair advantage. Confidential records reviewed by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists show how, long before that probe, one of China’s most important financial arms had played a key role in establishing Beijing’s economic foothold in Europe. Over the last decade, the records show, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China has quietly financed the expansion of Chinese wind technology across the continent. “ICBC tops the chart of the commercial banks in providing financing to the Chinese solar and wind renewables energy market,” ICBC London officers wrote in an internal 2021 memo. The bank’s clients included Goldwind Science & Technology Co., Ltd., the world’s top supplier of wind turbines, which is listed on the Shenzhen and Hong Kong stock exchanges and includes Chinese state entities among its largest shareholders. The company controls a relatively small share of the European market but is currently the main target of the EU investigation for obtaining grants, tax and preferential bank loans that allegedly helped it outpace its European peers. Sometimes called the “the Huawei of green energy,” a reference to the Chinese tech giant that has dwarfed its competition thanks to sustained government support , Goldwind’s global revenue topped $10 billion in 2025. ICIJ examined dozens of internal memos and other bank records from between 2016 and 2024 and found that ICBC London approved more than $140 million in loans to help Chinese state companies acquire shares in at least 16 U.K. wind farms. The bank has also facilitated at least $450 million in financing for Chinese energy firms’ operations in Europe. The findings are part of ICIJ’s China Capital investigation, which reveals the bank’s unique role in China’s fight for technological supremacy and national self-reliance. The investigation, in collaboration with 23 media partners, is based on 4.8 million confidential files from ICBC’s London branch and a U.K. subsidiary, referred to together as ICBC London. ICBC’s London headquarters. Image: Scilla Alecci/ICIJ The records provide new details on how ICBC London routinely justified deals as part of its support for the government’s top priorities: the massive infrastructure investment plan known as the Belt and Road Initiative and the industrial policy Made in China 2025. ICBC London has financed the international expansion of strategic Chinese energy firms, including some accused of benefiting China’s military apparatus and stealing competitors’ industrial secrets, the records show. In Africa, South America and other regions, loans helped China get copper, lithium and other commodities needed to transform its economy while expanding its political influence in resource-rich countries. ICBC did not respond to ICIJ’s requests for comment. In recent years, the European Commission, the EU’s executive arm, has used new foreign subsidies regulation to crack down on unfair competition and investigate several industries dominated by China. After probing the electric vehicles sector and railroad construction firms, European officials have recently directed their attention toward wind energy. The EU has launched an investigation into whether Chinese firms distorted the internal market by selling cheap products across the whole supply chain. European manufacturers are still the leading turbine providers in the region, but Chinese companies are expanding, according to the trade organization Global Wind Energy Council. Experts warn that increasing dependence on China for critical energy infrastructure could make the EU vulnerable to supply chain disruption, outages and even cybersecurity risks if geopolitical tensions rise. Western governments have been on the alert since 2024 when U.S. authorities found that Chinese-state sponsored hackers known as Volt Typhoon had been lying dormant for years inside critical U.S. infrastructure in preparation for future acts of sabotage. In the case of Goldwind, the European Commission suspects that Chinese government grants, tax breaks and “preferential financing” may have allowed the company “to offer, in certain cases, lower prices than its competitors, thereby winning more wind project tenders in the EU than it would have done in the absence of those foreign subsidies.” Goldwind didn’t respond to ICIJ’s requests for comment. In a public statement published earlier this year, the company said that it complies with local laws. Victor Shih, a political science professor at University of California San Diego who has researched technology financing, told ICIJ that bank loans are an important — and often overlooked — form of state subsidy because all Chinese state-owned institutions, including banks like ICBC, support Beijing’s priorities. “The EU is worried about subsidies, and banks are a big part of the puzzle,” Shih said. “There’s fiscal subsidies, which come from the government budget, but a lot of the investment is financed by bank loans.” green ambitions. “They’re trying to balance these multiple competing objectives that sometimes can contradict.” In a confidential brief for potential lenders, Goldwind touted its insulation from market headwinds as one of its strengths: “Backed by Strong [State Owned Enterprise] background with flexibility from market competition mechanism.” Goldwind had “strong access to funding owing to government support of low-cost financing to the renewable energy sectors,” the brief said. It also said that its subsidiaries in China benefited from tax breaks or were taxed at a preferential 15% rate because of their involvement in technology development or government-supported projects. The standard rate was 25% at the time. The company had already received loans “at favourable rates” from five Chinese state banks worth about $11.5 billion and government grants totalling at least $135 million to support research on advanced turbine models, the brief said. In 2018, as part of a $300 million loan with other banks, ICBC London and two other ICBC branches loaned $110 million to the wind company. In the following years, Goldwind went on to install thousands of turbines across six continents, including in Australia, North America and Europe. In 2021, ICBC branches also financed the company’s expansion in Ukraine, the records show. ‘A new reality’ In 2024, armed with new powers to combat companies benefiting from foreign state subsidies, the European Commission requested information from several Chinese wind companies to assess whether state financial backing had given them an unfair advantage over their competitors. Over the last decade, the growth of China’s economy and its increasing technological sophistication combined with Beijing’s shift toward authoritarianism and interventionist policies have triggered a tightening of global trade rules. “That is a reality of this new era that we’re in,” said Thilo Hanemann, an economist and global trade expert at Rhodium Group, a research firm. Hanemann said the shift had led many governments to reconsider their approach to China to ensure “no individual Chinese investor or bank or company can get to a market position where they could dominate a specific sector area.” There may be “some certain parts of our economy where we do not want to have either foreign investment overall or especially foreign investment from a non-allied nation,” he said. Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, and Xi Jinping, China’s president, following their meeting in Paris, France, in May 2024. Image: Nathan Laine/Bloomberg via Getty Images Earlier this year, European officials singled out Goldwind in public statements. While acknowledging the company’s limited presence in Europe, the officials found “sufficient indications” that Goldwind had received foreign subsidies that “may negatively affect competition for the supply of wind turbines and related services in the EU.” The company said in a public statement that it is cooperating with the European authorities. Beijing has urged the EU to stop the probe and has called the measures against the Chinese firms “discriminatory and restrictive.” A European Commission spokesperson told ICIJ that the probe is ongoing but declined to elaborate. Besides Goldwind, the agency is “still looking into the rest of the market,” the spokesperson said in an emailed statement. The wind industry now wants to “level the playing field,” according to Zipt, the WindEurope spokesperson, after Huawei and other Chinese firms upended Europe’s solar sector with cheaper inverters, the devices that turn solar panel output into grid electricity. “We are a continent that is not very rich in resources,” Zipt said. “So for the time being, solar and wind are the two big mechanisms that we can use to reduce our dependency on fossil fuels. But now the European Union is also clear that they don’t want to swap a dependency on Russian fossil fuel with a dependency on Chinese turbines.” Contributors: Jesús Escudero (ICIJ)

title: Trump Learns His Orbán Lesson
zh_title: 特朗普吸取了欧尔班的教训

content:
世界上最伟大民主国家的总统钦佩独裁领导人。他满怀深情地谈到俄罗斯的弗拉基米尔·普京、中国的习近平，甚至朝鲜的金正恩。但他和他的 MAGA 追随者长期以来显然希望效仿匈牙利前总理维克托·欧尔班 (Viktor Orbán) 的模式，他通过钻研匈牙利的民主机构（包括媒体和法院）统治了大约 20 年，要么破坏要么腐蚀它们。特朗普竭尽全力，如今却又将他引向同样的死胡同。去年春天，匈牙利的选民投票率达到了该国 1990 年民主转型以来的最高水平。选民们抛弃了欧尔班和他的政党青民盟，转而支持青民盟前成员彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar），后者将欧尔班与独裁、腐败和生活水平下降联系在一起。人们普遍预计欧尔班会尽一切努力颠覆投票，但他意识到自己面临的结果太大而无法挑战。匈牙利每个角落的人数都是压倒性的，欧尔班根本无法提出一个可笑的理由来对结果表示怀疑。昨晚，特朗普和他的政党经历了类似的命运，他们遭受了对美国民主的公然攻击、让腐败的恶臭笼罩白宫、发动一场愚蠢且不受欢迎的战争、承诺改善经济却带来通货膨胀和高油价的后果。
和欧尔班一样，他不得不无助地坐着，看着他的政党在民主党几乎灭绝的地方遭受民主党的殴打。（在堪萨斯州，民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿将成为参议员。汉密尔顿出生于 1964 年。堪萨斯州最后一位民主党参议员出生于 1879 年。） [阅读：特朗普重复了一个世纪以来的错误]总统对这一惨败的反应非常平静。当计票开始时，特朗普不是在谴责民主党，而是出于某种原因谴责福克斯新闻。在《真相社会》节目中，他抱怨自己非常讨厌福克斯少数几个内部自由派评论员之一杰西卡·塔洛夫的声音，并声称福克斯的收视率下降“因为他们花了太多时间报道特朗普疯狂的杜民主人士”。特朗普表示，事实上，福克斯忽视了美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的一项民意调查，该民调显示他在共和党人中比亚伯拉罕·林肯 (Abraham Lincoln) 更受欢迎。 （实际上，民意调查提出了一个开放式问题，即人们最钦佩哪位总统，受访者倾向于选择最近的总统。） 随着夜幕降临，共和党的损失不断增加，经常发布大量信息的特朗普却异常安静。晚上 10 点 30 分过后不久东部时间，他对不断加剧的坏消息做出了反应，穿上了由他的高张力自恋制成的盔甲。
“我没有参加选票，”他抱怨道，“如果我参加了，我们就会以压倒性的优势获胜！” （然后，当然是：“谢谢你对此事的关注。”）问题是，特朗普在过去几周里挑战美国人投票，就好像他在选票上一样，数百万人显然接受了他的提议。到傍晚时分，特朗普向欧尔班的转变已经完成。他再次表示，他会接受选举结果，并且愿意与民主党合作，但再次没有表现出他特有的好斗情绪。任何人都猜测他是否打算遵守这些承诺。 （在他听起来很和解的同时，他还贴出了一张帽子的照片，上面写着“否决”一词。）今天早上，

【原文 English Original】
The president of the world’s greatest democracy admires autocratic leaders. He speaks with great affection about Russia’s Vladimir Putin, China’s Xi Jinping, and even North Korea’s Kim Jong Un. But the model that he and his MAGA acolytes have long apparently hoped to emulate was that of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who ruled for some 20 years by boring into Hungary’s democratic institutions, including the media and the courts, and either gutting or corrupting them. Trump tried his best, and it has now led him to the same dead end. Last spring, Hungary experienced the highest voter turnout since the country’s 1990 transition to democracy. Voters threw out Orbán and his party, Fidesz, in favor of a former Fidesz member, Peter Magyar, who’d tied Orbán to autocracy, corruption, and decreasing living standards. Orbán, who was widely expected to do whatever he could to subvert the vote, realized he faced a result too big to challenge. The numbers were overwhelming in every corner of Hungary, and Orbán could not remotely make even a laughable case for casting doubt on the result. Last night, Trump and his party experienced a similar fate as they suffered the consequences of their brazen attacks on American democracy, of allowing the stench of corruption to envelop the White House, of starting a foolish and unpopular war, and of promising a better economy and instead delivering inflation and high gas prices. Like Orbán, he had to sit helplessly and watch his party take beatings from the Democratic Party in places where Democrats were supposedly almost extinct. (In Kansas, the Democrat Adam Hamilton will become a senator. Hamilton was born in 1964. The last Democratic senator from Kansas was born in 1879 .) [ Read: Trump repeats a centuries-old mistake ] The president’s reaction to this crushing loss has been remarkably muted. As vote counting began, Trump spent his time excoriating not the Democrats but, for some reason, Fox News. On Truth Social , he railed about how much he hated the voice of one of Fox’s few in-house liberal commentators, Jessica Tarlov, and claimed that Fox’s ratings were down “because they’re spending too much time covering the Trump Deranged Dumocrats.” In fact, Trump said, Fox was ignoring a CNN poll that showed him to be more popular among Republicans than Abraham Lincoln. (In reality, the poll asked an open-ended question about which president people most admire, and the respondents tended to choose recent presidents.) As the night wore on and Republican losses piled up, Trump, who often posts barrages of messages, was unusually quiet. Shortly after 10:30 p.m. eastern time, he reacted to the accelerating bad news by donning the suit of armor made of his high-tensile-strength narcissism. “I wasn’t on the Ballot,” he whined, “and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” (And then, of course: “Thank you for your attention to this matter.”) The problem is that Trump, over the past weeks, challenged Americans to vote as if he were on the ballot, and millions of people apparently took him up on the offer. By late evening, Trump’s transformation into Orbán was complete. He said —again without his characteristic combativeness—that he would accept the outcome of the election and that he would be willing to work with Democrats. Whether he means to hold to those commitments is anyone’s guess. (At the same time he was sounding conciliatory, he posted a picture of a hat with the word VETO on it.) This morning, Trump appeared at the worksite of his beloved White House ballroom. When reporters asked him about the election, he quietly deflected, saying that he would not have done anything differently, and then went back to talking about marble and kitchens. [ Read: The simple message that produced a Democratic landslide ] Whether Trump has sincerely accepted the victory of the Democrats and intends to cooperate with them in governing the country is, in a sense, irrelevant: The more important reality is that he faces an electoral result too decisive to challenge, as Orbán did. I was among the many who feared that he might inundate state election authorities with lawsuits or even try to seize ballots, but those possibilities evaporated before midnight. So many votes had been cast, even in red states, that any attempt to undermine the result would look either violently dictatorial or patently ridiculous. Trump, like Orbán, wanted to seize power using democratic means, and then eviscerate any future challenges to his power by destroying those same practices and institutions. Like Orbán, Trump’s arrogance, contempt for the law and toleration of corruption, and staggering incompetence pushed even former supporters beyond their limits. Unlike Orbán, he does not have to leave office, and he could provoke any number of crises between now and the 2028 elections. But he seems genuinely deflated by the scale of punishment that the American people have inflicted on his party and his chosen candidates. The Hungarians, many of whom perhaps thought Orbán was destined to be a permanent fixture in their life, relearned the lesson of their Cold War liberation: Mobilization, organization, and voting can bring down an autocracy. Last night, Americans proved that the same methods can forestall one.

title: Hong Kong BN(O) visa holders exempt from UK plan to double settlement wait to 10 years, but face tougher English requirement
zh_title: 香港 BN(O) 签证持有者可免于英国双重定居计划，等待 10 年，但面临更严格的英语要求
summary: 在英国的香港 BN(O) 签证持有者将不受一项提议的约束，该提议将从 2027 年起将定居资格期限延长一倍至十年。“大本钟”，位于伦敦威斯敏斯特英国议会大厦。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。周一，英国内政大臣沙巴纳·马哈茂德提出了一项移民改革，根据该改革，持工作签证的人在五年后将不再自动获得永久居留权。非法抵达的难民将面临20年的等待，如果乘坐小船抵达，则需要等待30年。持有 BN(O) 签证的香港移民仍将面临更严格的 B2 英语限制
content:
在英国的香港 BN(O) 签证持有者将不受一项提议的约束，该提议将从 2027 年起将定居资格期限延长一倍至十年。“大本钟”，位于伦敦威斯敏斯特英国议会大厦。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。周一，英国内政大臣沙巴纳·马哈茂德提出了一项移民改革，根据该改革，持工作签证的人在五年后将不再自动获得永久居留权。非法抵达的难民将面临20年的等待，如果乘坐小船抵达，则需要等待30年。根据新规定，持有 BN(O) 签证的香港移民仍将面临更严格的 B2 英语水平要求和犯罪记录审查。他们还不得持有任何政府债务。年收入至少 5 万英镑（53 万港元）的外来工人——包括医生、护士和教师——只需等待五年。收入超过125,000英镑（131万港元）的人可以在三年后申请定居。香港国际机场的离境大厅。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “获得的定居点在我们的移民体系中建立了一个新的范式，这是早就应该的，”马哈茂德周一告诉议会。 “我们现在能提供的最大权利之一取决于所做的贡献和履行的责任。现在必须赢得永远生活在这个国家的权利。这将不再是自动的。”香港人的签证计划是在北京于 2020 年颁布的香港国安法期间推出的。
已向超过 187,000 人发放了签证。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong BN(O) visa holders in the UK will be exempt from a proposal to double the qualifying period for settlement to ten years from 2027. “Big Ben,” at the UK Houses of Parliament, Westminster, London. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. On Monday, UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood laid out an immigration overhaul under which those on work visas would no longer automatically gain permanent residency after five years. Refugees who arrive illegally would face a wait for 20 years, or 30 if they arrived in a small boat. Hong Kong migrants holding the BN(O) visa would still face a tighter B2 English level language requirement and criminal record checks under the new rules. They must also hold no government debt. Migrant workers earning at least £50,000 (HK$530,000) per year – including doctors, nurses and teachers – will only have to wait five years. Those earning above £125,000 (HK$1.31 million) will be able to apply for settlement after three years. The departure hall in Hong Kong International Airport. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “[E]arned settlement institutes a new paradigm in our migration system, long overdue,” Mahmood told parliament on Monday. “That one of our greatest rights that we can offer now depends upon a contribution made and responsibilities met. The right to live in this country forever must now be earned. It will no longer be automatic.” The visa scheme for Hongkongers was introduced amid the 2020 enactment of the Beijing-imposed security law in the city. Over 187,000 people have been issued with the visa.

title: Hong Kong records GDP rise of over 5% in first three quarters, marking strongest growth in 5 years
zh_title: 香港前三季度GDP增长逾5% 创5年来最强劲增长
summary: 2026年第三季度，香港GDP强劲增长超过5%，今年前9个月的增长创五年来新高。尖沙咀海滨长廊上的人们。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。政府周二宣布，在出口增长加速和内需强劲的推动下，第三季度该市GDP同比增长5.2%。 2026 年前三个季度的实际 GDP 较 2025 年同期 9 个月同比增长 5.1%，创下历史最高纪录
content:
2026年第三季度，香港GDP强劲增长超过5%，今年前9个月的增长创五年来新高。尖沙咀海滨长廊上的人们。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。政府周二宣布，在出口增长加速和内需强劲的推动下，第三季度该市GDP同比增长5.2%。政府表示，2026 年前三个季度的实际 GDP 较 2025 年同期 9 个月同比增长 5.1%，创下五年来最强劲增长。政府发言人表示：“展望未来，香港经济前景依然乐观，最新数据显示增长势头持续。”发言人表示：“强劲的全球人工智能投资应继续支撑香港的商品出口。服务出口亦应受惠于入境旅游业的持续增长、充满活力的跨境交通和活跃的金融市场活动。”财政司司长陈茂波在周日发表的博文中写道，由于经济增长快于预期，政府可能会再次上调GDP预测。 8月初，政府将2026年全年GDP增​​长预测从2.5-3.5%上调至3.5-4.5%。财政司司长陈茂波。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
高盛在周三发布的报告中表示，预计香港全年GDP增​​速将达到5%，高于原来预测的4.2%。该投行表示，第三季度GDP强劲增长主要是受到净出口和政府消费反弹的推动。政府周二表示，香港第三季度私人消费支出较去年同期增长2.8%，继第二季度增长2.9%后保持稳定增长。与此同时，声明称，继第二季度“基本保持不变”之后，第三季度政府消费支出增长了1.7%。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong has seen a strong GDP increase of over 5 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, bringing the growth for the first nine months of the year to a five-year high. People on the waterfront promenade at Tsim Sha Tsui. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Driven by accelerating growth in exports and solid domestic demand, the city’s GDP grew by 5.2 per cent in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, the government announced on Tuesday. For the first three quarters of 2026 combined, real GDP grew by 5.1% over a year relative to the same nine-month period in 2025, marking the strongest growth in five years, the government said. “Looking ahead, Hong Kong’s economic outlook remains positive, with incoming data pointing to sustained growth momentum,” a government spokesperson said. “Robust global artificial intelligence investment should continue to underpin Hong Kong’s merchandise exports. Exports of services should also benefit from sustained growth in inbound tourism, vibrant cross-boundary traffic and active financial market activities,” the spokesperson said. Financial Secretary Paul Chan wrote in a blog post published on Sunday that the government might raise its GDP forecast again as the economy has grown faster than expected. Earlier in August, the government raised its 2026 full-year GDP growth forecast from 2.5-3.5 per cent to 3.5-4.5 per cent. Financial Secretary Paul Chan. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Goldman Sachs said in its report released on Wednesday that it expects Hong Kong’s full-year GDP growth to reach 5 per cent, higher than the original forecast of 4.2 per cent. The investment bank said the strong GDP growth in the third quarter was mainly driven by net exports and a rebound in government consumption. The government said on Tuesday that Hong Kong recorded a 2.8 per cent growth in private consumption expenditure in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, maintaining a steady pace following the 2.9 per cent growth in the second quarter. Meanwhile, government consumption expenditure recorded an increase of 1.7 per cent in the third quarter, after remaining “virtually unchanged” in the second quarter, according to the statement.

title: China seeks arrest of five Uyghurs held in Thailand: Bangkok
zh_title: 中国寻求逮捕在泰国关押的五名维吾尔人：曼谷
summary: 泰国安全局长周三表示，自 2014 年以来在泰国被拘留的五名维吾尔人受到了中国的逮捕令，并补充说法院将决定是否将他们遣返回中国。在这张 2022 年 9 月 30 日拍摄的照片中，人权活动人士认为，曼谷沙通地区的一个移民拘留中心关押着一群维吾尔人。照片：杰克·泰勒/法新社。在其中两人被泰国赦免后，人权组织对这些人表示担忧。活动人士称，他们是穆斯林少数群体的成员，他们在中国受到迫害。
content:
泰国安全局长周三表示，自 2014 年以来在泰国被拘留的五名维吾尔人受到了中国的逮捕令，并补充说法院将决定是否将他们遣返回中国。在这张 2022 年 9 月 30 日拍摄的照片中，人权活动人士认为，曼谷沙通地区的一个移民拘留中心关押着一群维吾尔人。照片：杰克·泰勒/法新社。上个月泰国赦免了其中两人，人权组织对这些人表示担忧。活动人士称，他们是穆斯林少数民族成员，在中国受到迫害。他们是 2014 年逃离中国并被关押在泰国的 300 多名维吾尔人中的一员。其中许多人已逐渐被转移——其中一组于 2015 年被转移到土耳其，其他人于 2015 年和 2025 年被转移到中国。这五人在 2020 年因试图逃避移民拘留而被监禁。一名维权人士和一名官员上周告诉法新社，其中两人被赦免，仍被拘留等待驱逐出境。根据泰国法律，被监禁的外国人只有在刑满后才能被驱逐出境。泰国国家安全委员会秘书长猜普拉克·敦普拉帕 (Chaipruak Doungprapat) 周三对记者表示：“这五人在中国有逮捕令，而且没有难民身份。”他表示，如果中国要求引渡他们，泰国外交部将做出评估，然后由法院做出裁决。
柴普鲁克说：“如果法院裁定他们有罪，他们将根据引渡条约被移交。”一面中国国旗。资料照片：Aboodi Vesakaran，来自 Pexels。 “如果他们赢了，这取决于是否有任何（其他）国家愿意接受他们。”柴普鲁克表示，他们的处境与去年被送回中国的 40 名维吾尔人不同，此举引发了国际谴责。 “与最后 40 人不同，这是一个正义问题，与政策无关，”他补充道，但没有详细说明。中国公安部去年表示，这 40 名被驱逐的中国人是“非法移民”。周三被问及最近五人的命运时，中国外交部发言人毛宁没有提供细节。她说：“中泰合作打击非法移民等跨境犯罪活动符合两国法律、国际法和国际惯例。” 2025 年 3 月 11 日，中国外交部发言人毛宁在新闻发布会上。图片：中国外交部。泰国不是《联合国难民公约》的缔约国，但受不驱回国际法律原则的约束，该原则禁止各国将人员送回生命或自由受到威胁的地方。国际特赦组织和人权观察组织表示，应允许两名被赦免的男子前往安全的第三国。
人权观察周三警告说，他们在中国面临“酷刑和其他严重虐待行为的严重风险”。 自 2017 年以来，北京被指控拘留了超过 100 万维吾尔人和其他穆斯林，这是联合国此前称可能构成反人类罪的行动的一部分。中国强烈否认这些指控，称其政策促进了经济发展并根除了大多数维吾尔人来自的新疆地区的极端主义。

【原文 English Original】
Five Uyghurs detained in Thailand since 2014 are subject to Chinese arrest warrants, the kingdom’s security chief said Wednesday, adding that a court would decide if they would be returned to China. In this photo taken on September 30, 2022, an immigration detention centre, where human rights activists believe that a group of Uyghurs are being detained, is pictured in the Sathorn area of Bangkok. Photo: Jack Taylor/AFP. Human rights groups have raised concerns about the men — members of the Muslim minority group who activists say are persecuted in China — after two of them were pardoned by Thailand last month. They are among more than 300 Uyghurs who fled China and were held in Thailand in 2014. Many have been gradually transferred — one group to Turkey in 2015 and others to China in 2015 and 2025. The five were jailed for trying to escape immigration detention in 2020. Of that group, the two pardoned remain in custody awaiting deportation, a rights campaigner and an official told AFP last week. Under Thai law, imprisoned foreign nationals can only be deported once their sentences are complete. “These five have arrest warrants in China and they have no refugee status,” Chaipruak Doungprapat, secretary-general of Thailand’s National Security Council, told reporters on Wednesday. He said that if China requests their extradition, Thailand’s foreign ministry will make an assessment and a court would then decide. “If the court rules that they are guilty, they will be handed over under the extradition treaty,” Chaipruak said. A Chinese flag. File photo: Aboodi Vesakaran, via Pexels. “If they win, it depends on whether any (other) country is willing to take them.” Chaipruak said their situation was different from that of 40 Uyghurs sent back to China last year, a move that sparked international condemnation. “This is a matter of justice, not related to policy, unlike the last 40 people,” he added, without elaborating. China’s public security ministry said last year that the 40 deported Chinese were “illegal migrants”. Asked Wednesday about the fate of the latest five, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning did not provide details. “China and Thailand’s cooperation in combating cross-border criminal activities such as illegal immigration is in line with the two countries’ laws, international law and international practice,” she said. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning during a press conference on March 11, 2025. Photo: China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Thailand is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention, but is bound by the international legal principle of non-refoulement, which bars countries from sending people back to places where their lives or freedom are in danger. Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch (HRW) said the two pardoned men should be allowed to travel to a safe third country. HRW warned Wednesday that in China they faced “grave risks of torture and other serious abuses”. Beijing has been accused of detaining more than a million Uyghurs and other Muslims since 2017, part of a campaign that the United Nations previously said could constitute crimes against humanity. China vehemently denies these allegations, saying its policies have boosted economic development and rooted out extremism in the Xinjiang region, where most Uyghurs are from.

title: Tai Po fire: Former top official urges gov’t to publish building inspection report to clear buyout doubts
zh_title: 大埔火警：前高官促政府公布验楼报告以释买断疑虑
summary: 一名香港前高级官员呼吁政府公布遭受火灾的宏福苑的结构检查报告，以打消那些拒绝政府公寓回购提议的房主的担忧。前运输及房屋局局长张建良。资料图片：香港政府一站通。香港前运输及房屋局局长张永明周三在《明报》发表的一篇评论文章中表示，利用专门立法从拒绝政府回购计划的业主手中买下公寓，将与私人财产权相抵触。
content:
一名香港前高级官员呼吁政府公布遭受火灾的宏福苑的结构检查报告，以打消那些拒绝政府公寓回购提议的房主的担忧。前运输及房屋局局长张建良。资料图片：香港政府一站通。香港前运输及房屋局局长张永明周三在《明报》发表的一篇评论文章中表示，利用专门立法从拒绝政府回购计划的业主手中买下公寓，将与私人财产权相抵触。截至10月中旬，宏福苑超过93%的房主已签署正式销售协议，将其公寓出售给政府，作为近一年前致命火灾后买​​断计划的一部分。政府表示，对于那些未签字的人，可以诉诸法律手段。 “《基本法》保护私人财产权，如果没有明确的‘公共利益’理由或合法的公共目的，政府不能征用私人资产，”张用中文写道。去年11月26日，大埔发生大火，吞没了正在进行大规模翻修工程的政府资助屋村的七栋建筑物。大火导致 168 人死亡，4,600 多名居民流离失所。
张说：“通过特别立法授权强制收购很容易引发人们对开创政府征用私人财产先例的担忧；必须极其谨慎地处理它，因为它可能面临无限期拖延的司法审查。”宏福法院，2026 年 8 月 20 日。照片：Kyle Lam。张说，迄今为止，房屋局尚未发布结构检查报告，“损坏的真实程度尚不清楚”。一些居民，包括一些拒绝政府买断的居民，对他们的房屋是否无法挽救表示怀疑。这位前部长表示：“少数持怀疑态度的业主仍与政府存在争议，其中一些人拒绝收购提议。” “结构检查报告应尽快公布，以消除公众疑虑。”张还对上周提交给政府的独立调查委员会的最终报告进行了评论，强调“邪恶的平庸”，强调“双重机构失败”，即政府未能发现不法行为，而私营部门看门人也未能履行职责。他形容官僚机构内部存在“平庸的邪恶”，检查肤浅，部门互相推诿。 2026 年 10 月 29 日，香港行政长官李家超和其他高级官员就 2025 年宏福苑致命火灾鞠躬致歉。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
他写道：“职业诚信崩溃，欺诈性玩忽职守，专业认证和第三方把关人沦为橡皮图章练习。”关于政府拟议的改革，张表示，组织文化需要“真正的转型”，“避免新瓶装旧酒”——这是立法者在李明博宣布改革方案后表达的担忧。在文中，张还谈到了前房屋部长何永琼的辞职以及围绕政治问责的讨论。何领导了住房局，该局负责监管声名狼藉的独立检查组。调查委员会报告还称，消防处

【原文 English Original】
A former top Hong Kong official has called on the government to release a structural inspection report of the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court to dispel the concerns of homeowners who have rejected the government’s apartment buyback offer. Former secretary for transport and housing Anthony Cheung. File Photo: GovHK. Hong Kong’s former secretary for transport and housing Anthony Cheung said in an op-ed published in Ming Pao on Wednesday that the use of specialised legislation to buy out flats from owners who have refused the government’s buyback scheme would be at odds with private property rights. As of mid-October, over 93 per cent of Wang Fuk Court homeowners have signed a formal sales agreement to sell their flats to the government as part of a buyout scheme following the deadly fire almost a year ago. The government has said it could resort to legal means for those who did not sign. “The Basic Law protects private property rights, and the government cannot expropriate private assets without a clear ‘public interest’ justification or a legitimate public purpose,” Cheung wrote in Chinese. The Tai Po fire broke out on November 26 last year, engulfing seven buildings in the government-subsidised estate during large-scale renovation works. The blaze killed 168 people and displaced over 4,600 residents. “Passing special legislation to authorise compulsory acquisition would easily stoke fears of setting a precedent for government expropriation of private property; it must be handled with extreme prudence, as it risks facing judicial reviews that could drag on indefinitely,” Cheung said. Wang Fuk Court on August 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam. To date, the Housing Bureau has yet to release the structural inspection report, “leaving the true extent of the damage unclear,” Cheung said. Some residents, including some who have rejected the government’s buyout, have expressed doubts that their homes are not salvageable. “A sceptical minority of owners remain locked in disputes with the government, with some rejecting the buyout proposal,” the former minister said. “The structural inspection report should be published as soon as possible to dispel public doubts.” ‘The banality of evil’ Cheung also commented on an independent probe committee’s final report that was submitted to the government last week, highlighting “dual institutional failures” where the government failed to detect wrongdoing and private sector gatekeepers failed to do their duty. He described a “banality of evil” within the bureaucracy, with superficial inspections and departments passing the buck. Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee and other top officials bow in apology on October 29, 2026 over the deadly 2025 Wang Fuk Court blaze. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “[There was] a collapse of professional integrity and fraudulent neglect of duty, where professional certification and third-party gatekeepers were reduced to mere rubber-stamp exercises,” he wrote. Regarding the government’s proposed reforms, Cheung said that “genuine transformation” was needed in organisational culture “to avoid putting old wine into new bottles” – a concern that lawmakers voiced after city leader Lee announced the reform package. In the article, Cheung also addressed former housing minister Winnie Ho’s resignation and the discussions around political accountability. Ho led the Housing Bureau, which oversaw the disgraced Independent Checking Unit. The probe committee report also said that the Fire Services Department, the Buildings Department, and the Labour Department, bore a share of the responsibility for the fire. “Naturally, the public questions why other bureau directors who also oversee implicated departments have remained in office. While the chief executive’s explanation that this was a ‘political decision’ may not entirely lay the public’s doubts to rest, such is life.”
